text:
Understanding Jefferson and this Page

The purpose of this post is to answer common questions I see in the many comments on this page and to spell out my overall mindset. At ThomasJefferson [.] com, the philosophy is built on five core principles. Primary source evidence (such as his letters) is valued over modern assumptions, the rule of innocent until proven guilty is strictly upheld, historical figures are not judged by modern standards, respectful and informed debate is welcomed while drive-by insults are blocked, and Thomas Jefferson is treated with basic human empathy for the massive personal sacrifices he made for this country.
 
Before diving deeper into those points, let me first set the scene. When it comes to Thomas Jefferson, there are three major types of people. First, there are his admirers. Second, there are his haters. Third, there are the people in the middle who love his accomplishments, just not the other parts of his life.
 
First of all, this page is for Thomas Jefferson admirers. This is not a blind love for him, but rather a well-researched admiration built on many years of study and reflection. Serious students of history dismiss uninformed attacks because arguments built on myths rather than primary sources are simply not worth debating. Conversely, if you happen to be an admirer who has not done all the research yet, maybe because you simply trusted the opinion of someone you respect, you still ended up on the right side of history. As the old saying goes, it is better to be lucky than good.
 
Because of this, haters have a short leash here. They are welcome if they come in genuinely wanting to understand. However, if they come into the comments repeating the same tired misinformation without any backup or proof, and refuse to consider and read the materials offered here, they will be blocked. Those old complaints are easily resolved by reading original source documents, which the critics rarely do. That is why they all sound the same, simply parroting talking points from an author or academic with an agenda, accepting everything blindly without any skepticism, critical thinking, or effort to verify if it is actually true. There are better things to do than to entertain amateur, surface-level attacks.
 
For example, recently a gentleman here was told that Jefferson actually wrote letters denying the Hemings charges, and he replied that he had been reading about Jefferson for over 40 years and had never heard that. Do not assume you know Thomas Jefferson just because you have read poor (usually modern liberal) biographies or have never dug deeper, settling instead for the historical equivalent of junk food. But more often than not, critics are simply everyday readers who were misled by biased academics pushing an agenda to fuel resentment toward Jefferson. If you have seen this irrational hostility firsthand in the academic world, you know exactly what I mean.
 
On the other hand, if you are a critic who takes the time to read the articles on this page and wants to question specific points or debate the issue respectfully, you are welcome to stay. The fact is, the more you learn the real history surrounding Jefferson, the more you realize he was a good and great man. Serious students of Jefferson and thus admirers determined this to be true a long time ago. There is a reason why some of America's greatest presidents, including Lincoln, FDR, and JFK, deeply admired Thomas Jefferson, and it is because they understood the facts.
 
Now we come to the people in the middle. They do not particularly love Jefferson, nor do they hate him. They usually understand that we should not judge historical figures by modern standards, yet they struggle to understand why a great man would own slaves, especially when he openly wrote that slavery was wrong.
 
For this concern, I suggest you start with this post: https://t.co/kz0DIDNBWX . I have received countless messages thanking me for this piece because it bridges that disconnect. It explains in logical detail, based on real historical facts and Virginia law, why Thomas Jefferson remained a slaveholder. Hint: it was not because he wanted to be.
 
Another common question from people in the middle is about the rumors of Jefferson having a relationship with an enslaved woman. They often ask what would be so wrong with that. Honestly, if a relationship were based on mutual love, there would be nothing wrong with it, and today it would even be celebrated. The issue here is simply about truth and evidence.
 
Jefferson himself denied the rumor, and many people close to him backed up his word. Why should anyone accept an accusation that he denied when there is no solid proof? A basic principle of fairness is innocent until proven guilty.
 
Even today, there is no conclusive proof from DNA to confirm those claims. In fact, DNA even exonerated Jefferson in a major historical rumor, a detail rarely publicized or shared by progressive academics. For over two centuries, many people suspected that a man named Thomas Woodson was Jefferson's son conceived during his time in France, largely because the timeline fit the boy's age perfectly and they shared a first name. The circumstantial evidence was extremely convincing. Yet the 1998 DNA study definitively proved that Jefferson was not his father. Jefferson was telling the truth all along.
 
Finally, people in the middle often say that Jefferson was just a man who did great things, but also had flaws. That is true of every human being who has ever lived. Saying it is like pointing out that the sun is bright. It is so obvious that it does not need to be said. Nobody feels the need to remind everyone that Thomas Edison was a flawed and hypocritical man, even though he was, just like anyone else. It is completely unnecessary, and it is just as ridiculous to constantly repeat it about Jefferson.
 
People do this because Jefferson is larger than life, and cynics always want to knock great figures down a peg to feel balanced. They say he was extraordinary, yet in the same breath insist he was complex, a paradox, or a hypocrite. No, Jefferson was a benevolent genius who gave and gave without asking for anything in return. People label him incorrectly simply because they do not understand him. How can you balance out an extraordinary individual by reducing them to ordinary? That goes against the very definition of extraordinary.
 
When people make flippant, careless remarks about Jefferson, it is wrong. Even though he passed away 200 years ago, people should still show basic human empathy. In his farewell letter to James Madison, Jefferson famously asked his friend to "take care of me when dead." That proves he cared deeply about how future generations would remember him. Given how much he sacrificed for this country, including his family fortune, his personal peace, and his own life, Jefferson deserves to be honored and respected by all Americans.
 
Thank you, Mr. Jefferson, for all you have done for us. Now it is our responsibility to continue your work and principles.

text:
Immigration uncertainty, visa delays, and shifting priorities are driving an increasing number of Indian professionals in the United States to return to India.

According to data from tech staffing firm TeamLease Digital, roughly 9,800 tech professionals returned to India in 2024, rising to 15,100 in 2025. By September 2026, another 12,900 had made the transition. Kamal Karanth, co-founder of staffing firm Xpheno, notes that the India-US talent corridor may see a net-positive year where India gains more tech talent from the US than it loses.

Contributing factors include stricter immigration scrutiny, delays in approvals for Optional Practical Training (OPT) and STEM OPT, and the emergence of Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India offering cross-border technical roles. However, returnees face financial trade-offs: domestic salary offers frequently range from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 30 lakh, compared to US compensation packages of $150,000 to $200,000 (roughly Rs 1.9 crore).

Source: The Times of India

Musk vs. Duffy: Tech Giant Claims FAA Rejected Free Starlink Before Massive US Flight Shutdown

Following a nationwide flight grounding in the United States due to a major FAA communications outage on November 13, 2026, a public exchange has erupted between tech billionaire Elon Musk and U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. Musk claimed on social media that he had previously offered free Starlink satellite internet terminals to the FAA to prevent such issues, but Duffy rejected the offer, stating they were not needed. In response, Secretary Duffy defended the decision, explaining that a ground-based network remains the best primary method for managing America's vast airspace, though he praised Starlink's speed and noted that the government is utilizing Musk's technology for specific parts of the airspace. Meanwhile, the massive system failure, which disrupted thousands of flights, has prompted Duffy to push Congress for a $50 billion budget to overhaul the nation's aging air traffic control infrastructure. https://t.co/R7hreUjT7W

$SPY MARKET UPDATE: TARGETS HIT. NOW WHAT? 🎯

Last week’s bearish roadmap played out perfectly.

I called for the $735 gap fill and a potential 200-day SMA retest around $729–726. Both targets were hit, with SPY making a fresh low near $727.

The bearish 10/100 and 20/100-day SMA crossovers, repeated resistance rejections and weakening momentum warned of another leg lower.

All downside targets achieved. My final put is closed, profits secured, and I’m entirely in cash. No more shorts for now.

So, what’s next?

1. Has SPY bottomed? Not necessarily.

Hitting downside targets doesn’t automatically end a correction.

SPY remains below its major short and intermediate term moving averages, with both the 10 and 20-day SMAs below the 100-day SMA.

Those bearish crosses helped confirm the decline. For a convincing reversal, I’d eventually want the opposite: both averages reclaiming the 100-day SMA.

I don’t need to wait for that to trade a bounce, but a tradable relief rally isn’t necessarily a confirmed bottom.

2. Preferred long entry zone: $721-715

Ideally, SPY retests its 50-week SMA around $720–721, with additional liquidity support near $715–716.

That $715–721 zone offers attractive potential risk/reward for calls, provided buyers defend it.

Could it mark the bottom before another rally towards ATHs? Absolutely. But I’d want confirmation rather than blindly calling a bottom in a falling market to sound cool.

3. What if SPY rallies immediately?

First resistance is $741, an area that has repeatedly rejected price.

Above that, $750–751 is the next major test.

A rejection around $751 could offer another short opportunity, especially below declining moving averages.

Conversely, reclaiming $751 and the 5 and 10-day SMAs would be an encouraging first step.

A sustained reclaim of the 100-day SMA, with a bullish 10/100 and 20/100 crossovers, would strengthen the case for a genuine reversal and potentially new ATHs.

One reclaim doesn’t confirm a bottom. Improving price structure, momentum and moving averages together carry more weight.

4. Nvidia earnings is why I’m cautious

Nvidia delivered another widely anticipated earnings beat. My bigger concern was guidance and confidence surrounding the leadership transition.

The board ruled out Jensen Huang’s immediate return, but longer-term leadership uncertainty remains.

I listened to the earnings call and didn’t find the reassurance particularly convincing.

Nvidia initially jumped several percentage points, pulling the broader market higher, but those gains have already started fading.

I flagged the rally to subscribers as suspicious. Strong results don’t guarantee sustained upside when expectations are elevated and the broader technical structure remains weak.

Let’s see whether buyers defend the gains during regular trading.

5. Anthropic IPO is potential liquidity catalyst

Thursday’s anticipated Anthropic IPO introduces another variable.

Could investors raise cash ahead of the offering, pressuring other tech stocks? Possibly.

Could it instead lift AI sector sentiment? Also possible.

I won’t assume either outcome. Price action will determine my next move.

6. Why I’m staying in cash

With VIX recently above 25, calls face potential implied-volatility contraction. SPY could bounce while falling IV still pressures options premiums.

That’s partly why I didn’t immediately switch from puts to calls after hitting my targets.

I’d rather wait for a cleaner entry: a confirmed reaction around $720–715 or improving bullish structure higher up.

BOTTOM LINE

My bearish targets are complete, puts closed and profits secured. Now I’m preparing for the next opportunity.

I’m not automatically bullish because the market fell, nor permanently bearish after successfully trading the decline.

Upside resistance: $741–742, then $750–751.

Preferred deeper dip buying zone: $720–715.

A convincing reversal could offer calls. Another rejection could offer puts. I’ll adapt.

text:
This account of Texas colonization leaves out much of the history documented by Jesús F. "Frank" de la Teja and other historians who have studied Spanish Texas, Mexican Texas, Tejano communities, and Indigenous peoples.

If you're a Texan unfamiliar with de la Teja and his work, he's someone worth learning about.

https://t.co/jzxsh6J8IF

There are legitimate historical facts in these posts, but they're assembled into a narrative where Anglo settlers are the principal actors, Mexican authorities manipulate them, Indigenous peoples are primarily a military threat, and Tejanos have almost no agency.

Let's examine the documented history.

The original Austin settlement

In December 1820, Moses Austin traveled to San Antonio and requested permission from Spanish authorities to bring 300 families into Texas. Approval came in January 1821, before Mexico became independent.

Erasmo Seguín, a prominent Tejano leader, supported the original proposal and was involved in the process. He later represented Texas in Mexico's constitutional congress. Tejanos were not simply spectators in the decisions shaping their communities.

Spanish authorities initially preferred settlement closer to San Antonio, but the Austins favored the lower Colorado River region. Stephen F. Austin subsequently received authorization to explore and select a suitable location, ultimately establishing his colony in the Brazos and Colorado river region.

Following Mexican independence in September 1821, Austin had to obtain authorization from the new government. Mexico did not automatically recognize the original Spanish arrangement.

The claim that Anglo settlers were expendable human shields

Frontier defense was a documented consideration. Spanish authorities expected settlers to help defend the territory, and later Mexican and Tejano officials also saw strategic benefits in immigration.

But that does not establish a deliberate scheme to deceive unsuspecting Anglo families into becoming expendable human shields against the Comanche.

The original colony was initiated through Moses Austin's request, approved under Spanish authority, and located through a process in which Stephen Austin actively participated.

This does not rule out later defensive-buffer policies elsewhere in Texas. Those claims deserve separate examination using evidence from the relevant period.

The population figures

The posts cite approximately 30,000 Anglo-Americans and 3,470 Mexicans in 1836.

Those figures closely resemble estimates reported by Henry M. Morfit in 1836, which also included approximately 14,200 Indigenous people and 5,000 enslaved Black people.

Excluded populations when describing who inhabited Texas.

Nor were Tejano communities confined almost entirely to the far south. San Antonio de Béxar, Goliad, and Nacogdoches were longstanding settlements before Anglo immigration accelerated.

Texas was not predominantly Anglo-American throughout nearly its entire period under Mexican sovereignty. When Mexico became independent in 1821, large-scale Anglo colonization was only beginning. The demographic transformation occurred over the following fifteen years.

Immigration, law, and slavery

The colonists were not simply unsuspecting recipients of generous land offers.

They actively sought settlement opportunities and were subject to the laws and conditions imposed by the governing authorities.

The 1825 Coahuila y Texas colonization law offered qualifying families substantial land grants, often including a league of grazing land and a labor of agricultural land. It also required settlers to accept constitutional and religious obligations.

Slavery is another major omission from the narrative.

Many Anglo settlers brought enslaved people, and the conflict over slavery became an important part of the political relationship between settlers and Mexican authorities.

This was not simply a story of farming families confronting Comanche raids.

The missing Tejano and Indigenous perspectives

Tejano leaders had their own political interests, economic ambitions, and reasons for supporting immigration. Those interests were not necessarily identical to those of officials in Mexico City, and Tejano opinion was not uniform.

Indigenous nations also had their own societies, territories, economies, diplomatic relationships, and political objectives.

Comanche power was a genuine factor shaping settlement, warfare, and government policy. But describing Indigenous peoples almost exclusively as a military obstacle overlooks much of that history.

The differences between Spanish, Mexican, and Anglo settlement patterns cannot be adequately explained through national stereotypes about courage, independence, or willingness to confront danger.

The historical record matters

We have contemporary correspondence, government authorizations, colonization laws, and extensive historical scholarship documenting these events.

The original Austin colony was not simply a Mexican government operation placing unsuspecting Anglo-Americans in Comanche territory.

Moses Austin requested permission from Spain. Spanish officials approved the proposal. Stephen F. Austin participated in choosing the colony's location. Mexican authorities subsequently authorized its continuation.

Tejanos participated in decisions affecting their province, while Indigenous nations continued exercising power across substantial portions of Texas.

This history is more complicated than the narrative presented in these posts.

A factual account can acknowledge Anglo settlers' hardships, Comanche military power, Mexican and Spanish strategic interests, and the contributions of Texians without erasing Tejano agency or Indigenous history.

Sources and further reading

Jesús F. de la Teja and other historians have contributed substantially to the study of Spanish and Mexican Texas.

Texas State Historical Association, Anglo-American Colonization:
https://t.co/jUAPEIOk8n
Mexican Texas, revised by Jesús F. de la Teja:
https://t.co/H63gaZpAEN

Republic of Texas, including historical population estimates:
https://t.co/d4mm4zODwx
Stephen F. Austin's January 20, 1824 correspondence:
https://t.co/TEdXKTEYAR

Spanish-era colonization correspondence and regulations:
https://t.co/BrDa9a7hSN

They hoped that the Anglos coming in would be a “human shield” and keep the Comanche busy so they didn’t come far enough south to attack the Mexican villages

Most of the Anglo settlers did not know about the Comanche and thought the Mexicans were just offering them a generous land deal

So they came in, accepted the land (often thousands of acres per family), set up farms, got destroyed by the Comanche, kept coming because they didn’t know better, and the raids kept getting worse as they unknowingly encroached farther into Comanche territory

Eventually the Anglo portion of Mexico (Texas) seceded and became an independent nation and they *still* had brutal Comanche problems, all the way past the Civil War and into the 1870s

The coasts were connected by the Transcontinental Railroad and buffalo hunters were killing all the buffalo on the high plains and Texans still couldn’t get to the middle of their state because the Comanche had such a brutal hold

My husband remembers his great-grandmother still sounding afraid talking about the Comanche in the 1990s because the family stories were so bad

Meanwhile Americans would gather a few families of kinfolk and just yolo into the middle of Comanche territory to set up lone farmsteads. A tough, self-reliant and headstrong people. That’s who settled Texas. “Immigrants” my ass.

text:
🏛️ 100 FACTS ABOUT THE ILIAD AND THE ODYSSEY

📜 HOMER AND THE POEMS
𝟏. The Iliad and the Odyssey are among the oldest surviving works of Western literature, traditionally credited to the poet Homer

𝟐. Most scholars date them to the late 8th or early 7th century BC, with the Iliad usually thought to be the older of the two

𝟑. Almost nothing is known about Homer himself, and ancient tradition said he was blind

𝟒. Several ancient cities, including Smyrna and Chios, claimed to be his birthplace

𝟓. Greeks often called him simply "the Poet", so famous that no name was needed

𝟔. Whether one poet composed both epics, or many, is the famous "Homeric Question", debated since antiquity

𝟕. Some ancient scholars, nicknamed the "Chorizontes" ("separators"), argued that the two poems had different authors

𝟖. Both are written in dactylic hexameter, a six-beat line used for Greek epic

𝟗. Their language is an artificial poetic mix of Greek dialects, mostly Ionic with older Aeolic forms

𝟏𝟎. In the 1930s Milman Parry and Albert Lord studied oral singers in Yugoslavia to show how the poems grew out of an oral tradition

𝟏𝟏. Stock phrases like "swift-footed Achilles", "rosy-fingered Dawn" and the "wine-dark sea" helped singers compose as they performed

𝟏𝟐. Professional reciters called rhapsodes performed Homer at festivals such as the Panathenaia in Athens

𝟏𝟑. A later tradition says the Athenian ruler Peisistratos had the poems collected and written down in the 6th century BC

𝟏𝟒. The division of each epic into 24 books is usually credited to scholars in Hellenistic Alexandria

𝟏𝟓. The Iliad runs to about 15,700 lines and the Odyssey to about 12,100

𝟏𝟔. Both open by calling on the Muse: "Sing, goddess, the rage of Achilles" and "Tell me, Muse, of the man of many ways"

⚔️ THE ILIAD
𝟏𝟕. "Iliad" means "the poem about Ilion", another name for Troy

𝟏𝟖. It covers only a few weeks, roughly 50 days, in the tenth and final year of the Trojan War

𝟏𝟗. Its very first word is "mēnin", "rage": the wrath of Achilles is the poem's theme

𝟐𝟎. The story begins with a quarrel between Achilles and Agamemnon over the captive woman Briseis

𝟐𝟏. Agamemnon takes Briseis after being forced to give up Chryseis, daughter of a priest of Apollo, when Apollo sends a plague on the Greek camp

𝟐𝟐. Achilles withdraws from battle, and his mother, the sea nymph Thetis, asks Zeus to let the Trojans win until the Greeks honour her son

𝟐𝟑. Book 2 contains the "Catalogue of Ships", listing 29 Greek contingents and about 1,186 ships

𝟐𝟒. The Wooden Horse never appears in the Iliad: the poem ends before Troy falls, and the horse is told of in the Odyssey

𝟐𝟓. Achilles' death is also not shown, although it is foretold several times

𝟐𝟔. In Book 3, Paris and Menelaus fight a duel to settle the war, but Aphrodite snatches Paris away

𝟐𝟕. From the walls of Troy, Helen points out the Greek heroes to King Priam, a scene known as the "Teichoskopia"

𝟐𝟖. In Book 5, the Greek hero Diomedes, helped by Athena, wounds the gods Aphrodite and Ares

𝟐𝟗. Hector's farewell to his wife Andromache in Book 6 includes their baby son crying in fear at his father's plumed helmet

𝟑𝟎. In Book 9, Odysseus, Ajax and Phoenix offer Achilles rich gifts to return, and he refuses

𝟑𝟏. Book 10, a night raid known as the "Doloneia", is thought by many scholars to be a later addition

𝟑𝟐. In Book 14, Hera seduces Zeus to lull him to sleep so Poseidon can help the Greeks

𝟑𝟑. Patroclus goes into battle wearing Achilles' armour and is killed by Hector, with help from Apollo

𝟑𝟒. The god Hephaestus forges Achilles new armour, and the description of his shield runs to some 130 lines

𝟑𝟓. The Shield of Achilles shows a whole world: cities at peace and at war, ploughing, harvest, a wedding and a dance

𝟑𝟔. Achilles even fights the river god Scamander, who tries to drown him

𝟑𝟕. Achilles chases Hector three times around the walls of Troy before killing him in Book 22

𝟑𝟖. Before that duel, Zeus weighs the fates of the two heroes on golden scales, and Hector's sinks

𝟑𝟗. Achilles drags Hector's body behind his chariot, but the gods keep it from decay

𝟒𝟎. Book 23 describes funeral games for Patroclus, with a chariot race, boxing, wrestling and a footrace

𝟒𝟏. In Book 24, the old King Priam secretly enters Achilles' tent and kisses the hands that killed his son to ransom his body

𝟒𝟐. The poem ends quietly with Hector's funeral: "Such were the funeral rites of Hector, tamer of horses"

𝟒𝟑. Achilles knew he could choose a long, obscure life or a short life with everlasting glory

𝟒𝟒. The gods take sides: Hera, Athena and Poseidon back the Greeks, while Apollo, Aphrodite and Ares favour Troy

𝟒𝟓. Homer never calls the Greeks "Greeks": they are Achaeans, Danaans or Argives

𝟒𝟔. More than 200 warriors are killed in the poem, many with grimly precise descriptions of their wounds

🌊 THE ODYSSEY
𝟒𝟕. The Odyssey follows Odysseus' 10-year journey home after the 10-year war, so he is away from Ithaca for 20 years

𝟒𝟖. Yet the main action of the poem takes only about 40 days

𝟒𝟗. The first four books, the "Telemachy", follow his son Telemachus as he seeks news of his father in Pylos and Sparta

𝟓𝟎. The goddess Athena guides Telemachus disguised as an old friend called Mentor, which gave English the word "mentor"

𝟓𝟏. We first meet Odysseus on the island of the nymph Calypso, who has kept him there for seven years

𝟓𝟐. Zeus sends Hermes to order Calypso to let him go, and Odysseus sails away on a raft he builds himself

𝟓𝟑. Shipwrecked by Poseidon, he reaches the land of the Phaeacians and meets the princess Nausicaa

𝟓𝟒. Most of his famous adventures, in Books 9 to 12, are told by Odysseus himself in flashback at the Phaeacian court

𝟓𝟓. Men who ate the fruit of the Lotus-Eaters forgot all wish to return home

𝟓𝟔. The one-eyed Cyclops Polyphemus, a son of Poseidon, traps Odysseus' men in his cave and eats several of them

𝟓𝟕. Odysseus tells him his name is "Nobody", so when he is blinded, the Cyclops cries that "Nobody" is hurting him

𝟓𝟖. The Greeks escape by clinging to the bellies of the giant's sheep

𝟓𝟗. Odysseus then shouts his real name, letting Polyphemus call down his father Poseidon's curse on him

𝟔𝟎. The wind god Aeolus gives him a bag holding the storm winds, but his crew opens it in sight of Ithaca

𝟔𝟏. The giant cannibal Laestrygonians destroy every ship in his fleet except his own

𝟔𝟐. The witch Circe turns his men into pigs, and Hermes gives Odysseus a magic herb called moly to resist her

𝟔𝟑. He ends up staying with Circe for a whole year

𝟔𝟒. In Book 11 he visits the land of the dead to consult the prophet Tiresias and meets his own mother's ghost

𝟔𝟓. There Achilles' ghost says he would rather be a poor labourer on earth than king of all the dead

𝟔𝟔. Passing the Sirens, his crew plug their ears with beeswax while Odysseus has himself tied to the mast to hear their song

𝟔𝟕. He must sail between the six-headed monster Scylla and the whirlpool Charybdis

𝟔𝟖. When his men eat the sacred cattle of the sun god Helios, Zeus destroys their ship and Odysseus is the only survivor

𝟔𝟗. The Phaeacians finally carry him home to Ithaca while he sleeps

𝟕𝟎. Athena disguises him as an old beggar so he can enter his own palace unrecognised

𝟕𝟏. His old dog Argos recognises him after 20 years, wags his tail, and dies

𝟕𝟐. His old nurse Eurycleia recognises him by a scar from a boar hunt while washing his feet

𝟕𝟑. Penelope fended off 108 suitors, partly by weaving a shroud by day and secretly unpicking it at night

𝟕𝟒. She sets a contest: string Odysseus' great bow and shoot an arrow through 12 axe heads

𝟕𝟓. Only the beggar can do it, and Odysseus, Telemachus and two loyal servants then kill the suitors

𝟕𝟔. Penelope tests him with a secret only he knows: their bed was built around the trunk of a living olive tree

𝟕𝟕. The poem ends with Athena making peace between Odysseus and the suitors' families

🏺 TROY, MYTH AND HISTORY
𝟕𝟖. Troy is identified with the mound of Hisarlik, near the Dardanelles in northwest Anatolia

𝟕𝟗. Frank Calvert dug there first, and Heinrich Schliemann began his famous excavations in 1871

𝟖𝟎. Schliemann's "Treasure of Priam" turned out to be roughly a thousand years older than any possible Trojan War

𝟖𝟏. At Mycenae in 1876 he found the gold "Mask of Agamemnon", now dated to about 1550-1500 BC, centuries before Agamemnon's era

𝟖𝟐. His famous line "I have gazed upon the face of Agamemnon" is probably a later invention

𝟖𝟑. Troy has at least nine main layers, and Troy VI or VIIa are usually seen as the best candidates for Homer's city

𝟖𝟒. Hittite texts mention a land called "Wilusa" and a people called "Ahhiyawa", which many link to Ilios and the Achaeans

𝟖𝟓. Homer describes a helmet covered in boar's tusks, a real Bronze Age type later found by archaeologists

𝟖𝟔. The ancient scholar Eratosthenes dated the fall of Troy to 1184/1183 BC

𝟖𝟕. Troy was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1998

𝟖𝟖. Where Homer's Ithaca really was is still debated, and some have argued for part of Kefalonia instead

🌍 LEGACY
𝟖𝟗. Alexander the Great reportedly kept a copy of the Iliad under his pillow, next to a dagger

𝟗𝟎. Plato reports that Homer was praised as the poet who "educated Greece"

𝟗𝟏. Livius Andronicus' Latin version of the Odyssey, from the 3rd century BC, is one of the first works of Latin literature

𝟗𝟐. Virgil's Aeneid models its first half on the Odyssey and its second half on the Iliad

𝟗𝟑. Homer was little read in medieval Western Europe, and Petrarch owned a Greek manuscript he could not read

𝟗𝟒. The first printed edition of Homer appeared in Florence in 1488

𝟗𝟓. Alexander Pope's English translation of the Iliad and the Odyssey made him one of the first English poets to grow rich from his work

𝟗𝟔. James Joyce's novel "Ulysses" (1922) maps a single day in Dublin onto the Odyssey

𝟗𝟕. Emily Wilson's 2017 Odyssey is widely described as the first English translation of the poem published by a woman

𝟗𝟖. Homer is by far the most common author among the ancient Greek literary papyri found in Egypt

𝟗𝟗. Words like "odyssey" and "mentor" come from the poems, but the story of Achilles' heel is not in Homer at all: it comes from later writers

𝟏𝟎𝟎. From "Troy" (2004) to Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" (2026), the poems keep returning to the big screen nearly 3,000 years on

📸 The gold "Mask of Agamemnon" from Mycenae, National Archaeological Museum, Athens. Photo: Gary Todd, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

     Californians Pay 68% More At The Pump Than Texans - And Blue States Got Smaller Post-Election Drops | ZeroHedge https://t.co/Fq9q6kGm3s
⛽️👁⛽️ This is one of those cases when data matter more than words. These charts rely on information from AAA. The first chart shows prices in all fifty states, along with the party that controlled the legislature for most of the last decade before the 2026 election. (That election will change the future for some states, notably Texas, but I was interested in the past.)Of the 25 states with the highest gasoline prices, 15 (or 60%) are Democrat-controlled, based on predominant legislative control from 2016-2025. The five states with the very highest gas prices - Hawaii, California, Nevada, Washington, and Oregon - all have predominantly Democrat-controlled legislatures.
It's clear that, for some states, geography and other factors that I haven't researched play a role. Not only is Hawaii an ardently Democrat state, but it's also an island. Everything must be shipped there, raising prices. Inland geography may also be a factor in Utah, Idaho, and Arizona being on that list. As Olivia Murray will be happy to tell you, Arizona is also notoriously corrupt, despite its ostensibly Republican control over the years.Nevertheless, the trend is clear: If you live in a blue state, you're much more likely to pay more for gas. It cannot have escaped your notice that, just as 15 of the top 25 most costly states have been run by Democrats, the opposite is true - more than true - for the most affordable states. Another major refinery has since stopped producing gasoline. Meanwhile, daily crude oil production has plummeted 77%, from 1.08 million barrels in 1985 to just 245,000 in August 2026. text:
Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic rivals, documents show, as China aims to broaden its AI strategy and offset tightening US curbs on its access to chips.

A Reuters review of more than 300 Chinese academic papers, patents, corporate disclosures, recruitment notices, and government documents reveals how the practice—known as distillation—has expanded beyond academic experiments into mainstream industrial use in China.

The records describe Chinese researchers using US models to generate answers, write code, and solve difficult problems, while Chinese firms build software to automate the process and deploy specialist workers to prepare material for smaller domestic models—an effort Beijing encourages to make AI cheaper across its manufacturing sector.

While distillation is legal, globally common, and cannot replicate a flagship model's full capabilities or replace advanced computing power, it preserves key skills in lower-cost systems, potentially blunting US curbs on companies like Nvidia ahead of the November 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies in September of industrial-scale distillation attacks, and Commerce Department officials warned Chinese regulators during July meetings in Chengdu that collecting output from top American models could constitute intellectual-property theft.

Chinese officials defended distillation as a standard development technique and offered no concrete commitments despite claiming openness to acting against IP theft, prompting Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to warn on X on July 23 that covert, industrial-scale distillation crossing into IP theft could trigger sanctions and Entity List designations.

FROM AMERICAN ANSWERS TO CHINESE MODELS

Distillation uses a powerful "teacher" model to generate answers or task demonstrations that train a smaller "student" system, allowing compute-constrained Chinese developers to make a single expensive query do repeated work, according to a former Alibaba Group engineer.

In a November 2024 paper, Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers selected roughly 5,000 answers from OpenAI's o1 model and translated them via GPT-4o mini into 10,750 bilingual examples to train Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B model, though they cautioned that over-reliance on distillation could stifle original innovation.

Alibaba researchers later described a systematic approach in an April 2025 paper using OpenAI's GPT-4 and GPT-4o to generate non-Chinese training material for smaller Qwen models, while a February 2026 paper by Shanghai Jiao Tong University and food-delivery giant Meituan detailed using GPT-4o to generate agent-coordination plans for programming tasks.

Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Alibaba, Meituan, China's Cyberspace Administration, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to requests for comment.

A GROWING GEOPOLITICAL DISPUTE

While OpenAI and Anthropic restrict using their outputs to train competing models without permission, a US official familiar with the July Chengdu talks said Washington views industrial-scale distillation as the primary reason Chinese AI models have narrowed the gap with American rivals—an assessment two people familiar with Chinese developers disputed, pointing also to gains in engineering, algorithms, data, and model design.

Rather than directly ordering firms to distill American models, Chinese government policies—including a January AI+Manufacturing package from eight agencies alongside initiatives in Shanghai and Shenzhen—encourage distillation to deploy smaller, cheaper AI across China's economy.

Concerned by rising geopolitical sensitivities, Chinese AI developers have in recent months asked Beijing's industry regulator to clarify the boundary between ordinary use of foreign models and organized output collection for training, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

text:
Some of what you mentioned was already covered in my original post.

"Raheem Morris is kicking ass" in San Francisco. 
So did Steve Wilks. 
So did Robert Saleh.
How have they faired as head coaches? 

Here's what you're missing. While Morris and Nagy may have been interested in the HC job, the Cardinals ultimately were not interested in them.

Nagy interviewed with 5 teams. All 5 passed on him. The Chiefs didn't even want him back. As for Arizona, Nagy didn't even make it to the 2nd round of interviews.

Morris was a finalist in Arizona but the Cardinals decided to go with an offensive minded coach.
He was offered the DC job, which he rejected.

While it's a bit of an exaggeration to say, "no veteran coach would take the job", the comment is rooted in the fact there have been several coaches and front office personnel who have rejected opportunities to join the Cardinals.

HC:
Mike Munchak and Jeff Hafley declined a 2nd, in-person, interview.
Saleh skipped his interview all together.
Sean McDermott said he had no interest in the job.
DeMeco Ryans skipped his interview while he was locking in with Houston.
Dan Quinn interviewed several times but opted to stay in Dallas.
Sean Payton came snd went.
Mike McCarthy just said no.

DC:
Gus Bradley, Raheem Morris, Charlie Bullen, Dino Vasso, and Anthony Weaver all declined offers/consideration for the Cardinals DC job.

GM
Ian Cunningham was offered the GM job in 2023. He turned down the Cardinals offer and stayed in a lesser role in Chicago.
Adam Peters and Ran Carthon declined requests to even be interviewed.

No, the fans aren't wrong in their assertion that veteran coaches are hard to attract, especially right now.

Subpar roster; especially on the defensive side.
Difficult and intrusive owner who keeps getting sued by former employees.
Cardinals recent track record of dysfunction, on and off the field.

I know fans like a scapegoat, but  damn this is weak.

Look, I know as Cardinals fans, this season has fallen short of anything different than what we've seen over the past 4 years.

But to suggest that either Raheem Morris or Matt Nagy would have done better is just... ludicrous.

Morris failed in both Tampa and Atlanta. A career record of 37-56, .398. Until this season (in San Francisco), his defenses have never ranked top-10. Steve Wilks' resume as a DC was actually better, and he was a disaster.

Nagy was a terrible play caller in Chicago. He's offense never ranked higher than 21st. He went 8-8 his 2nd season as a HC while having a top-5 defense. His time as OC was in Kansas City where he hasn't even been the primary play caller. KC initially wanted him back until the 2025 season played out. They literally let him walk after his contract expired.

With a career back-up as your QB1, Rallis (forced) as your DC, and the roster put together by Ossenfort, I doubt any other candidate would have had a successful season here.

Until Bidwill makes changes in the front office, by naming a President and changing GM's, I doubt we'll see any improvement. That's just the reality of the situation.

No credible evidence supports that claim. The story circulating online alleges Japan uncovered an Israeli plan to detonate dirty bombs in two US cities before Christmas and blame Iran. Fact-checking traced it to The People’s Voice, which supplied no verifiable evidence. Posts also used a fabricated CNN headline. Snopes rated the claim false. 

Japan’s actual 16 November travel advisory warns generally about terrorism around Christmas and New Year in Western countries. It does not identify an Israeli plot or mention dirty bombs. 

The People’s Voice is a website formerly called NewsPunch and, before that, YourNewsWire. It presents itself as an alternative news outlet.

It has a documented history of publishing false stories that independent fact-checkers have repeatedly debunked. In this case, its article offered no named Japanese intelligence officials, official warning, or verifiable evidence for the alleged Israeli plot. 

My earlier wording meant the claim was traced to that website—not that it was a credible news report.

The People’s Voice is based in Los Angeles, California, USA. It was founded in 2014 by Sean Adl-Tabatabai and Sinclair Treadway, originally under the name YourNewsWire.

Breaking News
California warns of 'imminent hazard to public safety' as it bars driverless cars from freeways

Officials in California have labeled Waymos and other self-driving cars an 'imminent hazard to public safety' as they banned the vehicles from state freeways following recent traffic incidents.

The Golden State's Department of Motor Vehicles ordered Waymo's driverless vehicles to stop operating and testing on all the state's freeways on November 11, citing an 'imminent hazard to public safety.'

It cited an incident in which three Waymo vehicles entered a construction closure on Highway 101 and a separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Interstate 280 in San Francisco. 

The construction zone incident occurred on November 5 and the second incident, which involved California Highway Patrol vehicles, occurred the next day on a highway in San Francisco, Jonathan Groveman, a department spokesperson, said in a statement.

Video of the November 6 incident circulated widely on social media last week. In the footage, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to bypass California Highway Patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break.

'The Department determined that Waymo´s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,' Groveman said.

Groveman added that 'similar incidents' previously occurred on May 18.

Waymo had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. 

The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.

But when the state banned the vehicles from its freeways, Waymo said it decided to withdraw its vehicles from highways across the country the same day.

'In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance,' spokesman Chris Pappas told The New York Times. 

The suspension was implemented last Wednesday, Pappas said, but he didn't say how long it would last.

Pappas also noted that the 'recent freeway construction zone encounters on US 101 in California' did not 'involve any injuries or collisions.'

California's restrictions bar Waymo from operating and testing its driverless vehicles on California freeways, according to Groveman.

text:
Me: American Kingpin: The Epic Hunt for the Criminal Mastermind Behind the Silk Road

Ai: American Kingpin is a gripping true-crime account of Ross Ulbricht, the young entrepreneur and computer programmer who created Silk Road, an underground online marketplace that became one of the largest illegal drug-trading platforms in the world.
The book follows Ulbricht's transformation from an idealistic young man fascinated by technology, libertarian philosophy and personal freedom into the mysterious figure known online as the Dread Pirate Roberts. Operating behind layers of encryption and anonymity on the dark web, he built a digital marketplace where people could buy and sell drugs, fake documents and other illegal goods using Bitcoin.
Nick Bilton takes readers inside the hidden world of the dark web, exploring how Silk Road operated, how Bitcoin helped facilitate anonymous transactions, and how Ulbricht attempted to build an empire beyond the reach of traditional law enforcement.
The narrative also follows the international investigation involving the FBI, DEA and other law enforcement agencies as they worked to identify the mastermind behind the marketplace. Through digital surveillance, undercover operations and painstaking detective work, investigators gradually closed in on Ulbricht, leading to his dramatic arrest in a San Francisco public library in 2013.
A major theme of the book is the dangerous intersection of ambition, technology, money, anonymity and power. It examines how someone with extraordinary technical skills and entrepreneurial instincts can use innovation to build something remarkable while allowing ideology, greed and unchecked authority to lead him into criminal territory.
Beyond the crime story, the book offers an inside look at the early evolution of Bitcoin, the dark web, online marketplaces and the challenges governments face when investigating crimes in an increasingly digital world.

Key themes and lessons
Entrepreneurship and ambition: How a seemingly ordinary idea can grow into an enormous enterprise.
Technology and innovation: How encryption, Bitcoin and the internet can transform commerce.
Power and corruption: How influence and success can gradually distort someone's judgment.
Risk and consequences: Why believing you are untouchable can lead to catastrophic decisions.
Law and freedom: The tension between individual liberty, government authority and social responsibility.

Who should read this book?
This book is particularly interesting for readers fascinated by entrepreneurship, technology, cryptocurrency, cybersecurity, investigative journalism, criminal psychology and the hidden economy of the internet.

Overall: American Kingpin reads almost like a Hollywood crime thriller, but its events are real. It is a fascinating account of how a young man's technological ambition turned into a billion-dollar criminal empire and one of the most extraordinary digital manhunts in modern history.

My take: A compelling read for anyone interested in how the internet creates entirely new opportunities for wealth, influence and power—and how those same opportunities can become dangerous when there are no meaningful boundaries.

1 AM Top-of-the-Hour News

The associated press has called the Alaska Senate race in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola over two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.: “Thank you, Alaska. We did it. From ADA to Metlakatla to Ukavik, you have made your voices heard, and it's clear that the status quo in DC cannot go on any longer. ”
It was the last Senate race that was left to be decided.
The victory gives Democrats their ninth Senate flip in the midterms. It's the most for the party since 1958.

Democrat Chuck Schumer says he will head the Senate when the new term begins in January.: “I'm confident I'll be the next leader, I have the votes, and we're all going to roll up our sleeves and we're going to focus on lowering costs, ending corruption. ”
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen says he is also running to be majority leader - saying the sweeping victory by Democrats in the midterm elections was a mandate from voters for change.

President Trump is in Manila holding bilateral talks with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
The president said that the United States is expanding its defense cooperation with Manila, and will probably do "something big" on nuclear power.: “With this visit, we're building on these ties to make our partnership even closer, although I don't imagine it can get much closer because of the relationship that we've had for a long time. ”
Philippine president Marcos:: “We are also exploring new areas of cooperation, particularly in technology, where American leadership and innovation continues to lead the way. We also see tremendous opportunities to work more closely through American leadership and super intelligence. ”
The president is next headed to China for an historical three way meeting with Xi Xinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.

The National Security Agency's highly classified communications system went down on Tuesday.
The outage impacted the N-S-A Net, which is responsible for sending and receiving top secret information.
NewsNation's Hannah Brandt reports: “A spokesperson says this was temporary. It happened during scheduled routine maintenance, they say, and they say, quote, mission critical capabilities remain fully operational. But this incident only adds to the growing list of technical disruptions that US companies and different systems that we've seen, adding to the concern over it as well. ”
Reports say it does not appear to be a cyber attack.
Apple also reported full outages with its Apple Music, App Store and AppleCare services, with issues on its iCloud interface. The company blamed an internal update for the problems.
Marriot International reported their own technology problems on Tuesday.

text:
Prosecutors Say C-130 Worth About $60 Million Was Damaged at Shannon Airport

A grand jury in New York indicted Daithi O’Corrain, 48, in connection with damage to a US military C-130 at Shannon Airport in Ireland. The aircraft, a C-130 Hercules, is estimated to be worth approximately $60 million, giving the alleged damage a substantial stated value even though the facts do not specify a repair bill. Prosecutors accuse O’Corrain of damaging the plane, and the indictment concerns destruction of government property; the accusation is not a finding of guilt. If convicted of that offense, he could receive a prison sentence of up to 10 years. The stated value describes the aircraft, while the possible prison term describes the consequence attached to a conviction, so the two figures measure different things.

The prosecution account begins with an alleged breach of the airport’s security boundary on 11 April. Prosecutors say O’Corrain then entered the parked C-130 and shut himself inside by barricading it. The aircraft was not described as flying at the time; it was parked at Shannon when the alleged actions took place. According to prosecutors, he cut wiring and hydraulic lines, broke the cockpit’s gauges, and struck the aircraft’s outer surface with an axe. They also allege that he put ball bearings into the plane’s fuel tanks, adding a separate form of interference to the damage described inside and outside the aircraft.

The indictment also describes how the plane’s windows were covered: O’Corrain allegedly used hammocks belonging to the crew for that purpose. The cockpit windshield, however, was left uncovered, according to the indictment. This detail records the alleged arrangement inside the aircraft, rather than adding a separate estimate of damage or a further charge. The other alleged actions cover several parts of the C-130: its cockpit instruments, wiring, hydraulic lines, exterior and fuel tanks. The account therefore identifies multiple kinds of alleged damage, but it supplies no itemized monetary total for them.

The plane belonged to the US Air National Guard, and it was traveling toward a military assignment in another country. The aircraft was rendered inoperable, according to the account of its intended journey and the incident. That means the reported consequence was not limited to damage to a parked aircraft: the C-130 could no longer continue to its military task. The available facts do not identify the country, the assignment’s purpose, or how long the aircraft remained out of service. They also do not provide a count of personnel or other aircraft affected, so the stated operational impact is specific to this C-130 and its planned journey.

The case has legal tracks in both the United States and Ireland, according to the reported charges and arrest. An Garda Síochána arrested O’Corrain immediately after the attack, and Irish authorities charged him with criminal damage and trespassing. Separately, a grand jury in New York indicted him over the alleged damage to US government property. The possible 10-year prison term belongs to the US destruction-of-government-property charge and applies only if there is a conviction. The facts identify the Irish charges but do not give a possible sentence for them, so that penalty should not be confused with the stated US maximum.

Manhattan US attorney Jamie McDonald said the indictment was intended to make clear that attacks on US military property would not be accepted. His statement sets out the prosecutor’s position on the alleged conduct; it does not establish that O’Corrain committed the offense. James Barnacle, who leads the FBI’s New York office, characterized the act as more than unplanned vandalism. That description is Barnacle’s assessment, while the sequence of alleged entry and damage is presented in the prosecutors’ account. Neither official statement changes the status of the claims as allegations in an indictment.

Supporters organized an online fundraiser and said O’Corrain had acted in protest against the US-Israel war in Gaza and US backing for Israel’s genocide. That account is attributed to the fundraiser’s supporters, rather than presented as a finding by the grand jury or prosecutors. The facts do not establish that the stated political motive was O’Corrain’s motive, and they do not describe him making that claim himself. The fundraiser’s explanation therefore sits alongside, but is distinct from, the legal account of the alleged breach and damage.

The reported aircraft value of approximately $60 million is a description of the C-130’s worth, not a quantified estimate of the harm caused in this incident. No cost for repairs, replacement, or lost use is supplied, although the aircraft was said to have become inoperable. Likewise, the possible sentence of up to 10 years is a maximum identified for a conviction, not a report of a sentence imposed. These distinctions matter because the aircraft’s valuation, its operational status, and the potential legal penalty describe separate consequences of the case. The available account does not state the outcome of the indictment or the Irish proceedings.

Taken together, the allegations concern entry into a secured airport area, actions inside a parked military aircraft, and damage that left it unable to operate. The plane’s role in a military assignment abroad gives the reported loss of operability a stated operational context beyond its approximate $60 million value. The indictment, the Irish charges, and the officials’ remarks describe the legal response and the authorities’ view of the incident, while leaving guilt unresolved. The supporters’ stated protest rationale offers a different account of motive, but the facts establish only that supporters circulated it through a fundraiser. What is specified is the alleged sequence, the aircraft’s stated value and assignment, the charges, and the maximum US prison term if conviction follows.

在深海几百米潜航三个月的核潜艇里，最致命的可能不是敌人的鱼雷，

而是新兵身上喷的两滴古龙香水。

每个上核潜艇的新兵在登艇前，都会经历一次比机场安检还严苛的搜包。

管带和老兵会把你行李翻个底朝天，香水、发胶、止汗喷雾、风油精，

甚至连做记号的粗头马克笔和涂改液，全都得当场没收。

很多人以为这是部队作风纪律，其实这是全艇一百多号人的保命底线。

核潜艇只要一下潜，那就是三个月完全与世隔绝的纯密闭大铁罐。

舱里所有的氧气全靠电解水，呼出来的二氧化碳全靠化学吸收塔一遍遍过滤循环。

在家里你喷两下香水觉得好闻，可到了密闭的核潜艇里，这些挥发出来的有机物根本排不出去。

它们会在空气里越聚越多，一旦被吸进几百度高温的空气催化燃烧装置里，

瞬间就会裂解成剧毒的酸性气体和神经毒素。

这玩意儿不仅能把价值上百万的精密空气净化滤芯彻底烧废，

还会让全艇几十上百个官兵在几天之内集体头痛恶心，甚至引发神经系统慢性中毒。

真要是到了那一发不可收拾的地步，整艘艇连潜伏任务都得被迫中断。

所以老潜艇兵退役回家，身上永远带着一股洗不掉的古怪潜艇味。

那是化学吸收剂散发出来的死鱼腥味，混杂着机油、臭氧和一百多个大老爷们三个月没晒过太阳的汗酸味。

据说潜艇兵换下来的作训服，在洗衣机里猛加柔顺剂洗上三五遍，挂在阳台上吹风半个月，

只要凑近一闻，骨子里那股深海大铁罐的味道依旧清晰刺鼻。

text:
We don't agree on much so I'm not so sure how far we can get with this, but the media muffed the story of the Brooks Brothers riot.

They did it by somehow omitting the fact that Miami-Dade was obligated to count all the ballots in that county and do so in a venue open to the public. It was doing neither. Cutting off public access was the spark that set off the protest. The intimidation narrative got elevated in the search for a motivation other than stopping the canvassing board from illegally limiting public observation.

Stopping votes from being counted? Yeah, but that's a half truth. The GOP had solid legal objections to what was happening (other than the situation in Miami-Dade). Remember, the Democrats were trying to decide Florida with four manual recounts in D-leaning counties. Who thinks that's a fair way to decide a whole state, where most counties had undervotes and overvotes? That's where the initial battle lines were drawn.

After that, the GOP legally fought the recount of undervotes (it wasn't really a statewide recount) ordered by the Florida Supreme Court. That was also a solid legal case, and the irony of it stems from the fact that Gore probably would have lost the recount the SCOTUS stopped. Gore needed the overvotes as well as the undervotes to have his best chance to overtake Bush. The GOP was arguing that sticking with undervotes treated overvote errors differently. They were right, and if the Florida court had agreed earlier it would have dissolved one of the primary SCOTUS objections to the relief they offered Gore. They didn't care for the lack of consistent standards either, of course.

So, anyway, not trying to derail your discussion, but I'm on a mission to correct the false narrative the media laid down on the BBR. If you're curious what evidence makes the case, simply ask. Cheers.

• Indoor air quality and whole-home filtration
• Water quality and filtration systems
• Circadian lighting and healthier sleep environments
• Home recovery spaces and infrared saunas
• Building materials and reducing unwanted environmental exposures
• Integrating wellness technology into modern homes

text:
USA VRS  AUSTRALIAN FOR NURSES

Most nurses lose 6-12 months and thousands of shillings by starting the US process, then changing to Australia, or vice versa.

Let me explain everything clearly, so you can make one decision and stick to it.

1. The Most Important Thing to Understand

Licence to practise is NOT the same as a visa to live and work.

Every country has 2 separate tracks:

1. Licence track- Can you legally work as a nurse there?
2. Visa track - Can you legally live and work there?

Passing NCLEX does NOT give you a visa. Getting a job offer does NOT give you a licence. You need both.

This is where most confusion comes from.

2. If You Choose the USA

The US pathway is long, but the long-term pay is the highest.

Step by step:

Step 1: Credential Evaluation - CGFNS / TruMerit CES
Your nursing school and Nursing Council of Kenya send your transcripts directly to TruMerit (formerly CGFNS). They check if your education is comparable to a US nursing degree.
- Time: 4-6 months, sometimes longer if your school is slow to respond
- Cost: Around $485 for the CES Professional Report

Step 2: Choose a State Board + Apply
You do NOT take NCLEX "for America". You take it for _one_ state, e.g. Texas, Florida, New York. Each state has different rules.
- Time: 2-6 months for board review

Step 3: English Test
Most states and VisaScreen require IELTS Academic / OET / TOEFL / PTE. You must check your specific state's scores.Train IELTS with just 8000 for  8 weeks with Dan Ndugu Morop 

Step 4: Pass NCLEX-RN
This is the exam you are reading for. You sit it at Pearson VUE, including centres in Kenya / India.
- Cost: $200 + $150 international scheduling fee
- You get an Authorization to Test (ATT), usually valid ∼90 days. Book quickly.

Step 5: Get State Licence
After you pass, the state issues your RN licence.

Step 6: VisaScreen Certificate
This is _mandatory_ for immigration, and it is different from NCLEX. It verifies your education, your Kenyan licence, your NCLEX pass, and your English.
- Cost: $740
- Time: 12-16 weeks after all documents are received

Step 7: Employer Sponsorship + EB-3 Green Card / Visa
An employer files for you. Then you wait for your priority date / visa interview.
- This is where your friend is stuck. He has done NCLEX and has a signed contract, but he is waiting for immigration steps. That wait is now routinely *12-18 months to arrive, and can be up to 3 years* depending on visa backlogs.

Total US Reality:
- To licence: 12-18 months
- To arrival in US: 3-5 years for many nurses, depending on visa retrogression
- Total official costs: $2,200 - $4,800, before study materials and travel
- Salary: $65,000 - $95,000 per year, depending on state

*US Advantage:* Highest pay, green card for family, 50 states to choose from later.
*US Disadvantage:* Slowest, most unpredictable visa. You can do everything right and still wait 2 years.

3. If You Choose Australia

Australia is now faster to _start working_, but you must follow the Australian regulator, AHPRA, not the US regulator.

Step by step:

Step 1: AHPRA Self-Check
Go to the AHPRA portal and enter your qualifications. For most Kenyan-trained nurses, you will be placed in *Stream B*.

Do this FIRST before you pay for any exam. It tells you your exact stream.

Step 2: English Test
AHPRA is strict:
- IELTS Academic: 7.0 in _each_ component, OR
- OET Nursing: B in all four components, OR
- PTE Academic: 65 in each skill

This English result is also used later for ANMAC, so do it well once.

*Step 3: Outcomes-Based Assessment (OBA)*
This has 2 parts:
a) *NCLEX-RN* - Yes, it is the _same_ NCLEX you are studying for now. Your reading is NOT wasted.
b) *OSCE* - A practical clinical exam held in Adelaide / Melbourne in Australia. You must travel for this.

*Step 4: AHPRA Registration*
After you pass OBA, you get registered as a nurse in Australia.

text:
I wrote this as a response to some one who didn't know of any poly relationships that worked and I wanted to offer up mine as an example of one that does. Be fore warned its a long one.

Hello, My Wife and I have done so and been Married for 16 years and going strong, She's even nursed me through Cancer 3 Times, The 3rd is on going.
We've been Poly from the beginning of our relationship but ours isn't a traditional one at all.

I was a performer for a very niche audience and my wife heard my voice on a Podcast and was enamored. We had mutual friends and met with a group of friends at a Dennys, She had just moved back to Florida from the midwest and needed a job, I was Working as a consultant for a failing Movie theater and was acting as their GM, my wife had prior theater experience so I hired her.

She was a fantastic worker. We were friendly and there was something there but we didn't act on it until one night I mentioned I was going to a local goth club and she and roommate ran into me at the club. We ended up hooking up as the kids call it. I was staying with a different group of friends while working the gig at the theater knowing it was temporary.  So a week later I ended up moving in with my soon to be wife and a week after that we got married on paper at the court house.  Two years after that we did a small ceremony with friends and family. In those 16 years we've each had separate relationships and we've shared.

The key is constant communication and recognizing not everyone is built for it. We also recognize that most people are in our lives for a few seasons sometimes many and some are life long but it's all temporary to one degree or another, so why deny each other all that life has to offer? I would never want to deny her happiness or limit her in any way nor she me.

We've both worked in the adult industry so some of that certainly factored in but our friends have referred to us as relationship goals as we are always in that new relationship energy there's still a lot of snuggling and being present with each other. Its not about sex either. I've had limited ability in that area especially during chemo and various surgery's and medications and again why would I deny her? We don't have children as much as we'd both like our jobs arent condusive to that, and my health casts a very big what if shadow.

I wont put my wifes specifics out on here but she has been mostly long distance dating 2 other  women for a couple years. They come over  every few months and we are all friends, I'm not involved with either of them sexually but I consider both to be very good friends and I have my own relationships with them. I haven't had a girl friend in awhile but some of my exs and I are still very close and in a traditional marriage some of those would be seen as crossing a line. This is what works for us, its not for everyone and we certainly have  non physical relationships with both men and women and we arent looking to sleep with every one we meet as is often the cliche with poly couples.

We genuinely love each other, and Id do anything for her and she for me as my full time caregiver she's had to do things no wife should and I'd even feel bad if I was in the hospital and a nurse had to attend to me at my worst but my wife has with out batting an eye. or making me feel bad about it.

She took the sickness and in health vow to the extreme.  I've spoken with many Cancer survivors and I can tell you by anecdote most marriages don't survive my kind of cancer no less two recurrences and a new one this year, not to mention all the auto immune issues and surgery's I've have had done.  I've had 5 so far this year with a big emergency surgery in march where my colon ruptured and had to be removed due in part to 20 years of crohns disease. I'm having a big 6th surgery this Friday to remove a large facial tumor that's attached itself to a major nerve cluster one the left side of my face effecting my eye ear and jaw which I hope I live through ad the nerve goes right into my brain.

The Surgery  has some serious risks its a 70/30 70% survive 30% dont. those arent great odds but my wife has stood by me and continues to stand by me and no one can tell me our relationship isnt as valid as the monogamous 2.5 kids in the burbs marriage ones. Where in many of those they become joyless, sexless affairs where the couples become more like roommates than lovers. That's not to say all of them are that way ,we certainly know some long term successful happy marriages but they arent the norm any more most of my married friends are on their 2nd 3rd or the 4th or more in some cases.

Not everyone is built the same, what works for some might not work for others, I certainly wouldn't suggest polyamory to everyone or anyone really because unless you have absolute trust and really good communication skills and can booth equally tell the other what's going on and what they are feeling it's probably not going to work,

You also have to be 100% honest with every one you date together or separately. Their emotional well being is just as important as either of yours and that is often over looked as many poly couples will see their 3rds or other relationships as playthings and not people and that in my opinion is so friggin wrong which is probably one of the reasons our relationship works and why I'm still friends with my Exs and as is my wife with hers and Exs isnt quite the right term we just move in and out of each others lives for seasons as I stated before.

I hope this helps to shed some light on what a Poly relationship can look like and be successful long term Maybe not everyone considers 16 years long term but I certainly do most peoples relationships these days tend not to last more than 6 or 7 years and often far less and many of the longer ones I know haven't had half the struggles ours had.

I also don't want anyone to think my marriage has been all one sided where she takes care of me. I've also taken great care of her, Ive supported every hobby she's had and gone above and beyond to help her.

One small example of this is she got into the clown fetish thing a long time ago, It was so not my thing but she was early into her cam girl career and she really want to embrace that persona as a character so I rebuilt her cam room to give it a Circus feel and taught myself how to make balloon animals all in one night. So the next day when she woke up she had the cam room she'd dreamed of as we had talked about it a great deal and I bought the supplies the week before. any way she woke up to a brand new cam room with a ton of balloon animals mostly elephants as those were her favorite and a note from me saying I may not get it but I'm all in on supporting you.

That character got her into several of the big a adult magazines playboy and hustler and she  has been a guest on numerous podcasts including some big ones like drinking bros.  That silly idea gave us a roof over our head, food in our fridge and provided after i wasnt able to work.  I'm not gonna lie its been a huge challenge and we've had to down size and we both know adult work has a  time limit.

We've been working on what comes next for a little while now but adult work is the only thing that's going to support a one income household with a ton of medical bills and related costs its not just prescriptions and copays but the gas and tolls getting to and from all the docs the lost works days having to take care of me and that alone makes a traditional 9 to 5 impossible.  Caregiver is a full time job by itself and it doesn't pay when your husband is the one you are caring for.

The adult industry has been our saving grace in more ways than one. Out of all the groups and  communities Ive been a part of long term like the Renaissance Festivals, Rocky Horror, Theater  and  venue owners, and IT colleagues. It was the people in the Adult Industry who most came through in our hour of need. Whether on my go fund me which has been up for almost 8 years  or  running their own fund raisers for us. It was them more than any other group for which I'll be eternally grateful.

So many look down on The Adult Industry folks even though so many out there consume our art and yes there is an art to this to be successful. So many think its easy money, its not. Imagine knowing your husband is in the ICU but you have rent and bills due and if you loose the health insurance your husband will surely die, with all that weighing on you you now have to go online and get naked, talk dirty,  be present, play therapist and  play a character with out any of your real life seeping through. You think that's easy? now spread that out over years.

It hasn't been all bad we've had a lot of fun with it over the years but it was supposed to be a temporary thing she did for couple years,  My wife  has an associates degree with no student debt and we had plans for a small farm and animal rescue that's now on the back burner and the money we'd put aside for that has been long since spent. The rough stuff aside, we've had the privilege to work with some really great loving and caring people. My wife and I are both proud to be part of that community.

So now that I've written my book I hope it's enlightened ya'll a bit. Well at least on  one poly relationship that's worked, albeit with some significant challenges. We all walk our own paths one size doesn't fit all and we shouldn't judge others for what works for them, so long as no kids are involved and everything is consensual among adults, how people choose to configure themselves and what relationships they have, is truly no one else's business  and shouldn't be looked down upon. To Quote the Different Strokes theme "What might be right for you may not be right for some.."
