Hello, My Wife and I have done so and been Married for 16 years and going strong, She's even nursed me through Cancer 3 Times, The 3rd is on going. 
We've been Poly from the beginning of our relationship but ours isn't a traditional one at all. 

I was a performer for a very niche audience and my wife heard my voice on a Podcast and was enamored. We had mutual friends and met with a group of friends at a Dennys, She had just moved back to Florida from the midwest and needed a job, I was Working as a consultant for a failing Movie theater and was acting as their GM, my wife had prior theater experience so I hired her. 

She was a fantastic worker. We were friendly and there was something there but we didn't act on it until one night I mentioned I was going to a local goth club and she and roommate ran into me at the club. We ended up hooking up as the kids call it. I was staying with a different group of friends while working the gig at the theater knowing it was temporary.  So a week later I ended up moving in with my soon to be wife and a week after that we got married on paper at the court house.  Two years after that we did a small ceremony with friends and family. In those 16 years we've each had separate relationships and we've shared. 

The key is constant communication and recognizing not everyone is built for it. We also recognize that most people are in our lives for a few seasons sometimes many and some are life long but it's all temporary to one degree or another, so why deny each other all that life has to offer? I would never want to deny her happiness or limit her in any way nor she me. 

We've both worked in the adult industry so some of that certainly factored in but our friends have referred to us as relationship goals as we are always in that new relationship energy there's still a lot of snuggling and being present with each other. Its not about sex either. I've had limited ability in that area especially during chemo and various surgery's and medications and again why would I deny her? We don't have children as much as we'd both like our jobs arent condusive to that, and my health casts a very big what if shadow.

 I wont put my wifes specifics out on here but she has been mostly long distance dating 2 other  women for a couple years. They come over  every few months and we are all friends, I'm not involved with either of them sexually but I consider both to be very good friends and I have my own relationships with them. I haven't had a girl friend in awhile but some of my exs and I are still very close and in a traditional marriage some of those would be seen as crossing a line. This is what works for us, its not for everyone and we certainly have  non physical relationships with both men and women and we arent looking to sleep with every one we meet as is often the cliche with poly couples.

 We genuinely love each other, and Id do anything for her and she for me as my full time caregiver she's had to do things no wife should and I'd even feel bad if I was in the hospital and a nurse had to attend to me at my worst but my wife has with out batting an eye. or making me feel bad about it. 

She took the sickness and in health vow to the extreme.  I've spoken with many Cancer survivors and I can tell you by anecdote most marriages don't survive my kind of cancer no less two recurrences and a new one this year, not to mention all the auto immune issues and surgery's I've have had done.  I've had 5 so far this year with a big emergency surgery in march where my colon ruptured and had to be removed due in part to 20 years of crohns disease. I'm having a big 6th surgery this Friday to remove a large facial tumor that's attached itself to a major nerve cluster one the left side of my face effecting my eye ear and jaw which I hope I live through ad the nerve goes right into my brain.

 The Surgery  has some serious risks its a 70/30 70% survive 30% dont. those arent great odds but my wife has stood by me and continues to stand by me and no one can tell me our relationship isnt as valid as the monogamous 2.5 kids in the burbs marriage ones. Where in many of those they become joyless, sexless affairs where the couples become more like roommates than lovers. That's not to say all of them are that way ,we certainly know some long term successful happy marriages but they arent the norm any more most of my married friends are on their 2nd 3rd or the 4th or more in some cases.

Not everyone is built the same, what works for some might not work for others, I certainly wouldn't suggest polyamory to everyone or anyone really because unless you have absolute trust and really good communication skills and can booth equally tell the other what's going on and what they are feeling it's probably not going to work, 

You also have to be 100% honest with every one you date together or separately. Their emotional well being is just as important as either of yours and that is often over looked as many poly couples will see their 3rds or other relationships as playthings and not people and that in my opinion is so friggin wrong which is probably one of the reasons our relationship works and why I'm still friends with my Exs and as is my wife with hers and Exs isnt quite the right term we just move in and out of each others lives for seasons as I stated before.

 I hope this helps to shed some light on what a Poly relationship can look like and be successful long term Maybe not everyone considers 16 years long term but I certainly do most peoples relationships these days tend not to last more than 6 or 7 years and often far less and many of the longer ones I know haven't had half the struggles ours had. 

I also don't want anyone to think my marriage has been all one sided where she takes care of me. I've also taken great care of her, Ive supported every hobby she's had and gone above and beyond to help her. 

One small example of this is she got into the clown fetish thing a long time ago, It was so not my thing but she was early into her cam girl career and she really want to embrace that persona as a character so I rebuilt her cam room to give it a Circus feel and taught myself how to make balloon animals all in one night. So the next day when she woke up she had the cam room she'd dreamed of as we had talked about it a great deal and I bought the supplies the week before. any way she woke up to a brand new cam room with a ton of balloon animals mostly elephants as those were her favorite and a note from me saying I may not get it but I'm all in on supporting you. 

That character got her into several of the big a adult magazines playboy and hustler and she  has been a guest on numerous podcasts including some big ones like drinking bros.  That silly idea gave us a roof over our head, food in our fridge and provided after i wasnt able to work.  I'm not gonna lie its been a huge challenge and we've had to down size and we both know adult work has a  time limit. 

We've been working on what comes next for a little while now but adult work is the only thing that's going to support a one income household with a ton of medical bills and related costs its not just prescriptions and copays but the gas and tolls getting to and from all the docs the lost works days having to take care of me and that alone makes a traditional 9 to 5 impossible.  Caregiver is a full time job by itself and it doesn't pay when your husband is the one you are caring for.

The adult industry has been our saving grace in more ways than one. Out of all the groups and  communities Ive been a part of long term like the Renaissance Festivals, Rocky Horror, Theater  and  venue owners, and IT colleagues. It was the people in the Adult Industry who most came through in our hour of need. Whether on my go fund me which has been up for almost 8 years  or  running their own fund raisers for us. It was them more than any other group for which I'll be eternally grateful.

 So many look down on The Adult Industry folks even though so many out there consume our art and yes there is an art to this to be successful. So many think its easy money, its not. Imagine knowing your husband is in the ICU but you have rent and bills due and if you loose the health insurance your husband will surely die, with all that weighing on you you now have to go online and get naked, talk dirty,  be present, play therapist and  play a character with out any of your real life seeping through. You think that's easy? now spread that out over years. 

It hasn't been all bad we've had a lot of fun with it over the years but it was supposed to be a temporary thing she did for couple years,  My wife  has an associates degree with no student debt and we had plans for a small farm and animal rescue thats now on the back burner and the money we'd put aside for that has ben long since spent. The rough stuff aside, we've had the privilege to work with some really great loving and caring people. My wife and I are both proud to be part of that community. 

So now that I've written my book I hope it's enlightened ya'll a bit. Well at least on  one poly relationship that's worked, albeit with some significant challenges. We all walk our own paths one size doesn't fit all and we shouldn't judge others for what works for them, so long as no kids are involved and everything is consensual among adults, how people choose to configure themselves and what relationships they have, is truly no one else's business  and shouldn't be looked down upon. To Quote the Different Strokes theme "What might be right for you may not be right for some.."

MNGOP: Nearly a Decade of Walz-DFL Policies Has Left Minnesota Near the Bottom in Economic Growth

The report ranks Minnesota 49th out of 50 states in GDP per capita growth this decade, along with 43rd in per capita income growth, 46th in wage growth, and 47th in median household income growth since 2019.

MNGOP Chairman Alex Plechash issued the following statement:

“These numbers are a stunning indictment of nearly a decade of failed Walz-DFL leadership. Minnesota was once an economic powerhouse. Today, we’re nearly dead last in economic growth. Years of higher taxes, anti-business mandates, excessive spending, and education policies that prioritize politics over academic excellence have come at a steep price”.

“Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar campaigned on cleaning up the mess in St. Paul. But this mess is the direct result of the very policies and political leaders she has supported for years. Minnesotans deserve more than a third Walz term”.

“Republicans will be relentless watchdogs, holding Klobuchar and the DFL accountable. But we will also offer real solutions to lower taxes, reduce regulations, restore educational excellence, and make Minnesota competitive again”.

“The question is whether Amy Klobuchar will listen and work with Republicans to reverse these failed policies, or simply continue the same agenda that put Minnesota at the bottom”.

“Minnesota can do better. Republicans are ready to lead with solutions. Is Amy Klobuchar ready to listen?”

🏀 BLAZERS 105–106 WOLVES: CLINGAN SHINES, NORI’S ROTATION RAISES QUESTIONS

First, give Donovan Clingan his flowers. 👏

28 MIN | 6 PTS | 9 REB | +17

His size, rebounding and interior presence gave Minnesota problems. One costly late turnover shouldn’t erase an otherwise strong performance.

But here’s what I don’t understand about Micah Nori’s rotation:

🔴 Robert Williams III: 15 MIN | -18
🔴 Branden Carlson: 14 MIN | -10
🔴 Micah Potter: 1 MIN | -6
❌ Yang Hansen: DNP

Plus/minus doesn’t tell the whole story. And I’m not claiming Yang would’ve guaranteed a win.

But why not even explore another option?

Clingan and Yang could complement each other.

Clingan brings rim protection, rebounding and physicality. Yang offers passing vision, high-post playmaking and offensive creativity.

Against Gobert, a high-low combination might create different looks and force Minnesota to adjust.

Would it work? Maybe. Would there be defensive risks? Absolutely.

That’s why it’s worth testing.

Portland also needs to own its late-game collapse. Blowing a seven-point lead and losing on a crucial inbound turnover raises questions about execution and coaching decisions.

My point isn’t that Yang deserves guaranteed minutes. It’s that Portland needs a real developmental plan for its first-round pick.

I can praise Clingan, respect Minnesota’s win, and still question Nori’s decision to give Yang zero minutes.

✊🏾 BMB EMPOWER NETWORK OPINION | Black voters answered Trump. The South made it historic.

Across the country, roughly nine in ten Black voters backed Democratic candidates for the U.S. House in the 2026 midterms, according to the AP Voter Poll. Donald Trump’s name was off the ballot. The Republicans carrying his MAGA agenda were on it. Black voters overwhelmingly rejected the offer. 

If you want to understand what Black political power looks like, start in Mississippi. In a state Trump carried by nearly 23 points just two years ago, Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction. Twelve majority-Black counties in Mississippi gave Colom more votes in a midterm than Kamala Harris received there in a presidential election. Those communities helped decide who gets to vote on federal judges and voting-rights legislation for the next six years. 

Georgia elected Keisha Lance Bottoms its first Black woman governor. In Texas, Black voters helped a coalition elect Gina Hinojosa governor and send James Talarico to the U.S. Senate. And the story reached well beyond the South. Wisconsin elected David Crowley its first Black governor. Give Black voters their credit as people who shaped those coalitions and changed who governs. 

And yes, there was an answer for the Supreme Court. In Louisiana v. Callais, the Court struck down Louisiana’s congressional map with its second majority-Black district. Southern states redrew district lines in the ruling’s wake. In North Carolina, Republicans drew a map aimed at winning 11 of 14 House seats. After voters had their say, Democrats were on track to win 11 of 14 themselves. The ruling still stands. So does the political rebuke. 

Here’s where white supremacy enters the argument. One of its oldest claims is that white Southerners are entitled to govern and Black Southerners are expected to live with their decisions. A Black woman preparing to govern Georgia and a Black Mississippian preparing to represent his entire state in the Senate answer that claim directly. People cast ballots for many reasons. The collective result carries a meaning of its own. 

Black voters gave Trump, MAGA and the Republican Party an unmistakable answer. Now Democrats owe those voters an answer of their own. When voting rights come up for a vote, when state budgets reach a governor’s desk, and when families ask whether they can finally get health coverage, what will you deliver with the power we helped put in your hands?

According to a US prosecution filing ahead of Nikhil Gupta’s sentencing, former RAW officer Vikash Yadav allegedly offered to arrange airport clearance in Imphal for an aircraft carrying drugs, along with the supply of AK-56 series rifles and Tokarev/M20 pistols. The offer was made as part of a proposed drug and weapons transaction intended as an additional incentive in the plot to assassinate Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.

The details, which appear in the prosecution’s sentencing submission, underline how Manipur was being positioned within a larger network of narcotics and arms trafficking. Imphal airport, in the heart of a state already struggling with cross-border drug flows, illegal arms and armed groups, was reportedly viewed as a viable transit point for such operations. The proposal also envisaged the movement of large quantities of drugs and weapons, further exposing the vulnerabilities that have long been exploited in the region.

These allegations are serious. They come against a backdrop of earlier cases in which security personnel themselves were found involved in drug-related activities in Manipur. Such incidents highlight how deep and entrenched the drugs network has become, extending even into layers of the security apparatus that are meant to counter it.

This revelation comes at a time when Manipur continues to face the combined threats of narcotics trafficking from Myanmar, the circulation of illegal arms, and the activities of armed groups that have repeatedly undermined peace. When even an airport in the state capital is alleged to have been offered as a facilitation point for such cargo, the scale of the challenge becomes clearer.

The depth of these networks demands more than routine enforcement. It calls for serious policy changes and stronger institutional measures to effectively tackle the challenge. Sustained vigilance, deeper probes into the involvement of those within the system and decisive action against the entire chain of trafficking are now essential if the state is to break free from the grip of narcotics and the violence it sustains.

text:
Sjoe! The Residual Chair🪑Who Gets Left Sitting Outside South🇿🇦Africa's Equity Arithmetic? ~ The Boy in the Water Queue🚰A Constitutional Promise Meets an Uncounted Future 📖 ~ Constitutional Dignity, Residual Reality⚖️The Debate South Africa Has Yet to Measure 🇿🇦
Sjoe. You open Government Gazette 52514 of 15 April 2025 and the arithmetic is already incomplete. The five-year sectoral numerical targets under the Employment Equity Act “are not intended to add up to 100 percent.” They exclude white males with no disabilities and foreign nationals from the preference calculation (Department of Employment and Labour, 2025). 

Preference is applied first. What remains is residual by design. 

Political scientists have long observed that once a residual category is institutionalised, organisations develop incentives to defend the boundary that creates it. Firms and universities face clear pressure on the preference side and quieter market pressure on the residual side. 

The result is a sorting mechanism whose cumulative effects on career choices and skills retention remain largely unmeasured at national level. Under high structural unemployment the leftover market becomes zero-sum. Local-search requirements before residual foreign appointments are unevenly enforced. Residual citizen priority after preference is absent by design.

A nine-year-old orphaned white boy stands in a municipal water queue. The tanker is late. He was born after the 1996 Constitution. Formal dignity under Section 10 remains intact. The residual market he will later enter treats white citizens and foreign nationals as interchangeable non-beneficiaries once preference has been served. 

Full citizenship rights stay intact. Residual priority does not. No public residual-occupancy series by citizenship exists. The design therefore continues to score while its effects on progression, emigration decisions and investment location stay opaque.

Sjoe!
The Gazette draws the line with bureaucratic neatness. The leftover chairs do not care how neat the line is. They simply remain the only ones left.

Stirring Questions:
If the targets are written not to reach 100 percent, who is the residual category intended to serve once preference has been applied?
Does the continued absence of residual-occupancy data by citizenship itself accelerate the political weight of the residual?
What mechanism remains to protect citizen priority in the leftover market after preference has already been served?

What these questions together reveal is the shift from the existence of the residual—which is statutory—to the time dimension. The longer the residual operates without residual-citizen priority or transparent data, the more the unmeasured costs accumulate as lived experience, even while no official debt exists.

1. After the Ratio

The apartheid-era per-pupil spending disparity is a documented historical fact. Research places the ratio near 16.6:1 in the late 1960s and near 4.4:1 by the late 1980s (Christie, 1985; Fiske & Ladd, 2004). Ramaphosa’s R12-to-R1 illustration simply restates that record. Musk left South Africa in that period. The boy in the queue did not. 

A reply that accepts the historical ratio, refuses to convert it into a continuing personal debt, and conditions further discussion on publication of the missing residual ledger is therefore tighter than one that stops at 1994. Without that series the framing remains partial. 

Economic implication follows: opportunity costs that are real for individuals but unaggregated at national level still shape behaviour. Skills emigration and firm location preferences respond to the residual gradient even while the national ledger stays empty.

SpaceX’s earlier offer of free satellite service, solar power and devices for more than 5,000 rural schools serving approximately 2.4 million pupils, at a cost near R500 million, was not accepted under the ownership rules. That package would have delivered connectivity without residual equity transfer. 

Additional capital could be conditioned on three outputs: residual-occupancy data by citizenship and local-search compliance; formal-sector growth that reduces leftover intensity; and practical support for the substrates the 9–11 window requires—reliable water logistics and specialised orphan-protection funding. 

Preference under Section 9(2) can remain temporary while these steps occur. Equity-equivalent programmes already allow multinationals to generate empowerment credit through 100 percent Black-owned suppliers without expanding residual local ownership. Both routes are legal. Both leave residual local citizens outside the preference arithmetic and the optical benefit. 

Redirecting resources toward measurement tests redesign rather than underwriting the scorecard. The residual market is therefore not only residual. It is selectively permeable to non-citizens through routes that leave the statutory scorecard untouched.

Sjoe!
The scorecard and the photograph were never required to agree. One keeps the arithmetic. The other keeps the caption. The residual chair does not mind which one sits in it.

Stirring Questions:
If residual occupancy data by citizenship were published tomorrow, would the give-back claim still rest solely on the pre-1994 ratio?
What stops capital from being directed at measurement and capacity expansion instead of scorecard compliance?
How many additional years of residual design under current scarcity are required before the cumulative opportunity costs become politically visible enough to force measurement?

What these questions together reveal is the conversion of an investment demand into a test of redesign. The school package and the residual ledger are independent. Together they ask whether the leftover market can be made less zero-sum before the next cohort enters it.

2. The Queue and the Gazette

Piaget’s concrete-operational stage, confirmed in contemporary Southern African developmental research, identifies the years roughly nine to eleven as a high-leverage window in which children construct durable judgments about fairness, institutional reliability and personal value (Piaget, 1952; Louw et al., 2024). The residual rules crystallised in Gazette 52514, ambient narratives that sometimes racialise ordinary competence standards, and the thinning of specialised protective services for the approximately 2.7 million orphaned children—about 13 percent of all children, most in kinship care (Statistics South Africa, 2025; Hall & Hendricks, 2025)—occupy precisely that window for the boy. 

Governance literature has long noted that formal systems and informal care arrangements are not perfect substitutes. When the formal system weakens, the informal system is asked to carry a heavier load without the resources to do so. Differential vulnerability appears exactly where developmental dependence is highest and private buffers are lowest. 

Thirty years of preference-first arithmetic without residual-citizen priority or published data have already shaped the environment he inhabits. The residual is no longer only an adult labour-market feature. It is an intergenerational inheritance whose developmental cost can be observed inside the non-racial order the 1996 text claimed to establish. 

Legal scholars have long observed that temporary measures of redress can harden into permanent expectations. Once the expectation of permanent racial accounting takes root, the original constitutional bargain becomes harder to defend in practice even if it remains intact on paper.

Section 235 states that the right of the South African people as a whole to self-determination, as manifested in this Constitution, does not preclude recognition of the right of self-determination of any community sharing a common cultural and language heritage, within a territorial entity in the Republic or in any other way determined by national legislation (Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996). The provision is permissive. 

Academic commentary has consistently noted that it has never been given operational content through detailed national legislation (de Villiers, 2014). By contrast, the residual targets operate daily. Any investment discussion therefore occurs inside a constitutional text that still contains this opening. An unactivated self-determination provision and an active residual filter now sit side by side. The 9–11 cohort will enter whichever instrument the adults leave in force. 

Constitutional time runs in legislative cycles. Developmental time runs in windows that close. The mismatch is structural.

Sjoe!
The scaffolding plans are exquisite. The builders, however, appear to be permanently in a meeting about the symbolism of the scaffolding. The children keep ageing on schedule.

Stirring Questions:
If the highest-leverage developmental period is being filled with residual narratives and thin scaffolding, what civic culture should we expect in fifteen years?
Can a non-racial constitution remain coherent while successive post-1994 cohorts carry permanent collective residual costs?
What measurable indicators would show that the 9–11 cohort’s emerging judgments of fairness are improving or deteriorating?

What these questions together reveal is the mismatch between constitutional time and developmental time. Constitutions operate in legislative cycles. Children operate in windows that close. The questions force the two clocks into the same conversation.

3. The Neighbouring Settlement

Zimbabwe’s 2000 fast-track process extinguished titles. The 2020 Global Compensation Deed established a framework of approximately US$3.5 billion for improvements on the farms, not the land itself. By October 2026 cash payments plus dollar-denominated Treasury bonds had reached roughly US$508–521 million for early batches of claimants, explicitly linked to arrears clearance and capital-market re-engagement (Bloomberg, 2026). 

South Africa has extinguished no equivalent residual titles or contracts. Gazette 52514 continues to define a residual pool for future opportunities. Ramaphosa’s 29 August 2025 remarks at the Zimbabwe Agricultural Show described the post-1980 reforms as essential for historical redress and food security, and as mirroring South Africa’s own experience. 

The legal categories remain distinct—completed property extinguishment versus ongoing opportunity sorting. Yet the political signal travels. Crystallised costs can compel instruments while unmeasured ones merely accumulate. 

International comparisons sharpen the point. Preference regimes that retained residual citizen priority after temporary measures tended to face less political friction once scarcity intensified. Those that treated residual seats as fully interchangeable between citizens and non-citizens often saw residual competition become a durable feature of labour-market politics. 

Every additional year of residual design under scarcity increases the chance the parallel is later invoked. The boy in the water queue supplies the living measure of the choice still available. Residual costs that remain unmeasured can still shape behaviour and eventually force settlement or redesign once the political calculus shifts.

Sjoe!
One government is settling yesterday’s residual with bonds and cash. The other is still allocating today’s residual with scorecards. The calendar is the same. The paperwork is not.

Stirring Questions:
If residual costs only become payable once a political decision crystallises them, what evidence threshold would be required before South Africa’s residual opportunity costs moved from individual experience to national conversation?
Does the Zimbabwean precedent alter the political calculus for residual redesign inside South Africa even while the legal categories remain distinct?
When a state pays former owners to restore investor trust, what does that imply for the long-term cost of leaving residual competition unmeasured?

What these questions together reveal is that the comparison stays inside its proper role: a concrete demonstration that residual costs can force settlement once crystallised, while insisting that South Africa’s residual has not yet crossed that threshold. 

The questions prevent both denial of the design and premature equivalence.

Synthesis

Independent lines of evidence converge from different fields. 
Statutory text creates the residual by design (Department of Employment and Labour, 2025). 
Developmental psychology identifies a high-leverage window currently occupied by residual rules and thin scaffolding (Piaget, 1952; Louw et al., 2024). 
Official statistics quantify a large orphan population at elevated baseline risk (Statistics South Africa, 2025). 
Constitutional text supplies both inherent dignity and an unused self-determination clause (Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996; de Villiers, 2014). 
Neighbouring compensation figures show that crystallised residuals can produce instruments (Bloomberg, 2026). 

Multiple independent witnesses describe the same institutional object from different angles: the residual is consequential as design and experience; the residual total remains a hypothesis; redesign remains available inside functioning constitutional institutions. Think of them as overlapping fingerprints or independent witnesses describing the same event. 

The claim is falsifiable: publish residual-occupancy data by citizenship, track specialised funding release rates, and measure whether the 9–11 cohort’s emerging judgments of fairness improve or deteriorate. 

If the indicators move toward competence, trust and reduced intergenerational suspicion, the argument weakens. If they do not, the argument strengthens. The stakes are the civic capacities of the next generation. 

The scaffolding is either raised around agency or it is left thin while the residual continues to score.

Objections

Some will argue that white representation at top management remains high relative to economically active population share. The apex figure is accurate and belongs in the same analysis. It does not cancel residual pressure lower down, nor does it alter the statutory fact that white citizens and foreign nationals share the non-preference residual. 

Others will say larger structural problems must be solved first. Developmental science suggests the opposite sequencing: deficits formed in the concrete-operational stage become harder and more expensive to reverse later. Waiting for perfect conditions is itself a form of the inefficiency under examination. 

A third view holds that racial consciousness remains necessary indefinitely. The constitutional text speaks of persons. Permanent essentialism and shared standards of evidence and trust pull in opposite directions.

Conclusion

The residual is not a contradiction in terms. It is the precise description of the system as it currently operates. Formal dignity is inherent, universal and criminally protected. Residual opportunity design, shared material scarcity, thin protective scaffolding and ambient narrative occupy the same childhood without themselves constituting criminal impairment of that dignity. 

The orphaned white boy aged 9–11 stands in the water queue today and will later enter the residual market. His legal claim remains whole. The conditions that shape its lived formation and future expression are structured by statute, capacity and scarcity. 

Publish the residual occupancy series by citizenship, or accept that he will inherit an uncounted gradient the 1996 text never named. 

The chairs are still residual. They need not stay that way. 

The cumulative evidence demonstrates that residual design is real, consequential under scarcity, and legally distinct from property seizure, with the residual total remaining a hypothesis rather than an established liability. 

The precise task is to decide, on evidence, whether residual citizen priority after preference should be restored and whether the overall opportunity set can be expanded. 

The adults still hold the pen. 

Sjoe.
The cumulative evidence proves the residual is real as design, consequential under scarcity for the post-1994 cohort, and still open to measurement or redesign.

text:
Doctor Strange didn't give Thanos the Time Stone because he trusted him or because he had surrendered. He gave it away because, out of the 14,000,605 possible futures he examined in Avengers: Infinity War, only one showed the Avengers ultimately defeating Thanos. The crucial detail is that Strange initially tells Tony Stark he would sacrifice Tony or Peter Parker rather than surrender the Stone. Yet when Thanos is about to kill Tony on Titan, Strange suddenly offers it in exchange for Tony's life. That reversal tells us something important: after examining the possible futures, Strange realized that Tony's survival was essential to the one successful outcome. The Avengers couldn't simply prevent Thanos from collecting the Stones at that moment; according to Strange's vision, the path to victory required events to unfold differently. Strange wasn't trying to win the battle on Titan. He was making sure they could eventually win the war. And when he tells Tony, “We're in the endgame now,” he's revealing that the apparent defeat is part of a much larger sequence of events.

And yes, Tony Stark really was that important, because Avengers: Endgame reveals that Strange wasn't merely saving a friend; he was preserving the person who would make victory possible. Five years after the Snap, Scott Lang returns from the Quantum Realm with the idea of using it for time travel, but Tony is the one who solves the crucial navigation problem that makes the Avengers' Time Heist possible. That mission allows them to recover the Infinity Stones and reverse Thanos's destruction. Then, during the final battle, when Thanos threatens to wipe out the universe and rebuild it, Tony uses his nanotechnology to take the Stones and sacrifice himself to destroy Thanos and his army. Strange's single raised finger confirms that this is the victorious future he foresaw. Marvel's official account supports this interpretation, and Endgame co-writer Stephen McFeely has explained that Strange's vision already implied Tony would die achieving that victory. There is one important distinction: the films don't prove that every imaginable alternative was impossible, only that this was the sole victory among the futures Strange examined. But within the story, surrendering the Time Stone was necessary to preserve the chain of events leading to that outcome. The heartbreaking irony is that Strange saved Tony from dying on Titan because Tony still had one final sacrifice to make. He wasn't saving Tony from death forever. He was saving him for the moment when his death could save everyone else.

This historic photograph shows the grave of U.S. Army Air Forces Flight Officer Joseph Levy, a P-40 Warhawk fighter pilot who was shot down by Japanese anti-aircraft fire over Kiska Island in the Aleutian Islands, Alaska; captured on August 25, 1943, after Allied forces retook the island...

The wooden marker was erected by Imperial Japanese Army troops who buried him with respect. The handwritten sign reads:

"Sleeping here, a brave air-hero who lost youth and happiness for his Mother land. July 25 - Nippon Army".

Levy's remains were later exhumed and returned to the United States for a final resting place. 

. . . 

The grave of an American pilot buried by Imperial Japanese troops. The gesture stands out as a rare act of wartime respect from enemy troops.

The words carved in humble characters show a soldier’s compassion even in war. Kiska was part of the Aleutian Campaign and saw actual combat between U.S. and Japanese forces. 

In the aftermath, American troops found and exhumed several graves on the island before retreating, but this one was noted for its surprising dignity.

This memorial offers a poignant contrast to the brutality of war. It reminds us that humanity can persist even in moments of conflict. A simple wooden tribute endures as evidence that honor can cross the boundaries of hostility.

Not bad for a soldier born in Nairobi, Kenya. 

In 1995, Charles Roland Vincent Walker - Roly to his fellow officers - was serving in East Tyrone with the 1st Battalion, @Irish_Guards. Three decades later, as Chief of the General Staff, General Sir Roly Walker led a British military delegation to Rawalpindi for talks with Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.

The visit offers Britain a chance to deepen defence cooperation in a part of the world that matters to it. 

Rawalpindi is also home to Global Industrial & Defence Solutions, one of Pakistan's leading state-owned defence groups. It markets and exports military equipment and technology for land, air and naval forces. Pakistani press reports put its workforce at about 27,000.

There is a little history in the address. In 1851, Lord Dalhousie decided to establish a permanent cantonment at Rawalpindi, where the 53rd Regiment of Foot had already taken up quarters. The city's garrison church followed in 1854. Robert Milman, the Bishop of Calcutta, was buried there after his death in Rawalpindi in 1876. 

The city went on to house the British Indian Army's Northern Command, whose headquarters formed the nucleus of Pakistan Army GHQ at Partition in 1947, under its first commander-in-chief, General Sir Frank Messervy. It was at GHQ in Rawalpindi that Walker was received with a guard of honour.

The public account of Walker's visit makes no mention of Kakul. I hope he gets the chance to go. It was there, in the hills near Abbottabad, that the Pakistan Military Academy took shape in the months after independence. Colonel Francis Ingall was given the job of establishing it on the Sandhurst model, and the academy held its first passing-out parade in November 1948. In the years since, Kakul has made those traditions its own.

@RMASandhurst had a chance to see just how well on 11 June 2026. 

Major Haider Gulzar, the academy's adjutant, led a nine-member Pakistani contingent that won the international team trophy and took the prizes for Best Pace Sticker and Best Driver. 

It was Pakistan's fourth documented victory, following wins in 2018, 2019 and 2020. The British Army's account called it a second successive win, though the Sandhurst Trust and Forces News both put Bahrain Police first and Pakistan second in 2025. 

In the war on terrorism, there is a figure worth pausing over.

@BrownUniversity's @CostsOfWar project estimates that between October 2001 and April 2021, Pakistan lost 9,314 military and police personnel in the conflicts that followed 9/11.

The losses, meanwhile, have gone on. In 2026 alone, up to 16 November, the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies @PICSSIsb recorded 599 security personnel killed in terrorist attacks. The Pakistan Army is truly an army worthy of its name.

And if you have ever wondered how important the relationship between the British and Pakistani armies is, I challenge you to search X for "General Sir Roly Walker", the Chief of the General Staff.

Almost every Indian household has at least one "combo" endowment or money-back insurance policy pitched with the promise: "Your life is covered AND you get guaranteed returns back at maturity!"

Here is the reality check: Trying to combine life protection and wealth creation into a single policy gives you the worst of both worlds, a dangerously low life cover for your family AND slow 4% to 5.5% returns that barely keep up with inflation!

Why Keeping Term Insurance and Mutual Funds Separate Wins Every Time:

• THE "COMBO" COVER IS TOO SMALL: If you pay ₹1,00,000 a year into an endowment plan, your life cover is often only ₹10 Lakhs to ₹15 Lakhs. If something happens to the breadwinner, ₹10 Lakhs will barely support a family for 18 months! A pure Term Insurance plan gives a ₹1 Crore to ₹2 Crore cover for a fraction of that cost.

• THE HIDDEN RETURN DRAG (4.5% vs. 12%): Suppose you put ₹1,00,000/year for 20 years into a combo policy earning ~5%—your corpus reaches ~₹34 Lakhs. Now imagine paying ₹15,000/year for a ₹1.5 Crore Term Plan and investing the remaining ₹85,000/year (~₹7,083/month SIP) into diversified Equity Mutual Funds at an assumed 12% return. Your mutual fund corpus alone grows to ~₹70+ Lakhs!

• ZERO FLEXIBILITY & LOCK-IN PENALTIES: Combo policies lock your cash for 15 to 25 years. If you miss premiums or need urgent liquidity in Year 4, heavy surrender charges wipe out a huge chunk of your own money. Mutual funds offer transparent liquidity whenever life priorities shift.

• CRYSTAL-CLEAR PURPOSE: Insurance is a shield designed to protect your family's lifestyle in your absence. Mutual funds are a growth engine designed to fund your dreams while you are alive. Let each tool do the one job it was built for!

3 Smart Steps to Clean Up Your Portfolio Today:

1. SEPARATE YOUR SAFETY FROM YOUR GROWTH: Buy a pure Term Life Insurance plan (10x to 15x your annual income) + Health Insurance first, so your family's downside is 100% protected.

2. CHANNEL SURPLUS SAVINGS INTO GOAL-BASED SIPs: Invest the money you save on hefty combo premiums into diversified Equity, Flexi Cap, or Multi-Asset Mutual Funds aligned with your 7+ year milestones.

3. AUDIT EXISTING POLICIES WITH AN AMFI-REGISTERED MFD: Before buying any new "guaranteed return" plan or surrendering an old policy, consult an AMFI-registered Mutual Fund Distributor to calculate its true IRR and build a clean Regular Plan wealth roadmap.

The Bottom Line:
Don't buy a Swiss Army knife when you need a dedicated shield and a high-speed engine. Protect your family with Term Insurance and build real wealth with Mutual Funds.

text:
Sounds like someone picked a shitty location to launch their rockets and expand their business if they really cared about their neighbors, the environment or how it affects other people around them. Sounds like poor planning and lack of foresight. Plenty of other places with no one within miles to build on… 

Why should people have to uproot their families because somebody decided they’re gonna build a rocket in a populated place? Families are more important than rockets for most humans in touch with humanity. Most people care about the stability of their families over rocket launches. A lot of these people were there, long before he bought the land and didn’t agree to this. 
There is no land in the US that would allow this to happen without residential neighborhoods within 30 miles of them. Which led me to look into how they did this in the first place.👇Looks like manipulation, exploitation and leverage. 

“SpaceX was allowed to build in Boca Chica through a mix of strategic location shopping, intense state political backing, and an incremental permitting process that started small and scaled up after billions were already poured in concrete.

1. The "Bait-and-Switch" Permitting Path
•Starting Small (2012–2014): When SpaceX applied for federal approval, it pitched Boca Chica as a quiet commercial spaceport for up to 12 launches a year of its much smaller Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets—not the massive, experimental Starship system.

•Passing the Initial Review: Based on those smaller numbers, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a full Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) in 2014 concluding the site would have minimal impact on neighboring South Padre Island and Port Isabel (about 5 miles away).

•Scaling Up Once Built: After building its factories and launch pad, SpaceX pivoted to Starship—a rocket roughly twice as powerful as the Saturn V moon rocket—and repeatedly asked the FAA for amended approvals (such as the 2022 Programmatic Environmental Assessment) rather than starting over from scratch.

2. Aggressive Texas State & Local Support
•Changing State Law (2013): Before SpaceX even broke ground, the Texas Legislature passed a law specifically allowing Cameron County to close Boca Chica Beach and Highway 4 for spaceflight activities—something previously illegal under Texas’s strict Open Beaches Act.

•Millions in Incentives: Texas state officials and local economic development boards offered SpaceX roughly $15 million to $20 million in direct grants, tax abatements, and infrastructure funding to beat out competing bids from Florida, Georgia, and Puerto Rico.

•Economic Desperation: Cameron County has long been one of the poorest counties in the U.S. Local officials viewed SpaceX as a once-in-a-generation economic lifeline and largely waved through early land purchases and zoning requests.

3. Exploiting a Regulatory Gray Area

•Fragmented Land Ownership: Unlike Cape Canaveral—where the federal government owns a massive, unified 15,000-acre buffer zone—Boca Chica was a patchwork of tiny private lots, state parkland, and federal wildlife refuges. SpaceX quietly bought up dozens of small residential lots in Boca Chica Village through shell companies (like Dogleg Park LLC) before announcing its plans, establishing a foothold right in the middle of PROTECTED STATE and FEDERAL land.

•No Zoning Laws: Unincorporated Cameron County had almost no traditional zoning restrictions preventing heavy industrial rocket manufacturing next to a coastal village or WILDLIFE REFUGE.

4. Strategic Leverage Over Federal Regulators

Once SpaceX became NASA’s sole contractor to land astronauts on the Moon (via the Artemis program) and the Pentagon's primary launch provider, federal agencies faced enormous political pressure not to slow down Starship development—leading regulators to repeatedly grant conditional approvals and mitigations rather than shutting the site down.”  -Google Ai

text:
This is what you get when you have people that refuse to assimilate to our laws and culture. This guy honestly thinks he should get special treatment. 

 Georgia patrol officer clocked a 2021 Ford Escape flying down the highway at 94 mph in a posted 70 mph zone, this should have been an open-and-shut, five-minute roadside stop.

 The officer ran the information, walked back up with a citation in hand, and explained the process. All the driver had to do was sign his name, take his copy, and handle it through court or pay the fine down the line.

​Instead, the driver decided roadside legal fiction was a better strategy.
​Claiming he was being targeted for having an out-of-state license, he flatly refused to sign the citation and demanded to speak to a supervisor on scene before doing anything.

 The officer clearly and repeatedly explained the reality: there is no statutory right to hold an officer hostage on the shoulder waiting for a supervisor over a speeding ticket, and signing the document is strictly an acknowledgment of receipt, not an admission of guilt.

In Georgia, under O.C.G.A. § 40-13-2.1, that signature is your written promise to appear. Refusing it strips away the citation-and-release mechanism, leaving an officer with only one lawful option: physical custodial arrest.
​When given the clear choice to sign or face booking, the driver doubled down, asserting he wasn't going to sign AND wasn't going to jail.

When ordered to step out under well-established Supreme Court precedent (Pennsylvania v. Mimms), he refused lawful commands to exit, forcing the officer to physically remove him from the vehicle and place him in cuffs.

​The sense of entitlement didn't stop with the driver. Inside the SUV, three passengers, including an elderly man, sat recording while the officer bent over backward to avoid towing their vehicle. The officer offered to release the Ford Escape on the spot to anyone with a valid license so they wouldn't be stranded.

Instead, a female passenger refused to produce identification, declared they wouldn't leave until the driver was released, and dared law enforcement to tow the car with them inside. It took another responding officer arriving on scene to de-escalate their roadside standoff and retrieve the keys so they could follow the transport unit to the facility.

​The courtroom, however, doesn't entertain roadside sovereign-style theories.

​The 33-year-old driver was charged with speeding (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-181) and misdemeanor obstruction of a law enforcement officer (O.C.G.A. § 16-10-24). The judge adjudicated him guilty on both counts, handing down:

 6 months of probation

$821 in total fines and court costs ($321 for speeding, $500 for obstruction)

25 hours of mandatory community service

​A simple signature takes five seconds. Pretending you can dictate statutory procedure from behind the steering wheel costs hundreds of dollars, community labor, and a criminal record.

text:
A rare sighting in Uttarakhand’s mountains! 

Migratory Gadwall ducks have arrived at the Ason River in Kapkot, Bageshwar district, after travelling thousands of miles from Siberia and other northern regions.

According to Divisional Forest Officer Prakash Chandra, this is the first recorded sighting of the species in the Kapkot area. The birds have arrived to spend the winter here and are expected to remain around the river until March.

Gadwall ducks migrate south as temperatures drop in their northern breeding grounds. They typically return in spring, around March–April.

Their arrival has brought excitement among local residents and nature enthusiasts. The river’s calm waters and surrounding wetland habitat offer a seasonal refuge for these migratory visitors.

The Forest Department has stepped up monitoring to ensure the birds are protected and their habitat remains undisturbed. The sighting also puts Kapkot on the map as a promising destination for birdwatching and nature tourism.

text:
The Miami-based AI startup Subquadratic came out of stealth mode last month with a huge claim. It announced that it had solved a mathematical bottleneck that had been holding back large language models for almost a decade.

The details were thin, and many people were unconvinced. But Subquadratic has started to bring the receipts, sharing the results of an independent evaluation of its new tech. The results suggest that the company’s claims might be worth paying attention to.

According to Subquadratic, it has developed a new kind of LLM, called SubQ, that is faster and cheaper and uses a lot less energy than any other model on the market. The company also claims that SubQ is able to process up to 12 times as much text at once as most other models, allowing it to carry out a range of data-heavy tasks, such as analyzing hundreds of documents or entire code bases.

What’s more, Subquadratic says, SubQ does this while more or less matching the performance of the best models put out by Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic on key tasks like coding.

The problem was that the company at first provided little evidence for its claims beyond a handful of self-published test scores. And it has yet to make SubQ widely available for people to try out themselves.

So it’s no surprise that Subquadratic’s claims were met with skepticism. Dan McAteer, an artificial-intelligence engineer, captured the overall response on X: “SubQ is either the biggest breakthrough since the Transformer … or it’s AI Theranos.”

A month on, the company has published more information about its model, including the results of additional independent tests run by the third-party firm Appen.

“We expected healthy skepticism,” says Subquadratic cofounder and chief technology officer Alex Whedon. “In hindsight, releasing the third-party benchmarks alongside the initial announcement would have preempted much of the skepticism, which is why we’re taking the time to make sure any future results are fully verified before putting them out.”

Subquadratic asked Appen, which evaluates other companies’ models, to run its tests on SubQ. The results seem to back up a lot of Subquadratic’s claims. “That was really exciting to me, it validated their architecture,” says Jeanine Sinanan-Singh, Appen’s director of generative AI research.

“I was like, ‘Wow, this could be a game changer,’ because models struggle with speed and inefficiency,” she adds. “But when you have kind of shocking results, it’s really not as credible when you say it yourself.”

SubQ won’t replace existing top models across the board, but it could offer huge increases in speed at a fraction of the typical cost for certain tasks. Subquadratic insists that in the long run, though, its breakthrough could change how LLMs are built. “We hope we’re kicking off a new age of efficiency,” says Justin Dangel, the firm’s cofounder and CEO. “We don’t think anybody will be building on transformers in a few years.”

Attention!

To understand why Subquadratic’s claims are a big deal, let’s dig into how most LLMs work. The key mechanism inside an LLM is a type of neural network called a transformer, which runs a process known as dense attention. Today’s LLMs typically chain together multiple transformers. (The foundational paper of the LLM era, published by researchers at Google in 2017, was titled “Attention Is All You Need.”)

Dense attention works like this: When a transformer processes a chunk of text, it first encodes each word (or part of a word, known as a token) with a number. To capture the meaning of the full text, it then multiplies each of those numbers with every other number for that text. For example, a piece of text 10,000 words long would kick off almost 50 million individual multiplications. That’s a lot of computation and the main reason that LLMs are notorious power hogs.

“If you want to summarize The Great Gatsby, you have to look at the first word and the last word together, and then you have to look at every other combination,” says Dangel.

As the length of the text increases, the number of computations skyrockets. That’s because each additional number must be multiplied by all other previous numbers. Double the number of words, and you roughly quadruple the number of computations, a rate of increase known as a quadratic expansion.

(You can picture this yourself: Draw a circle and mark dots around its edge. Each dot is a token. Then draw lines between pairs of dots to represent the multiplication of those two tokens. A circle with five dots will have 10 lines crossing it. Make it 10 dots and you will have 45 lines, 20 dots and you will have 190 lines, and so on.)

Slashing costs

Subquadratic’s solution is to ditch dense attention, the core operation of a transformer, in favor of what’s known as sparse attention, which slashes the number of computations needed. Instead of multiplying the number assigned to each token by every other number, sparse attention selects just some of the numbers to multiply. The idea is that not all relationships between words in a piece of text matter.

“Sparse attention says not all of those relationships are important, because they’re not,” says Whedon. “If you’re reading a book, you’re not going to look at the first and second words, first and third—that’s insane.”

It’s a simple approach, and Subquadratic is not the first to try it. “Pretty much everything under the sun has been attempted,” says Will Depue, an independent AI researcher who previously worked at OpenAI. “It’s not impossible, but it’s akin to running a four-minute mile.”

Previous techniques for selecting which numbers to multiply and which to ignore have not produced a mechanism that can capture the meaning of a document as well as dense attention can.

Subquadratic claims to have cracked the problem at last. It pitches SubQ as the first sparse-attention LLM that rivals mainstream dense-attention models in performance.

“Historically, most mechanisms have used fixed patterns, like always comparing the first word to the fifth,” says Whedon. “That’s pretty limiting. Language is too sophisticated for that. And so, one of the things that makes our mechanism unique is that we dynamically select which ones are important.”

The firm won’t say exactly how SubQ chooses which words to focus on, but the selection is calculated on the fly and differs for each piece of text the model is given. “That’s kind of where the secret sauce is,” says Whedon.

Testing, testing

The upshot is that for certain tasks, SubQ may be faster and cheaper to run than most other models. Appen evaluated SubQ on a handful of standard tests. In a straight-up speed test, which sets a baseline for how fast a model can operate in theory rather than assessing what a model can actually do, Appen found that SubQ was 56 times faster than models using FlashAttention, a previous sparse-attention technique. 

On LiveCodeBench, a test that looks at how well models perform on competitive coding problems taken from real contests, SubQ scored 89.7%, putting it in the same ballpark as other top coding models. “This model continues to provide frontier-level performance in coding,” says Appen’s Sinanan-Singh.

Subquadratic’s claims about cost are harder to verify because SubQ is not yet widely available. According to Dangel, it costs $2,600 to run Anthropic’s LLM Opus 4.6 through RULER 128, a test developed by Nvidia to assess a model’s ability to retrieve information from large data sets. And SubQ? “It cost us eight dollars,” he says.

SubQ does seem to be able to handle a lot of text at once. The model has a context window (roughly akin to a working memory) up to 12 million tokens long. Most top models today have context windows one million tokens long. In a demo that Whedon ran for me, he asked SubQ to perform a task that required it to reason about information contained in 400 documents. It responded in seconds. When he gave Perplexity—a popular LLM-powered search engine—the same task, it failed to load all 400 documents. 

Appen put SubQ through the Needle-in-a-Haystack test, which, like RULER, assesses how well a model retrieves specific information buried in a large data set. In its report, Appen states that Subquadratic’s model scored 98% with context windows six million and 12 million tokens long, “sustaining near-perfect long-context retrieval at scales few models are tested at.”

Too good to be true?

Despite the high scores, benchmarks paint an incomplete picture of what a model can and cannot do. Testing under very specific conditions is not a substitute for running a model on a wide range of real tasks.

Subquadratic is offering SubQ as a model tailored to coding and to searching very large data sets. It says that tens of thousands of potential users have already signed up for early access, including more than 500 enterprise customers. But there’s a long waitlist, and the firm has given very few people access so far. Subquadratic’s response is that it is a new, small company with limited resources and cannot serve too many people at once.

Until more people get their hands on the model and try it out for themselves, some skepticism is justified. One nagging issue is that Subquadratic reused the weights (values set within a model during training that determine how it will behave) from a version of the Chinese open-source model Qwen to bootstrap SubQ, rather than training it from scratch. That’s a common approach for model makers to take, but it cuts across Subquadratic’s claim that it has fully reinvented how LLMs work.  

“They may have built something real and useful,” says Depue. “But the public evidence does not yet justify the stronger claim that they have solved the quadratic attention bottleneck.”

In the meantime, Subquadratic cofounder Whedon insists that making something different was his only option. If you want to build a competitive model, you have to have new ideas, he says: “We’re more up against it than OpenAI is.”

text:
Mythology Drop: Niiname-sai – Japan's Ancient Thanksgiving and the Sacred Harvest

Long before the modern American Thanksgiving holiday existed, Japan had its own ancient tradition of giving thanks for the harvest through a ceremony known as Niiname-sai (新嘗祭). Rooted in Shinto religious traditions, this annual celebration honored the kami, the spiritual beings and divine forces associated with nature, agriculture, and the world around humanity. 

The ceremony centered on newly harvested rice, one of the most important crops in Japanese civilization. During the ritual, the emperor traditionally offered newly harvested rice and other agricultural products to the kami before partaking in the food himself. 

One important deity associated with this tradition is Amaterasu Ōmikami, the sun goddess and one of the most significant figures in Japanese mythology. According to the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, Japan's foundational chronicles, Amaterasu is closely connected to rice cultivation, divine authority, and the origins of the imperial lineage.

The ceremony has deep roots in Japanese mythology, with the Nihon Shoki, completed in 720 CE, recording an imperial Niiname-sai observance in 673 CE. The tradition is believed to have much older origins, associated with the development of rice agriculture during Japan's Yayoi period. 

What makes this celebration especially interesting is that the relationship between food and the divine was not simply symbolic: the ritual involved offering the first fruits of the harvest to the kami and sharing in the sacred meal. 

The ceremony also has a connection to the Japanese understanding of renewal, prosperity, and the relationship between humanity and nature. Today, November 23, is celebrated as Kinrō Kansha no Hi (Labor Thanksgiving Day), a national holiday established in 1948 that recognizes labor and expresses gratitude for the contributions people make to society. Although the modern holiday is not identical to the ancient religious ceremony, it inherited its calendar date and historical connection to harvest traditions. 

Japan's ancient Thanksgiving reminds us that gratitude for food, agriculture, and the forces believed to sustain life has played an important role in civilizations across the world. Could Japan's ancient harvest ceremonies help us better understand why so many societies connected the act of giving thanks with the divine?

text:
Brad Pitt bought his elderly neighbor’s house — then reportedly let him continue living there rent-free for the rest of his life. ❤️

The unusual arrangement came to light through actress Cassandra Peterson, better known as Elvira, who once owned the Los Feliz property that became the center of Pitt’s sprawling Los Angeles estate.

Over the years, Pitt purchased several neighboring properties to expand the compound. One belonged to an elderly widower named John, who was around 90 at the time.

Rather than require John to leave his longtime home after purchasing it, Pitt reportedly made him an offer:

Stay as long as you live. No rent required.

It turned into a considerably longer commitment than anyone may have expected.

John lived to 105 years old, meaning the arrangement appears to have lasted roughly 15 years. Peterson later joked that John “just kept living forever,” adding that Pitt was probably thinking, “Well, you know, he can live there till he dies, which might be any minute now.”

But John kept going.

An important distinction often lost when the story is retold is that Pitt was already buying surrounding properties for his estate. The generous part wasn’t simply purchasing John’s house — it was allowing an elderly man to remain in his home afterward without paying rent.

Peterson also remembered Pitt as consistently kind and respectful during the years they were neighbors.

For John, a property sale therefore didn't mean losing the place he had called home.

He sold his house at around 90 — and was reportedly allowed to keep calling it home until 105. ❤️

Would you make the same arrangement if you bought a home from someone who had lived there for decades?

Sources: Cassandra Peterson’s People interview; Fox News; NZ Herald; Tribune India; La Vanguardia.

Iloilo seeks more traditional dishes for 2027 food fest
By Perla Lena

ILOILO CITY – The Iloilo provincial government is encouraging local food producers and slow food communities to showcase traditional Ilonggo dishes at the Kasadyahan sa Kabanwahanan Food Festival, one of the highlights of the 2027 Dinagyang Festival.
Provincial Tourism Officer Aulynn Yue Sin said about 10 of the 50 kiosks at this year's food festival, held along Muelle Loney behind the provincial capitol, featured slow food.

In an interview, Sin said slow food highlights heritage dishes prepared using locally sourced ingredients.

The provincial government hopes to feature more local specialties, including blue crab and other seafood from coastal municipalities, as well as food products from upland communities.

"We encourage all 12 municipalities to showcase their traditional food," Sin said in an interview on Tuesday, noting that Bingawan already has its own slow food community.
The 12 municipalities will also participate in the Kasadyahan sa Kabanwahanan festival showcase on Jan. 23.

"This time, we will make it bigger. We want to ensure that our featured foods are safe to consume, delicious, and will showcase the various municipalities of the province of Iloilo," she said.

Governor Arthur Defensor Jr. said food preparation and processing are just as important as the dishes themselves.

"We want to move towards that direction, to showcase the preparation. We want it to be world-class. Our municipalities have so much to offer, especially in terms of slow food," he said.

Defensor said the initiative also aims to introduce more Ilonggo culinary specialties to a wider audience. (PNA)

TRADITIONAL CUISINE. A participant showcases a local dish during the 2026 Kasadyahan sa Kabanwahanan Food Festival. The Iloilo provincial government is inviting slow food communities and local food producers to join the 2027 edition to promote traditional Ilonggo cuisine. text:
When whales beach themselves, it has been impossible to rescue them due to their size and weight.  I asked Chat GPT to invent a solution to this problem.  Here's what it came up with.  Project Leviathan: A Mechanical Rescue System for Stranded Whales

CONCEPTUAL MARINE ENGINEERING PROPOSAL

I believe it is possible to design a machine capable of rescuing even extraordinarily large stranded whales. The key is to stop thinking about lifting a whale and start thinking about restoring the buoyancy that the ocean normally provides.

A whale's greatest physical disadvantage on land is its enormous mass. But that same whale, once supported by water, becomes comparatively easy to move.

My proposed invention is called the Leviathan Rescue System (LRS), a portable, modular rescue apparatus that combines inflatable supports, controlled water displacement, low-friction transport, and amphibious machinery.

The objective would be to rescue whales ranging from smaller species weighing several tons to exceptionally large baleen whales weighing more than 100 tons.

This is a conceptual engineering design, not an existing, field-tested whale rescue system. Several individual technologies already exist, but integrating them into a safe, large-scale rescue apparatus would require substantial development and testing.

1. The central engineering problem

Consider a stranded humpback whale weighing approximately 30,000 kilograms, or 30 metric tons.

APPROXIMATE WEIGHT FORCE ON LAND

294,300 newtons

Equivalent to approximately 66,100 pounds-force

That is an enormous load, particularly because whales are not anatomically designed to support their own weight on a hard surface.

The principal dangers include compression of internal organs, impaired breathing and circulation, overheating, dehydration, and tissue damage. The longer the animal remains stranded, the greater the risk of serious injury.

Simply attaching cables to a whale and pulling it into the ocean could cause catastrophic damage to its skin, fins, spine, and internal organs.

My solution would distribute the whale's weight over a broad, compliant surface and use water to reduce the effective load before moving the animal.

2. The invention: A floating cradle that comes to the whale

Conceptual visual reference for the proposed rescue cradle. The exact shape and support geometry would need to be engineered and tested.Inflatable Rescue Cradle for Whale Rescue and Controlled Floating Operations | Inflatable Rescue Cradle Whale https://t.co/Sqx7nJkzqe
The system would have five major components.

A. Inflatable flotation pontoons

Two or more long, reinforced inflatable chambers would run parallel to the whale. These would be connected to a flexible support cradle. Each pontoon would contain independently controlled air compartments, allowing the system to adjust buoyancy and balance.

B. A flexible rescue cradle

A wide, padded, water-permeable membrane would support the whale's body. It would be designed to avoid concentrated pressure on the pectoral fins, tail, head, and other vulnerable anatomy. Pressure sensors would identify potentially dangerous loading.

C. A portable water-delivery system

High-volume pumps would deliver filtered seawater to temporary flexible containment barriers around the whale. The goal would be to create enough water depth to reduce ground pressure and permit controlled flotation. The blowhole must remain unobstructed.

D. An amphibious transport platform

A low-profile, remotely operated tracked machine would move on sand and shallow seabeds. Rather than pulling the whale directly, it would reposition the cradle through distributed attachment points and load-limited winches.

E. Computer-controlled load management

Sensors would monitor cradle tension, pressure distribution, tilt, water depth, and movement. The system would automatically halt if any measurement exceeded a veterinarian-approved limit.

3. How a rescue would work

Veterinary assessment and stabilizationAuthorized marine mammal veterinarians would first determine whether the whale is a suitable candidate for refloating. The rescue system would not be activated merely because the animal is alive.

Position the cradleA rescue team would deploy the flotation chambers alongside the whale. A segmented support membrane would be introduced beneath the body using carefully engineered, low-force methods. This is one of the hardest unresolved parts of the invention: inserting support beneath a massive whale without injuring it or destabilizing the surrounding sand.

Introduce water and establish buoyancyIf the terrain permits, temporary barriers would retain pumped seawater around the whale. As water depth increases, the whale's effective weight on the ground would decrease. The pontoons would be inflated gradually, providing supplementary support.

Move toward deeper waterOnce the whale is sufficiently buoyant and supported, the amphibious transport system would guide the cradle slowly toward the ocean. Movement would be stopped immediately if excessive pressure, twisting, or animal distress were detected.

Release and monitorIn suitable water depth, the cradle would open and the flotation chambers would move away without entangling the whale. Veterinarians would evaluate its ability to breathe, maintain orientation, and swim before authorizing release.
4. Could buoyancy really lift such a massive animal?

Yes, in principle. Archimedes' principle gives us a starting point:
\[ F_b=\rho gV \]

Where \(F_b\) is buoyant force, \(\rho\) is seawater density, \(g\) is gravitational acceleration, and \(V\) is the volume of displaced water.
At a seawater density of approximately 1,025 kilograms per cubic meter, each cubic meter of submerged air-filled flotation volume provides roughly 1.025 metric tons of gross buoyant support, before subtracting the flotation structure's own weight.

Here's a simplified engineering calculator for exploring flotation requirements.
Assumes fully submerged air chambers in seawater, with no structural weight, losses, or safety factor. It does not predict actual whale support loads.Leviathan buoyancy calculator
Illustrative calculation only, not a safe lifting prescription.Whale mass30 metric tonsSupplemental support target20%Target buoyant support6.0 tons
Ideal submerged air volume5.9 m³

For example, a 30-ton whale needing 20% supplemental support would require approximately 5.9 cubic meters of fully submerged air volume, under these idealized assumptions.

The important distinction is that the cradle would not necessarily have to lift all 30 tons. If the whale is already partially submerged, the surrounding seawater supplies much of the buoyancy.

That makes the system potentially more practical than a conventional crane.

5. The biggest engineering challenges

There are several serious obstacles that would have to be solved before the invention could be used on a living whale.

Challenge

Proposed engineering approach

Whale's fragile anatomy

Distributed, compliant support with pressure monitoring

Inserting a cradle underneath

Segmented membrane deployment, tested on anatomical models

Unstable sand

Wide load-spreading pads and seabed assessment

Waves and currents

Weather limits, emergency release, stabilized pontoons

Maintaining breathing

Open blowhole clearance and veterinary monitoring

Very large whale mass

Modular buoyancy units and redundant load paths

Rapid deployment

Containerized equipment stationed at strategic coastal locations

One particularly important issue is water containment. Pumping seawater into an enclosure on a porous beach may accomplish very little if it immediately drains through the sand. A realistic design might require a flexible impermeable basin, and installing that basin without harming the whale is another substantial challenge.

There is also a biological limitation: restoring buoyancy does not necessarily reverse organ damage or treat the illness that caused the stranding.
6. What makes this different from existing rescue equipment?
Inflatable rescue pontoons are already used for smaller stranded cetaceans. But according to NOAA Fisheries, there is currently no safe, generally applicable way to refloat most large whale species without risking further injury. NOAA also warns that towing a whale by its tail can cause devastating injuries.
NOAA Fisheries+2
The innovation I would pursue is not simply a bigger inflatable pontoon.
It is the integration of:
A modular cradle that can accommodate different whale sizes.
Controlled local flooding to restore natural buoyancy.
Automated pressure and load management.
Remote-controlled, low-force transport.
A quick-release mechanism that does not require rescuers to enter dangerous positions near the animal.
Existing rescue practices would be the foundation, but the combination could offer a new approach worth investigating.
7. How I would develop the prototype
Submit the system to marine mammal veterinarians, NOAA, and authorized rescue organizations for independent safety evaluation. Any live-animal application would require appropriate authorization and ethical review.Phase 1Small-scale laboratory testingBuild a 1:10 scale system and test it with a weighted, anatomically representative model in a sand-and-water tank.Phase 2Full-size mechanical testingTest the cradle with a compliant, instrumented dummy representing a small whale, measuring pressure, movement, and flotation stability.Phase 3Coastal field trialsConduct unmanned trials on beaches with different slopes, sediment types, tides, and surf conditions.Phase 4Specialist evaluation
8. A second invention that might be even more practical
There is another possibility I find especially promising: a portable tidal rescue lagoon.
Instead of trying to move the whale immediately, the rescue team would construct a temporary water-retaining enclosure around it, allowing rising seawater or pumped seawater to surround the animal.
Once buoyancy is restored, a floating cradle could guide the whale toward a controlled opening facing deeper water.
This could reduce the need for a large land-based vehicle. It would be most suitable for certain gently sloping beaches, although seepage, wave loads, installation time, and the animal's condition would remain major obstacles.

The two systems could ultimately complement each other: the lagoon restores buoyancy, and the cradle provides controlled support and movement.

My proposed next step

I would focus initial research on the Leviathan floating cradle combined with a portable tidal lagoon, rather than attempting to build a giant whale-lifting machine.

The governing principle would be:

Don't lift the whale out of its environment. Recreate enough of its environment to let buoyancy do the work.

NOAA's published guidance makes clear that large-whale refloating remains exceptionally difficult and that rescue decisions must be made by trained, authorized professionals.

NOAA Fisheries+1

This invention would be an attempt to expand their options, not replace their judgment.

I think the most interesting next engineering exercise would be to design a full-scale rescue apparatus for a 30-ton humpback whale, complete with approximate dimensions, flotation requirements, pumps, materials, and deployment mechanics. That would help us determine whether Project Leviathan is merely theoretically possible or could become a practical rescue technology.
