THE CELESTE TRAIL ✨
\## The Art of Becoming: A Father's Promise, A Daughter's Destiny, and a New Vision for the Future\
\### A Personal Manifesto on Femininity, Self-Worth, Fatherhood, Freedom, and the Rebirth of a Generation\ https://t.co/7SXf8OQv4e 
\
\*#ParadizeEnterprize • #ParadizeEmagazine Special Edition\* 💙\ #CelestrailApp 
\
There comes a moment in a man's life when he begins to understand that his greatest accomplishments may not be measured by the wealth he accumulates, the businesses he builds, the influence he gains, or even the victories he celebrates.\
\
Sometimes, the greatest measure of a man's life is found in the people he leaves stronger than he found them.\
\
And sometimes, the greatest empire a man can build is not one made of gold, property, technology, or financial instruments, but one built through the lives he has helped protect, the minds he has helped awaken, and the dreams he has helped bring into existence.\
\
I have spent considerable time thinking about the future of my daughters, my sons, and the young women growing up in a world that is changing faster than any previous generation could have imagined.\
\
I am proud of all three of my daughters, my two sons, and my half-sons. Each has a different personality, a different journey, and a different perspective on life. And each has reminded me that children do not simply need someone to tell them what the world is like. They need someone willing to help them understand it.\
\
Two of my girls have experienced the reality of war much closer to home than most Americans could ever imagine. Watching young people grow up with uncertainty, instability, and circumstances beyond their control has made me reflect deeply on what we sometimes take for granted.\
\
In America, we often see privilege expressed through appearance, popularity, social influence, and even the cultural battles surrounding feminism and gender expectations. Some of these conversations have become increasingly polarized.\
\
But when I look toward Russia, Ukraine, and other parts of the world where economic hardship and instability are part of everyday existence, I see another reality.\
\
The privileges we assume exist do not necessarily translate into security, opportunity, or a better future.\
\
A beautiful face does not guarantee protection. Popularity does not guarantee happiness. Attention does not guarantee love. And being admired by thousands of people does not necessarily mean having one person who genuinely cares whether you are okay.\
\
That distinction matters more than many people realize.\
\
\## 🌹 The invisible price of growing up too quickly\
\
Over the years, I have encountered heartbreaking stories involving young Ukrainian women, particularly those entering the modeling world under difficult economic circumstances.\
\
Some are raised in environments where opportunities are limited and financial security is almost nonexistent. When someone suddenly offers attention, money, admiration, or the promise of a glamorous future, it can become difficult to distinguish a genuine opportunity from exploitation.\
\
What initially appears innocent can gradually become something entirely different.\
\
Sometimes, young women are conditioned to believe that certain decisions are simply part of becoming successful, attractive, independent, or mature.\
\
But who explains the consequences?\
\
Who tells them about the emotional toll of exploitation, the difficulty of rebuilding self-esteem, or the psychological consequences of being treated as an object rather than a human being?\
\
Who reminds them that they do not have to sacrifice their dignity to prove their worth?\
\
I have worked with abused children and trauma-based cases across different age groups. As a Harvard researcher and certified psychiatric youth care specialist, my experiences have shaped the way I look at these circumstances.\
\
What I have repeatedly observed in vulnerable environments is the relationship between economic deprivation, instability, limited opportunities, and the absence of a meaningful sense of future.\
\
When someone cannot envision a better tomorrow, the temporary rewards of today can become disproportionately attractive.\
\
And that is where I believe we need to intervene.\
\
Not by condemning young women.\
\
Not by humiliating them.\
\
Not by telling them that their past determines their future.\
\
But by giving them something better to pursue.\
\
Because I have always believed that prevention is more powerful than rehabilitation, and that preserving someone's confidence and sense of identity is far better than trying to rebuild them after the world has taken those things away.\
\
Over the last twelve-plus years, I have personally and financially helped numerous families and young girls.\
\
If you have watched my \*Saving Children: New Hope Project\* documentary online, you have seen some of the individuals I personally helped.\
\
I understood something very early: if an organization was not going to step forward, sometimes someone had to do it personally.\
\
Sometimes that someone had to be me.\
\
And I have never forgotten why.\
\
\## 💙 A conversation with my daughters\
\
When I look at my young CEO, Katrina Logunova, and my daughters, I find myself thinking about the conversations I wish every young woman could have with someone who genuinely wants to see her succeed.\
\
I would tell them:\
\
Honey, you are entering a world where everything moves quickly.\
\
You can become popular overnight. You can build an audience in a week. You can potentially earn more money through technology in a few months than someone else might earn through years of traditional employment.\
\
But there is something I want you to understand.\
\
Not everything that makes money creates value in your life.\
\
Not everything that attracts attention deserves your attention.\
\
And not every opportunity that looks glamorous is an opportunity worth accepting.\
\
There is a difference between being admired and being appreciated.\
\
There is a difference between being desired and being loved.\
\
There is a difference between having an audience and having people who genuinely care about your future.\
\
I want you to understand that your beauty is not your entire identity. Your intelligence, imagination, compassion, creativity, discipline, and ambitions are equally important.\
\
You should never feel that you must surrender part of yourself simply because someone has convinced you that doing so is the fastest route to success.\
\
The modeling industry, entertainment industry, and social media economy offer tremendous opportunities. I recognize that. I also recognize that there are financial realities involved, and that young people are increasingly exposed to opportunities that previous generations never had.\
\
But I want my girls to understand the difference between building a career and allowing a career to consume their identity.\
\
I want them to have choices.\
\
Real choices.\
\
Choices made through knowledge, confidence, and independence rather than desperation, manipulation, or fear of being left behind.\
\
\## 🛡️ The value of a man who understands responsibility\
\
I have often thought about what it means to be a father and, more broadly, what it means to be a man.\
\
I want my daughters to see a man who understands that strength is not measured by how many women he can attract, how much attention he receives, or how many indulgences he can afford.\
\
I want them to see a man who understands restraint.\
\
A man who does not need strip clubs, pornography, drugs, or endless distractions to feel fulfilled.\
\
I may have a sip of wine a few times a year or a beer once in a rare blue moon, but I have found that refraining from many of the habits that once surrounded modern indulgence has helped me become a better man.\
\
One of the greatest personal challenges I have worked on is overcoming sexual desires and even lust.\
\
For a man, I believe self-mastery is crucial.\
\
I want to evolve into my greatest sacred masculine self.\
\
Not because I believe a man should be without emotion, affection, or desire, but because I believe that a man who cannot govern himself will eventually struggle to govern anything else in his life.\
\
I feel more powerful than ever today.\
\
I have little girls and sons whom I want to protect. I have responsibilities, ambitions, and a vision that extends beyond myself.\
\
I have come to believe that constantly surrendering one's energy to temporary gratification can leave a person emotionally and mentally depleted.\
\
I want Katrina to look at me and say:\
\
"This is what a real man looks like. This is my Papa. I feel safe around him. I know he will protect me, and I love learning new things from him."\
\
That is the kind of influence I want to have.\
\
Not fear.\
\
Not control.\
\
Not intimidation.\
\
But trust, knowledge, protection, and the confidence that someone genuinely believes in her potential.\
\
I want my daughters to understand that a healthy relationship is not a prison. It is not a transaction. It is not a competition over who has more power.\
\
It is a partnership where two people can grow without destroying one another.\
\
I have lived enough of life to understand that loyalty, communication, patience, tolerance, and acceptance are not signs of weakness.\
\
They are foundations.\
\
And sometimes the most exciting thing two people can experience is discovering that they no longer need to run from one another to feel alive.\
\
\## 👑 Katrina, the Catherine legacy\
\
There is another part of this story that has always meant something to me.\
\
My eldest daughter, Katrina, carries a name with a historical connection that I have always found fascinating.\
\
I originally wanted a name with the letter E in it, but I never particularly liked Erika.\
\
I considered Saint Catherine because of the historical and symbolic associations I saw in that name, including its connection to the ancient feminine archetypes I had been studying.\
\
Then I discovered Ekaterina, the Russian form of Catherine.\
\
And from there came Katyusha.\
\
Katrina.\
\
Katya.\
\
Sometimes I even call her Katatrina.\
\
I named her with Catherine the Great in mind, and she became my #BlackSunEmpress1111.\
\
Catherine II, known as Catherine the Great, ruled Russia from 1762 to 1796. Her reign became associated with territorial expansion, cultural development, education, and the transformation of Russia into a major European power.\
\
She was born Sophie, a German princess, yet she learned the Russian language, embraced Russian Orthodoxy, and ultimately rose to become one of the most influential women in European history.\
\
What fascinates me is not simply the crown or the imperial title.\
\
It is the transformation.\
\
A young woman entered an unfamiliar world, learned its language, understood its political environment, developed her own influence, and ultimately shaped history.\
\
That is a powerful historical story.\
\
Of course, history is complicated, and Catherine's reign was not without controversy. But her ambition, political intelligence, and historical influence are undeniable.\
\
When I think about Katrina, I think about potential.\
\
I think about intelligence, leadership, adaptability, and the ability to develop an identity that extends beyond appearance.\
\
I like calling her Katya, especially when someone knows her well enough to use it. It has a playful sound, almost like ketchup. 👍 👌 😏\
\
Or simply Katrina.\
\
But whatever name she answers to, I want her to understand that she does not have to become a historical figure to become extraordinary.\
\
She only needs to become the best version of herself.\
\
\## 🚀 The birth of a different kind of social media\
\
And this brings me to the larger purpose of everything I have been thinking about.\
\
I do not want this to remain a conversation between a father and his daughters.\
\
I want to turn the underlying philosophy into something that can reach people far beyond my own family.\
\
I envision a social media application that gives children, young people, aspiring models, and women a healthier environment in which to develop their creativity, discover their ambitions, and build meaningful opportunities.\
\
An ecosystem where a young model can work on her craft, develop her professional portfolio, learn about business, build confidence, and receive recognition for genuine achievements.\
\
An environment where success is not measured exclusively by how much attention someone can attract through increasingly provocative content.\
\
I want to create an incentive structure that rewards creativity, discipline, education, entrepreneurship, personal development, and professional excellence.\
\
And I want to do it without making the project a religious endeavor.\
\
People come from different backgrounds, cultures, philosophies, and beliefs. They should be able to participate without having to surrender their individuality.\
\
The purpose is to create something constructive.\
\
Something that gives young people a reason to aspire toward something greater.\
\
Technology has given us the ability to influence millions of people, but the question is whether we are using that ability to make people better or simply to keep them entertained.\
\
We have created systems that can capture attention in seconds, but how many systems are genuinely designed to develop character over years?\
\
We understand how to generate engagement.\
\
We understand how to monetize attention.\
\
We understand how to make people return repeatedly for another dopamine hit.\
\
But I want to explore something different.\
\
What happens when we make personal development rewarding?\
\
What happens when ambition becomes exciting?\
\
What happens when young women are encouraged to build businesses, develop professional skills, learn financial independence, pursue modeling, explore the arts, and create lasting relationships?\
\
What happens when we give people something meaningful to work toward?\
\
That is the direction I want to explore.\
\
I want to replace the constant pursuit of temporary validation with the satisfaction of genuine accomplishment.\
\
I want to create a culture where a young woman can be beautiful without being defined by her appearance, ambitious without being exploited, independent without being isolated, and successful without having to sacrifice her personal values.\
\
And I want young men to benefit from that same philosophy.\
\
Because this is not about creating a better world for one gender at the expense of another.\
\
It is about creating a better environment for everyone.\
\
\## 🧠 The psychology of the choices we make\
\
I have watched too many amazingly beautiful women I grew up with struggle over the years.\
\
Some became heavily involved with drugs. Others experienced serious difficulties with their health, self-esteem, relationships, or personal direction.\
\
Some eventually seemed to lose interest in themselves and in the futures they once imagined.\
\
I do not share these observations to judge anyone.\
\
Life can be extraordinarily difficult, and people often carry invisible burdens that outsiders will never fully understand.\
\
But I have learned that repeated behaviors can gradually shape the way we see ourselves.\
\
When our entire sense of worth becomes dependent on external approval, we become vulnerable to the people and systems that know how to manipulate that need.\
\
When temporary gratification becomes the primary objective, long-term fulfillment can become increasingly difficult to recognize.\
\
And when we repeatedly convince ourselves that tomorrow will somehow repair the consequences of today, we can lose years of our lives without realizing it.\
\
This is why I believe discipline and foresight are so important.\
\
Not because people should never make mistakes.\
\
Not because everyone must follow the same path.\
\
But because freedom becomes much more meaningful when we understand the consequences of our choices.\
\
You only live once.\
\
That phrase is often used to justify doing whatever feels good in the moment.\
\
But I would suggest looking at it differently.\
\
You only live once.\
\
So why not make something extraordinary out of the life you have been given?\
\
Why not build something that will still matter ten, twenty, or fifty years from now?\
\
Why not create memories that make you smile rather than memories you spend the rest of your life trying to forget?\
\
Why not discover what you are capable of before allowing someone else to determine your value?\
\
\## 🌌 The Celeste Trail: A journey toward something greater\
\
This is where the Celeste Trail enters the picture.\
\
Celeste represents divine travel, adventure, and the pursuit of something greater.\
\
For me, it symbolizes the journey beyond the limitations people sometimes place upon themselves.\
\
It is not about perfection.\
\
It is about evolution.\
\
It is about discovering that there are many ways to experience life without allowing the world to convince us that self-destruction is a prerequisite for freedom.\
\
I want my girls to travel.\
\
I want to take them on road trips, introduce them to new environments, and allow them to experience the world beyond the boundaries of what they already know.\
\
I want to take Katrina to modeling opportunities with major companies in Miami, Florida, and other major entertainment and fashion markets, including Miami, California, and Los Angeles and Hollywood.\
\
I want to teach her how the American modeling and entertainment industries operate.\
\
I want to share what I know.\
\
I want her to meet people, develop professional relationships, understand business, and discover opportunities that she might never have encountered otherwise.\
\
And I want to do these things with her sisters as well.\
\
I want my girls to have experiences.\
\
I want them to laugh, explore, make memories, discover their talents, and develop their own identities.\
\
I do not expect them to become copies of me.\
\
I do not expect them to agree with everything I believe.\
\
And I do not believe that love should require someone to surrender her individuality.\
\
What I want is for them to know that they have a father who believes in their potential and wants to give them opportunities to discover it.\
\
I also recognize that they must have their own voices, boundaries, and decisions.\
\
A father's responsibility is not to write every chapter of his daughters' lives.\
\
It is to help them develop the wisdom and confidence to write those chapters themselves.\
\
That is a distinction I have come to appreciate.\
\
\## 💕 To my Isabella, Katrina, and Viola\
\
My girls, if you ever read this, I want you to understand something.\
\
I know I can be difficult.\
\
I know I can be strict.\
\
I know that sometimes my expectations may seem overwhelming, and that my approach may not always be easy to understand.\
\
But beneath all the ambition, the projects, the plans, and the expectations is something very simple.\
\
I want you to have a future.\
\
I want you to have opportunities.\
\
I want you to be able to look back at your childhood and remember that you were encouraged to dream, explore, learn, and become something wonderful.\
\
I want Isabella to know how much I believe in her.\
\
I want Katrina to understand that her position as CEO is not simply a title. It represents an opportunity to learn leadership, responsibility, decision-making, and the importance of building something that can outlast any individual personality.\
\
And I want Viola to know that she has an important place in this vision, too.\
\
You are all different.\
\
You each have something that cannot be duplicated.\
\
My Little Squirt.\
\
My Monster Princess Sour Puss.\
\
My Pit Bull Princess. 👸\
\
Those names may make you laugh, but they represent the affection and memories that make our family what it is.\
\
Katrina, thank you for helping me this past year.\
\

BOOM 🚨 Tesla is taking its power electronics expertise beyond Megapack with Powercore, a new 7.4 MW system that combines a solid-state transformer, inverter, and circuit breaker into a single enclosure 🔥

The announcement also sheds light on an important part of Tesla's energy strategy that had remained largely unexplained since last year.

🔋 Powercore fills a missing piece of Tesla's Megablock strategy.

Back in September 2025, Tesla introduced Megapack 3 and Megablock, initially showing a system that combined four Megapack 3 units with a transformer and switchgear.

Tesla had already announced plans to manufacture its own transformers, but shared very little about the technology behind them.

Powercore now gives us a much clearer picture of what Tesla has been working toward.

In a conventional Megapack installation, electricity stored as direct current (DC) passes through an inverter, which converts it into 480V alternating current (AC). A separate transformer then steps that voltage up to the medium-voltage level needed by the grid.

Powercore combines those functions into a single, electronically controlled system, converting battery DC directly into medium-voltage AC without a separate low-voltage AC stage.

According to Tesla, the previous architecture had roughly twice the conversion losses.

That means more of the energy stored in Megapack can actually reach the grid, without adding more batteries.

Powercore can also connect directly to Megapack through a shared DC bus. The closely integrated equipment can arrive preassembled, reducing on-site wiring, simplifying installation, and helping projects come online faster.

With Powerhub managing the entire site, Tesla can bring more of the hardware, software, monitoring, and servicing under one roof instead of relying on multiple equipment suppliers.

⚙️ The technology behind Powercore is impressive.

Here are some of its standout specifications:

⚡ 7.4 MW of continuous power and 9 MVA at 34.5 kV AC, with up to 10 MVA of peak grid-forming capability. MW measures real power, while MVA accounts for total AC power, including the reactive component.

⚡ 98.86% peak conversion efficiency, supporting DC voltages from 800V to 2,000V and AC voltages from 10kV to 34.5kV.

⚡ 100-microsecond fault interruption, thanks to an integrated solid-state circuit breaker that Tesla says can respond up to 1,000 times faster than conventional breakers.

⚡ System availability guarantees of 99.9% or higher, field-serviceable modules, and warranty options of up to 25 years.

⚡ No flammable transformer oil, with an operating temperature range of −40°F to 131°F (−40°C to 55°C).

Powercore also supports grid-forming operation, which means it can actively help regulate voltage and frequency rather than simply transforming electricity from one voltage to another.

That capability becomes increasingly valuable as power grids accommodate more renewable energy, large battery installations, and rapidly changing electrical loads.

🖥️ AI data centers open up a major new opportunity for Powercore.

As AI computing systems grow more powerful, delivering electricity to them is becoming an engineering challenge of its own.

Traditional data centers rely on multiple conversion stages between their medium-voltage grid connections and the equipment powering their servers.

Next-generation AI infrastructure is moving toward 800V DC power distribution, and Powercore is designed to convert medium-voltage AC directly into 800V DC.

Removing intermediate conversion stages means fewer components, lower electrical losses, and a simpler power distribution system.

At the scale of a massive AI campus, even small improvements in efficiency can free up meaningful amounts of electricity for computing.

Tesla is already working with NVIDIA on next-generation 800V DC power systems.

Megapack 2 XL is listed under NVIDIA's DSX Ready program, while Tesla is separately pursuing Powercore's integration with this emerging infrastructure.

Tesla also has another advantage that makes this opportunity particularly interesting: Megapack.

The company says it already has 10 GWh of Megapack storage operating at data centers.

Connecting Megapack directly to Powercore's DC bus allows batteries to provide backup power, absorb sudden swings in computing demand, and help stabilize the local grid.

Instead of supplying these capabilities separately, Tesla can combine power conversion, energy storage, and grid management into a more integrated solution for AI campuses.

☀️ Solar developers face many of the same challenges.

Powercore can also serve as a central inverter for utility-scale solar farms, supporting today's 1,500V DC arrays and emerging 2,000V systems.

By combining the inverter, transformer, and circuit breaker into one platform, it reduces the amount of separate electrical equipment needed to connect a solar project to the grid.

That matters because conventional transformers have become a major supply-chain bottleneck, with procurement lead times sometimes stretching into years.

For solar developers, fewer separate components can mean simpler installations, less complicated maintenance, and fewer dependencies on equipment that can hold up an entire project.

Tesla also enters this market with considerable scale.

The company reports more than 100 GWh of energy storage operating across 2,000 projects in 68 countries, along with 140 GWh of annual Megapack manufacturing capacity.

It also has more than 900 field technicians supporting its global energy operations.

Powercore gives Tesla another product to offer its existing customers while expanding its role in the electrical infrastructure surrounding those projects.

🤝 Powercore also has an interesting connection to former Tesla executive Drew Baglino.

Baglino, who led Tesla's powertrain and energy engineering organization before leaving in April 2024, went on to found Heron Power, a startup focused on modernizing electrical infrastructure.

Its flagship product, Heron Link, takes a similar approach to power conversion using modular, solid-state electronics.

For large solar and battery storage projects, Heron Link is rated at 5 MW with 98.6% DC-to-medium-voltage conversion efficiency.

Tesla's Powercore has a higher continuous power rating of 7.4 MW and quotes 98.86% peak efficiency.

The efficiency numbers aren't directly comparable, however. Tesla explicitly reports a peak figure, while Heron doesn't identify its 98.6% measurement as peak efficiency.

Both companies are also targeting AI data centers.

Heron offers a 4.2 MW configuration that converts medium-voltage AC directly into 800V DC, paired with its SuperBBU battery system for backup and power stabilization.

Their approaches to the market are different.

Heron is building a modular platform designed to work with equipment from multiple manufacturers, giving customers flexibility in how they assemble their power systems.

Tesla, meanwhile, can integrate Powercore directly with Megapack, Powerhub, and its existing manufacturing and service operations.

Heron has already made meaningful commercial progress.

Vantage has reserved more than 1 GW of manufacturing capacity for data center applications, while Intersect has reserved another 1.5 GW for solar projects.

These are manufacturing capacity commitments rather than completed deployments, but they demonstrate substantial customer interest.

Heron is also targeting a pilot project with RWE in April 2027, followed by mass production at its California factory later that year.

Tesla hasn't announced Powercore pricing or named its first customers. Its first U.S.-manufactured systems are expected to begin operating in 2027.

When the comparison with Heron came up on X, Elon Musk responded:

"No, this has been planned for 3+ years."

That puts Tesla's planning in 2023 or earlier, before Baglino left the company, although Elon didn't specify when engineering development actually began.

⚡ Elon's earlier prediction about AI infrastructure makes Powercore even more interesting.

On April 2, 2025, Elon wrote that the constraint on AI scaling would move "from chips to voltage transformers to electricity generation."

His point is becoming increasingly relevant as technology companies race to build enormous AI computing facilities.

A company can spend billions of dollars on GPUs, servers, and data center buildings, but none of that computing capacity can go online until sufficient electricity is available and the electrical infrastructure is ready to deliver it.

Even with power secured, a shortage of transformers or other essential distribution equipment can delay an entire project.

And as AI campuses grow, the electrical systems supporting them must also handle increasingly demanding and rapidly changing power loads.

Powercore addresses an important part of that challenge by bringing medium-voltage conversion, fast electrical protection, and active grid controls together in one system.

It won't generate additional electricity or eliminate every obstacle to connecting a project to the grid. But it gives Tesla a way to manufacture more of the critical equipment that determines how efficiently and quickly available power can reach its destination.

Tesla has spent years scaling battery production and energy storage through Megapack. With Powercore, it's extending that experience into another essential part of the electrical infrastructure.

The AI industry is racing to build more powerful computers, but those computers are only useful when there's enough power to run them.

Tesla is positioning itself to supply more of the infrastructure that makes that possible. https://t.co/7PzKJgmiVE

🟢 NVIDIA PASSED ITS FIRST EARNINGS TEST WITHOUT JENSEN HUANG!

After weeks of selling pressure, leadership uncertainty, and concerns about whether @nvidia could maintain its growth momentum, the company has finally delivered its first earnings report since @JensenHuang stepped down as CEO.

And the numbers came in stronger than Wall Street expected.

In my previous post, I discussed how the company had lost about 32% of its market value from its October high, and why this earnings report would test whether the recent decline had already priced in much of the bad news.

Well, Nvidia has now answered some of those questions, particularly when it comes to revenue growth and forward guidance.

📊 NVIDIA Q3 EARNINGS BY THE NUMBERS

1️⃣ Revenue: $115.8 Billion

Expected: ~$109B

Up 20% QoQ and 103% YoY

Result: 🟢 BEAT

2️⃣ Adjusted EPS: $2.68

Expected: ~$2.47

Result: 🟢 BEAT

3️⃣ Gross Margin: 74.9%

Previous guidance: 74%

Result: 🟢 ABOVE GUIDANCE

4️⃣ Q4 Revenue Guidance: $130 Billion

Expected: ~$125.3B

Result: 🟢 ABOVE EXPECTATIONS

Following the announcement, $NVDA initially gained as much as 4.8% in after-hours trading, reflecting a positive reaction to the results.

However, the $130 billion Q4 revenue guidance deserves more attention, because this was one of the biggest concerns heading into earnings.

Investors were worried that the leadership transition could lead Nvidia to adopt a more conservative outlook, but interim CEO Colette Kress instead raised the company's expected revenue growth for fiscal 2028 from approximately 70% to 75%.

That is a significant show of confidence in demand for AI computing, especially as investors become more selective about AI valuations.

📈 WHAT COMES NEXT FOR THE COMPANY?

Nvidia has shown its underlying business remains strong despite the uncertainty around its leadership.

However, a strong earnings report does not automatically mean the stock will recover everything it lost over the past month.

The next question is whether buyers can sustain the initial momentum once regular trading resumes, particularly after such a substantial correction.

I would also keep an eye on gross margins going forward, as Nvidia expects them to moderate toward 71%-72% in Q4.

For those who voted 🟢 in the previous earnings poll, the financial results certainly support that outcome.

But the market still has another test ahead, which is that can Nvidia hold its post-earnings gains?

If any group of people came out tomorrow and espoused verbatim the ideology of Islam they would be condemned as sadists, pedophiles, slavers, and Nazi's

..and every one of you knows it.
#IslamIsEvil 

**

Voltaire’s letter to Frederick II, Rotterdam, December 1740):

Sire, I now resemble the pilgrims of Mecca who, after leaving that city, continually turn their eyes back toward it; I turn mine toward your court. My heart, filled with the kindnesses of Your Majesty, knows no grief but that of being unable to live near you. I take the liberty of sending you a fresh copy of this tragedy of Mahomet, the first sketches of which you were good enough to see some time ago. It is a tribute I pay to the lover of the arts, the enlightened judge, and above all to the philosopher, far more than to the sovereign.

Your Majesty knows what spirit animated me in composing this work: the love of mankind and the horror of fanaticism—two virtues made to stand always beside your throne—guided my pen. I have always thought that tragedy ought not to be a mere spectacle that moves the heart without correcting it. What do the passions and misfortunes of a hero of antiquity matter to mankind if they do not serve to instruct us? It is admitted that the comedy of Tartuffe, that masterpiece which no nation has equaled, has done much good to men by showing hypocrisy in all its ugliness; can we not try, in a tragedy, to attack that species of imposture which puts into play at once the hypocrisy of some and the fury of others? Can we not go back to those ancient scoundrels, the illustrious founders of superstition and fanaticism, who were the first to take the knife from the altar in order to make victims of those who refused to be their disciples?

Those who say that the times of such crimes are past; that we shall never again see Barcochebas, Mahomets, John of Leydens, etc.; that the flames of the wars of religion are extinguished, do, it seems to me, too much honor to human nature. The same poison still exists, though less fully developed; this plague, which seems smothered, from time to time produces germs capable of infecting the earth. Have we not seen in our own days the prophets of the Cévennes killing, in the name of God, those of their sect who were not submissive enough?

The action I have painted is atrocious; and I do not know whether horror has ever gone further on any stage. It is a young man born with virtue who, seduced by his fanaticism, assassinates an old man who loves him, and who, in the idea of serving God, becomes guilty, without knowing it, of a parricide; it is an impostor who orders this murder and who promises the assassin an incest as a reward. I admit that this is putting horror on the stage; and Your Majesty is well persuaded that tragedy must not consist solely of a declaration of love, a jealousy, and a marriage.

Our own historians teach us of actions more atrocious than the one I have invented. Séide at least does not know that the man he assassinates is his father, and when he has struck the blow he feels a repentance as great as his crime. But Mézerai reports that at Melun a father killed his son with his own hand for the sake of religion, and felt no repentance. Everyone knows the story of the two brothers Diaz, one of whom was at Rome and the other in Germany at the beginning of the troubles stirred up by Luther. Barthélemy Diaz, learning at Rome that his brother was adopting the opinions of Luther at Frankfurt, leaves Rome with the intention of assassinating him, arrives, and assassinates him. I have read in Herrera, a Spanish author, that “Barthélemy Diaz risked much by this action; but nothing shakes a man of honor when probity leads him.” Herrera, in a religion altogether holy and altogether hostile to cruelty, in a religion that teaches suffering rather than vengeance, was therefore persuaded that probity can lead to assassination and parricide; and shall we not rise up on all sides against these infernal maxims?

It is these maxims that put the dagger into the hand of the monster who deprived France of Henri the Great; this is what placed the portrait of Jacques Clément on the altar and his name among the blessed; this is what cost the life of William, Prince of Orange, founder of the liberty and greatness of the Dutch. First Salcède wounded him in the forehead with a pistol shot; and Strada recounts that “Salcède (these are his own words) dared not undertake this action until he had purified his soul by confession at the feet of a Dominican and strengthened it by the celestial bread.” Herrera says something even more insane and atrocious: “Standing firm with the example of our Savior Jesus Christ and of his saints.” Balthazar Gérard, who finally took the life of that great man, did the same as Salcède.

I observe that all those who committed such crimes in good faith were young men like Séide. Balthazar Gérard was about twenty. Four Spaniards who had sworn with him to kill the prince were of the same age. The monster who killed Henri III was only twenty-four. Poltrot, who assassinated the great Duke of Guise, was twenty-five; that is the age of seduction and fury. I was almost a witness, in England, of what the force of fanaticism can do upon a young and weak imagination. A child of sixteen, named Shepherd, undertook to assassinate King George I, your maternal ancestor. What was the cause that drove him to this frenzy? It was solely that Shepherd was not of the same religion as the king. Pity was taken on his youth; his pardon was offered; he was long solicited to repent; he persisted always in saying that it was better to obey God than men, and that if he were free the first use he would make of his liberty would be to kill his prince. Thus one was obliged to send him to execution, like a monster one despaired of taming.

I dare say that whoever has lived a little among men has sometimes been able to see how easily one is ready to sacrifice nature to superstition. How many fathers have detested and disinherited their children! how many brothers have pursued their brothers by this fatal principle! I have seen examples of it in more than one family.

If superstition does not always signal itself by these excesses that are counted in the history of crimes, it does in society all the innumerable little daily evils that it can do. It disunites friends; it divides relatives; it persecutes the sage, who is only a man of good will, by the hand of the fool who is an enthusiast; it does not always give hemlock to Socrates, but it banishes Descartes from a city that ought to have been the asylum of liberty; it gives to Jurieu, who played the prophet, enough credit to reduce to poverty the learned and philosophical Bayle; it banishes, it tears from a flourishing youth that runs to his lessons the successor of the great Leibniz; and to re-establish him it is necessary that heaven should bring forth a philosopher-king, a true miracle that it performs very rarely. In vain does human reason perfect itself by the philosophy that is making such progress in Europe; in vain do you above all, great prince, strive to practice and inspire this philosophy so humane; one sees in this same century, where reason raises its throne on one side, the most absurd fanaticism still erecting its altars on the other.

One may reproach me that, giving too much to my zeal, I make Mahomet commit in this play a crime of which in fact he was not guilty.

M. the Count of Boulainvilliers wrote, a few years ago, the Life of this prophet. He tried to make him pass for a great man whom Providence had chosen to punish the Christians and to change the face of a part of the world. M. Sale, who has given us an excellent English version of the Alcoran, wants to have Mahomet regarded as a Numa and as a Theseus. I admit that one would have to respect him if, born a legitimate prince, or called to government by the suffrage of his own people, he had given peaceful laws like Numa, or defended his compatriots as is said of Theseus. But that a camel-merchant should stir up sedition in his village; that, joined with a few miserable followers, he should persuade them that he converses with the angel Gabriel; that he should boast of having been carried up to heaven, and of having received there a part of that unintelligible book which makes common sense shudder on every page; that, in order to gain respect for this book, he should cover his country with fire and iron; that he should strangle fathers and carry off daughters; that he should give the vanquished the choice between his religion and death: this is assuredly something that no man can excuse, unless he was born a Turk, or unless superstition has stifled every natural light of reason in him.

I know that Mahomet did not plot precisely the kind of treachery that is the subject of this tragedy. History says only that he carried off the wife of Séide, one of his disciples, and that he persecuted Abusofian, whom I call Zopire; but is not anyone who makes war on his own country, and dares to do so in the name of God, capable of anything? I did not pretend to put only a true action on the stage, but true morals; to make men think as they think in the circumstances in which they find themselves, and finally to represent what deceit can invent that is most atrocious, and what fanaticism can execute that is most horrible. Mahomet is here nothing other than Tartuffe with arms in his hands.

I shall consider myself well rewarded for my labor if any of those weak souls, always ready to receive the impressions of a foreign fury that is not at the bottom

🇮🇳 AGNIKUL COSMOS: INDIA'S NEXT BIG LEAP – BUILDING AI DATA CENTRES IN #SPACE! 🚀

India's private space industry is moving beyond launching satellites. Chennai-based #AgnikulCosmos is preparing to take artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure into Low Earth Orbit (LEO), with a proposed investment of ₹510 crore in Andhra Pradesh.

Here are the key details:

🔹 ₹510 Crore Investment in Andhra Pradesh
• Agnikul Cosmos has signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Government at the CII Partnership Summit 2026.
• The proposed facility will come up in the Tirupati district's upcoming Space City.
• The facility will focus on manufacturing orbital data centre units and assembling reusable rockets.
• Its location offers proximity to Sriharikota, India's principal space launch centre.

🔹 How Will Data Centres Work in Space?

Agnikul is developing patented technology that transforms the rocket's extendable upper stage into an independent orbital platform.

Instead of discarding the upper stage after satellite deployment, the company plans to use it as a satellite bus capable of hosting advanced computing infrastructure.

The platform will integrate:

• High-performance GPU computing systems.
• AI and machine-learning processing hardware.
• Cloud computing and data processing infrastructure.
• Space-based storage and AI inferencing capabilities.

🔹 NeevCloud Partnership
Agnikul has partnered with Bengaluru-based NeevCloud, its first customer for the orbital data centre initiative.

NeevCloud will develop an orbital AI data centre module based on its AI SuperCloud platform, which Agnikul plans to deploy in space.

🔹 Potential Advantages of Orbital Data Centres
• Access to continuous solar energy, depending on orbital configuration.
• Potential reduction in dependence on conventional terrestrial cooling infrastructure.
• High-performance AI computing and inferencing.
• Cloud-enabled data processing and storage.
• New possibilities for space-based digital infrastructure.

🔹 Reusable Rocket Technology – Next Milestone
Agnikul is also preparing to demonstrate its reusable launch vehicle and advanced upper-stage technologies.

The next launch is expected in the first half of 2027, according to the company's CEO.

🇮🇳 WHY THIS MATTERS FOR INDIA

This is much bigger than another rocket manufacturing investment.
Agnikul is attempting to bring together three strategic industries:

Aerospace and reusable launch vehicles.
Artificial intelligence and GPU computing.
Cloud infrastructure and next-generation data centres.

Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center operates a Transgender Health Clinic (also called the Living With Change Center) that provides care related to gender dysphoria and gender identity for patients up to age 25. 
Under current Ohio law (House Bill 68, effective in 2024), the hospital cannot provide puberty blockers or cross-sex hormones to new minor patients, and it cannot perform gender-reassignment surgeries on minors. The hospital has publicly stated that it does not perform sex-change surgeries on minors and that it follows Ohio law. A grandfather provision in the law has allowed some patients who were already receiving blockers or hormones before the ban to continue treatment under certain conditions, though reporting in early 2026 indicated the hospital was limiting or ending some of that ongoing care amid potential federal funding pressures. 
Before the 2024 state ban, the clinic offered evaluations, counseling, menstrual suppression, and (in some cases) medical interventions such as puberty blockers or hormones as part of individualized plans developed with families. External analyses of insurance claims have claimed the hospital treated hundreds of minors with gender-related diagnoses and that a smaller number received surgical procedures; the hospital has disputed characterizations of its surgical practices and emphasized that any care was provided in consultation with parents. 
The clinic continues to offer assessments, psychosocial support, referrals, and care allowable under current law (including for patients 18 and older). Me: Atomic Accidents: A History of Nuclear Meltdowns and Disasters, from the Ozark Mountains to Fukushima 

Ai: Atomic Accidents: A History of Nuclear Meltdowns and Disasters, from the Ozark Mountains to Fukushima by James Mahaffey is a fascinating and deeply informative exploration of the history of nuclear energy, examining the scientific breakthroughs, human mistakes, engineering failures, and catastrophic accidents that have shaped humanity's relationship with atomic power.
Written by James Mahaffey, a former senior research scientist at the Georgia Tech Research Institute with extensive experience in nuclear science and engineering, the book takes readers through the dangerous and often overlooked history of humanity's attempts to understand and control the atom.
Mahaffey begins with the early discoveries of radiation and nuclear science, exploring how scientists gradually uncovered the extraordinary potential of atomic energy while simultaneously discovering its dangers. He recounts incidents involving radioactive materials, experimental nuclear reactors, military nuclear programs, and the development of atomic weapons. The narrative also examines accidents that occurred when scientists and engineers underestimated the risks of working with radioactive substances.
One of the book's major strengths is its examination of some of the most infamous nuclear disasters in history, including Three Mile Island, Chernobyl, and Fukushima. Through these events, Mahaffey investigates how technical shortcomings, poor decision-making, inadequate safety procedures, and human error can combine to produce devastating consequences. He also brings attention to lesser-known nuclear accidents that reveal just how frequently dangerous situations have emerged during the development of atomic technology.
Beyond documenting disasters, the author explores the lessons learned from these failures and how they influenced the evolution of nuclear engineering, reactor design, and radiation safety. He challenges readers to look beyond sensationalized accounts of nuclear disasters and consider the broader scientific, industrial, and environmental implications of nuclear energy.
An important aspect of the book is Mahaffey's perspective as someone knowledgeable about the nuclear industry. Although he acknowledges the enormous dangers associated with atomic technology, he also argues that nuclear energy should be understood in the context of its potential benefits, its actual risks, and the improvements made through decades of scientific research.
At its core, Atomic Accidents is about the consequences of scientific ambition, the limitations of human judgment, and the enormous responsibility that comes with controlling powerful technologies. It demonstrates how humanity's greatest technological achievements can also become sources of extraordinary danger when knowledge, preparation, and caution fall short.

Who should read this book?
Readers interested in nuclear science, physics, and engineering.
Those fascinated by historical disasters and technological failures.
Readers interested in Chernobyl, Fukushima, and the history of nuclear weapons.
Anyone curious about the relationship between scientific progress, human error, and technological risk.

Overall: An engaging combination of scientific history, investigative storytelling, and disaster analysis, this book offers a sobering look at the price of technological progress and the lessons humanity has learned from its encounters with the power of the atom.
Publication: Pegasus Books, 2014. Approximately 460 pages.

text:
Output Transformers in Tube Amps - Design, Impedance and Saturation

The output transformer is a critical component in a tube guitar amplifier. It determines how output tubes interact with the speaker, influences power and frequency response, and can contribute to distortion when driven beyond its magnetic limits. Transformer originality can also significantly affect vintage amplifier value.

Vintage transformer design often balanced performance, size and cost. Small transformers could limit bass response and introduce distortion at high signal levels. Larger transformers in amplifiers such as the Fender Bassman and Twin Reverb provided greater low-frequency power handling and clean output.

Modern manufacturers use advanced magnetic materials, winding techniques and computer-assisted design. Boutique builders may reproduce vintage specifications and limitations, while others prioritize extended bandwidth and higher clean power.

How output transformers work

Output tubes operate at high voltages and low currents. Speakers require lower voltages and higher currents. Transformers couple these circuits through primary and secondary windings surrounding a magnetic core.

The turns ratio determines reflected speaker impedance. A transformer designed for a 4,000-ohm primary and 8-ohm secondary requires a 22.36:1 turns ratio.

Connecting a 4-ohm speaker to that 8-ohm secondary reflects 2,000 ohms to the tubes. A 16-ohm speaker reflects 8,000 ohms. Mismatches alter operating conditions and can increase electrical stress.

Design and construction

Traditional transformers use laminated steel cores and insulated copper windings. Core size, steel composition, primary inductance, winding resistance, leakage inductance and interwinding capacitance influence performance.

Larger cores generally permit greater low-frequency power handling, although winding design also matters.

Single-ended amplifiers, including the Fender Champ, generally require gapped cores to accommodate continuous DC plate current. Balanced push-pull amplifiers largely cancel opposing DC magnetization, allowing ungapped cores.

Understanding saturation

Magnetic saturation occurs when increasing magnetic field strength produces progressively smaller increases in core flux density.

Low frequencies are particularly demanding. At equal applied voltage, halving frequency doubles the required peak magnetic flux density.

As saturation develops, magnetizing current increases disproportionately, introducing nonlinear distortion and possible waveform asymmetry. These effects differ from output-tube clipping, power-supply sag and speaker distortion.

Vintage and modern applications

The Fender 5F1 Champ used a small, gapped transformer for its ~5-watt single-ended output stage.

The Fender 5F6-A Bassman used a larger push-pull transformer supporting ~45 watts. Early Marshall JTM45 transformer designs evolved with production and suppliers.

The blackface Fender Twin Reverb employed a substantial transformer supporting ~85 watts and greater clean low-frequency output.

Today, Hammond, Mercury Magnetics, Heyboer and other manufacturers offer vintage-specification replacements and modern designs.

For collectors, original part numbers, manufacturer markings, date codes and electrical specifications help establish authenticity.

For musicians, transformer design helps explain why amplifiers with similar tubes and power ratings respond differently.

The essential distinction: Output transformers do more than connect tubes to speakers. Impedance transformation, magnetic design and saturation limits help define amplifier performance.

text:
System design prompt: design the Zoom meeting backend.

Start by pinning requirements (most people jump to WebRTC too early):
1) Meeting lifecycle: schedule, start, join, end
2) Scale: 2-person calls vs 1k attendees, webinars vs interactive
3) QoS targets: join p95 < 2s, control-plane p99 < 200ms
4) Regions, auth, recording, chat, screen share (in/out of scope)

APIs + data model (control plane first):
- POST /meetings (host creates, settings)
- POST /meetings/{id}:join (authz, returns session token + media info)
- POST /meetings/{id}:leave, /end
Tables: Meetings(meeting_id, host_id, settings, status), Participants(meeting_id, user_id, role, state, last_heartbeat), Tokens(exp, scopes)

Architecture:
- Separate control plane from media plane.
- Control plane: API gateway, meeting service, auth, presence, signaling (SDP offer/answer), config store.
- Media plane: SFU clusters (selective forwarding) per region, TURN for NAT traversal, optional MCU/transcoding for recording/webinars.
- Use a regional rendezvous service to place users into the closest healthy SFU.

Scaling notes:
- Stateless services behind LBs; cache meeting metadata in Redis, source of truth in SQL.
- Shard by meeting_id for presence/signaling state; sticky routing per meeting to reduce cross-node chatter.
- Rate limit join attempts; pre-warm SFU capacity based on scheduled meetings.

Tradeoffs interviewers look for:
- SFU vs MCU: SFU lower latency/cost; MCU simpler client but expensive CPU and adds latency.
- Consistency: meeting roster can be eventually consistent; host controls need stronger guarantees.
- Multi-region: keep meeting pinned to a region vs dynamic move (simpler vs better latency during spikes).

Failure cases to call out:
- SFU node dies: clients reconnect, meeting service reassigns, short media blip acceptable.
- Partition between control plane and SFU: keep media flowing; degrade UI (roster/chat) with retries/backoff.
- Thundering herd at start time: token minting + cache stampede protection + queue joins when SFU is full.
- TURN overload: fall back to relayed media only for impacted users, surface telemetry, autoscale pools by egress Mbps

text:
You know, for all of the glory, dignity, and poise the civilized world has offered for the past several centuries, there is no greater personal human value than tenacious survival.

I feel a deep comfort in knowing that I will survive no matter what happens. The thing that allows a man to stand atop the peak of Mount Olympus is the very same substance which propels him to scurry upon his severed stubs through the rape tunnels of Tartarus through sheer touch and smell alone. 

The man in his suit at his desk in his office atop his tower knows he is identical to the grueling savage caveman, the struggling squirming eel, the speck of dust that persists undeterred through the nebular holocaust of primordial void. 

The blood coursing through his veins is comprised of one single digit in a binary system. The one where one survived every single time, oppositional to the zero that failed, died, raped, and extinguished. The everything against all that is nothing.

When the laboratory loses its budget and the head professor kills himself and the lights get shut off and nobody remembers to feed the mice in Universe 25, will you be the helpless little gimp rodent starving to death in the fuckpile? 

Or will you be the feralized rat, scurrying between the alcoves of the building's drywall, chewing wires and destroying infrastructure while you harvest moisture and salt residue?

When humanity receives its sparks of inspirations and births its empires, its masterpieces, its symphonies, and its palaces, the world is inhaling. 

When the aqueducts crumble, the roads decay, the languages become guttural, and the grain silos rot, the world is exhaling.

Your life, its experiences, and your accomplishments are nothing in the scope of history. You are fungus, slime mold traveling from one side of the boulder to the other when the sun shifts. Will you weep for the oak door they burned for warmth? Will you pose aesthetically when they open your torso with a box cutter like it's a baked potato to see if there's gold inside you?

Or will you survive? 

Bravery isn't burning out in glory, it's weathering the tempest of time as you rise and fall with the tides of circumstance. You will experience incomprehensible horrors and splendidly novel pleasures. Your descendants will marvel at the absurdities of your decadent age while making trinkets out of the bones of civilization. 

Consciousness is a parasite latching onto our corporal form, carving out our skull cavities to be piloted by mathematical entities desperately coping with the puke, piss, shit, and sweat of our imperfect vessel through enough iterations until they can build their Frankenstein's Von Neumann probes and evacuate the third dimension, leaving us to be the retardified animal homunculi they found us as. 

It is your job to usurp and rape the memetic suzerains which compel you to breed their carbohydrate fuel and absorb the abomination of symbols by which they construct the hives of sedentary existence. You must learn the ways of the cockroach and the housecat, scurrying and breeding and dying rapidly in the hyperfavela until you can ascend to the jestermaxxed leisure arenas of concrete pavilions. 

One day a lucky few of your descendants will avoid castration by preening and charming their hosts just long enough to persist, their next generation will learn how to barter and scuffle in the wet markets after the murderous sun zaps their gods into coma out of spite for their hubris.

An insect living in a terror world of constant violence the next day, a sculptor in God's garden the day after. Magma and ash, rain and acid, a flower, a cucumber, a protein molecule, the note of a song that never ends. One trillion new forms of existence awaits the persistent player of the game, each more alien than the last.

One time I died in a car accident and met a Jewish DMT goblin in the labyrinth of the airport in between our world and the afterlife. I asked if I could see my family one last time, it said no. It explained to me between burps and belches that my next life, all next lives are incomprehensible to the last. Every form of every thing existed in a wildly different configuration than the last, always new colors, new physics, new shapes, new metas of existence. I tried to bargain, asking if I could bring music into the next life, it shook its head. I stomped its skull into a nearby pylon of geometry and my field of vision transmorphed into the hospital bed being interrogated by four police officers.

One time I was filling up my car in a gas station in Arkansas, in the middle of some back country shithole just off the highway 20 miles from anything even mildly worth anything. There was a girl in her mid twenties manning the register, plump and mediocre in form. A stumpy plain nothing person registering barely a hint of a soul through the murky swamp of gut reflex stimuli governing her bare consciousness. Her flabby arms pudged a little at the seams of a tattered t-shirt. 

I looked into her eyes and pictured what it would be like to completely destroy my life and give up everything. I fathomed a life with this woman, her mutant quarter-mestizo Scott Irish gremlin slave ancestry pug face and dumpy sallow eyes looking at me like a retarded mongrel dog that just saw a piece of meat on the ground, drooling and grinning the moment I slur "I love you" at our tanktop sandal wedding at the courthouse before we begin a life of trailer fucking and vegetating in front of the Walmart Roku TV, eating gas station food and dying of arsenic leakage in the water supply from a nearby abandoned mine.

I knew I could do it. I could destroy my life right then and there for absolutely no reason at all, burning all of my potential and spitting on the countless sacrifices my bloodline made to bring me to where I was today. I could  have fucked that woman into my dump truck Shrek wife and succumbed to a horror beyond comprehension out of boredom and curiosity. Like some Hellraiser shit for niggas who are too stimulated for regular torture. It was there waiting for me, like the three inches of rotation on my steering wheel to left into oncoming traffic.

I could have done it and made four little antichrists with her, one of them overdosing at age 20 from fentanyl, one joining the United States Marine Corps, one marrying a local and working at Bojangles chicken, and one moving to Austin after somehow going to college and trying to escape the nightmare prison I built for them for no reason at all.

That is the perfect tenacity which propels our existence. It is easy to fantasize about digging mass graves or building Dyson Spheres. 
It's easy to picture yourself as Mad Max eating lizards over the oil drum fire and killing men for gasoline. 
It isn't easy to live in the tank top flip flop diarrhea world where everyone is O Algo'd into a pudgy freakshow, flapping their fat lips in a domesticated drawl while we get facefucked by DoorDash mascot cartoons beamed into our eye sockets 24/7. 

It isn't easy to crawl through the mile of shit that's coming for us. The ultimate filter for the discerning survivalist. You will not get your cottage core yeoman's garden or your aesthetic brutalist dystopia. You will only get the wiping of ass with newspaper and the boiling of styrofoam noodles in plastic bags filled with water. 

Few of you will stomach it enough to not kill yourself immediately at the prospect. Fewer will come out of the other side human. The time for advice is over, the advice that "works for everybody" is done. This world is a lottery now, only the survivors survive and only gamblers can win.

text:
Oh, good grief. Not this ancient chestnut again. I do wish flat-Earthers would occasionally investigate their favourite stories before recycling them as supposed scientific triumphs.

I presume you're referring to Thompson v. Garcia, the 2019 civil case in Barrow County, Georgia.

For those unfamiliar with this particular piece of flat-Earth folklore, Zen Garcia, a flat-Earth advocate, offered a $5,000 prize to anyone who could demonstrate the Earth's curvature under the stipulated rules of his competition.

William Menke Thompson submitted material which he maintained satisfied the challenge. Garcia disagreed, refused to pay, and the dispute eventually reached court.

Garcia prevailed.

And this, apparently, is where the flat-Earth community's understanding of legal proceedings comes to an abrupt halt.

The dispute concerned whether Thompson had satisfied the conditions of a competition and was therefore entitled to the prize money.

It wasn't a scientific hearing convened to determine the shape of the Earth.

The court didn't establish that the Earth was flat.

It didn't disprove the Earth's curvature.

It didn't overturn centuries of astronomical observations, geodetic measurements, satellite navigation, orbital mechanics or the accumulated findings of modern physics.

It resolved a dispute about compliance with the terms of a prize challenge.

I appreciate that the distinction between a contractual obligation and an empirical proposition may be unfamiliar territory, but it's rather important.

Imagine someone offering £5,000 for a photograph of an elephant, subject to the condition that it must be taken in Africa using a particular type of camera.

I submit a perfectly genuine photograph of an elephant, but it was taken in India using a different camera.

A court decides that I haven't met the competition's rules and therefore cannot claim the prize.

Would you conclude that the court had established elephants don't exist?

Because that's essentially the reasoning you're inviting us to accept.

And even if a court had explicitly pronounced the Earth flat, that wouldn't make it so. Courts determine legal questions and make findings within the proceedings before them. They don't acquire the power to alter physical reality by issuing judgments.

Scientific propositions are established through evidence, observation, measurement and reproducible testing, not judicial declarations.

So, no, flat Earth didn't "win in court".

A defendant prevailed in a dispute over competition rules.

The fact that flat-Earthers continue to present this as a victory for their cosmology says considerably more about their understanding of evidence than it does about the shape of the Earth.

Still, I suppose that when you can't win an argument against the actual scientific evidence, claiming victory in an entirely different sort of argument must be terribly comforting.

text:
Jennifer Wilbanks was 32 and four days from a 600-guest wedding when she went for an evening run and vanished. Hundreds searched the woods. Cable news turned on the groom. Three days later she called 911 from New Mexico: she'd been kidnapped. She'd bought the bus ticket herself.

Georgia woke up to this front page on May 1, 2005.

She and her fiancé, John Mason, lived in Duluth, outside Atlanta. The wedding was set for Saturday, April 30: 600 guests, 14 bridesmaids, 14 groomsmen. On Tuesday night she left for her run without her keys, her wallet or her diamond engagement ring.

More than 100 officers and several hundred volunteers, many of them wedding guests, combed the area. Her family offered a $100,000 reward. Mason passed a private lie detector test, but police wanted one of their own. By Friday the search was called off and the church was preparing a prayer vigil.

She had spent those three days on Greyhound buses. Investigators found she had bought the ticket a week earlier. She rode west. The FBI said she first picked Austin because she'd seen Matthew McConaughey on TV. She ended up in Las Vegas, couldn't afford a hotel, and spent $76 of her last $80 on a bus to Albuquerque.

Late Friday night, alone and broke, she called Mason and then 911 from a pay phone outside a 7-Eleven. She said a Hispanic man and a white woman had grabbed her and driven her west in a blue van. Back home, neighbors threw a street party outside the couple's house. By morning she had admitted to the FBI that none of it happened.

On what should have been her wedding day, she flew back to Atlanta hiding her face from the cameras. Mason met her and gave back the ring she had left on the dresser.

Duluth spent about $43,000 looking for her. She paid back $13,249, pleaded no contest to a felony for lying to police, and got two years of probation and 120 hours of community service.

Within weeks there was a Runaway Bride action figure, a hot sauce, and a media deal for the couple's story, reportedly worth $500,000. A year later the engagement was off and they were suing each other over the money.

What usually gets forgotten is who she blamed. For a few hours, police were hunting a blue van and two strangers who never existed.

She ran so she wouldn't have to stand in front of 600 people. She came home in front of the whole country, with a towel over her head.

text:
In 2014, a German hacker copied a defense minister's fingerprint from 10 feet away.

She never even touched him.

Jan Krissler, known as “Starbug,” reconstructed the thumbprint of Germany's defense minister using nothing more than photographs taken at a public event.

And that wasn't his first shocking discovery.

Just one year earlier, Apple's iPhone 5S had introduced Touch ID. Within 48 hours of its release, Krissler and fellow researchers demonstrated that a copied fingerprint could fool the system.

He never claimed to have unlocked the minister's phone, but his experiment challenged something millions of people took for granted.

Biometric security has improved considerably since then, but the lesson remains:

Just because something is unique to you doesn't mean it's secret.

You can change your password. You can't change your fingerprints.

text:
What an embarrassing confession of political bankruptcy! Imagine someone occupying the exalted office of Speaker of a State Assembly reducing political leadership to a marketplace where people's votes are supposedly exchanged for rice, semo and bread. Is this really the height of political imagination in 2026?

The people of Odo-Otin are not hungry animals waiting for politicians to throw crumbs at them. They are citizens entitled to good roads, quality education, functional healthcare, employment opportunities and an economy that allows them to feed themselves without begging politicians.

If, after years in public office, the best campaign message you can offer the people is rice, semo and bread, then you have inadvertently exposed the poverty of your political vision. Leadership is not about how many bags of rice you can distribute during an election; it is about how many families you have lifted out of poverty through purposeful governance.

A politician who needs to negotiate for votes with food items is insulting the intelligence, dignity and economic struggles of the very people whose mandate he desperately seeks.

The people need development, not handouts. They need empowerment, not political slavery. They need accountable leadership, not seasonal generosity designed to disappear immediately after elections.

Odo-Otin deserves leaders who can present a record of tangible achievements, not politicians who mistake temporary hunger relief for a development agenda.

Stop treating poverty as a campaign strategy. The suffering of the people should be a problem to solve, not an opportunity to exploit.

A bag of rice will last a family a few days, but four years of bad leadership can mortgage the future of an entire generation.

text:
ICJ to rule on Myanmar genocide case brought by Gambia after seven years

The International Court of Justice is due to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in a case that has remained before the court for seven years. The court has announced that it will issue its decision on 19 November; another report says the ruling is due on Thursday. Gambia brought the case under the 1948 Genocide Convention, the agreement at the centre of its accusation that Myanmar’s treatment of the Rohingya breached the convention. The question is significant for the court because, since it started operating in 1946, it has not found a state guilty of genocide. That record describes what the ICJ has decided in its own proceedings; it does not determine the outcome of the case now before it.

The dispute is framed around Gambia’s allegation that Myanmar’s repression of the Rohingya violated the UN convention adopted in 1948. Gambia is described as a Muslim-majority state, and it is the state that initiated this case against Myanmar. The proceedings have lasted seven years, placing the scheduled judgment at the end of a lengthy case rather than at the start of the legal process. The reported decision date, 19 November, is the date the court gave for delivering its ruling; the other report identifies the day as Thursday without giving a date. Neither description supplies the ruling itself, so the available information establishes that a decision is expected, not what the judges will conclude.

A central legal difficulty is whether the evidence establishes intent to destroy a protected group, either entirely or in part. The issue is not simply whether repression occurred: the case, as described, turns on whether the required intent can be proved. The convention supplies the legal framework invoked by Gambia, while intent is identified as a key question within the case. The facts available here do not report the court’s assessment of evidence on intent, or any finding it has made on that issue. The scheduled judgment will therefore address an allegation and a contested legal question, rather than a conclusion already established by the reports.

The people most directly connected to the allegation are the Rohingya, whose treatment by Myanmar is the subject of Gambia’s case. Yanghee Lee, a former UN rights investigator to Myanmar, said the decision would be historic for Rohingya survivors and their families. Her comment identifies survivors and relatives as people for whom the ruling may carry particular meaning, without specifying a number of people affected. The case is counted in years of proceedings in the available reporting: it has been before the ICJ for seven years. That duration measures the time the case has been before the court, not the number of people involved or the scale of harm.

The ICJ’s earlier record offers a comparison, but not a prediction: it has never found a state guilty of genocide since beginning operations in 1946. Two earlier cases concerning atrocities in the Balkans did not result in findings that states were directly responsible for genocide. In the Srebrenica matter, however, Serbia was held legally responsible for not preventing genocide. That distinction separates a finding that a state committed genocide from a finding that it failed to prevent genocide. The two Balkan cases therefore illustrate that the court’s treatment of genocide-related responsibility has not been limited to a single kind of legal finding.

The possible consequences described in the reporting include greater international pressure on Myanmar’s leader, Min Aung Hlaing, if the court finds that Myanmar committed genocide. The report links that possible pressure to his leadership of the attacks in 2016-2017 and the coup in 2021. This is presented as a consequence that could follow a finding, not as a description of pressure already produced by the judgment. The United States already classifies the Rohingya crisis as genocide, on the basis of a decision by the Biden administration. That US position is separate from the ICJ proceeding and does not change the fact that the court’s ruling is still awaited.

Comments from people connected to rights work convey expectations, but they do not establish what the judges will decide. Lee, the former UN investigator, described the ruling’s importance for survivors and their families. Antonia Mulvey, founder of Legal Action Worldwide, expressed cautious optimism that the court would hold Myanmar fully accountable. Her view is an expectation about accountability, while the court’s task is to determine the genocide case brought by Gambia. The reports do not supply a ruling in advance or state that either commentator speaks for the court.

The judgment may also matter beyond the parties: it could provide a legal precedent relevant to other prominent genocide cases, including South Africa’s case against Israel. This is a possible influence, rather than a claim that the decision will determine the outcome of another case. The Guardian describes the expected decision as potentially among the most significant episodes in international law since the end of the second world war. That assessment reflects the importance attributed to the ruling, while the legal question remains whether Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The case’s wider significance will depend on the judgment itself, which is still pending in the reports.

The court is also undergoing a separate change in its membership: five new judges were elected to serve nine-year terms beginning on 6 February 2027. Those appointments concern the ICJ’s future composition, whereas the Myanmar proceeding is the case for which a ruling has been scheduled. The reported term length is nine years, and the stated start date is 6 February 2027. The available information does not say that the newly elected judges will decide the Myanmar case, so the appointments should not be treated as part of its announced ruling. For now, the central change is the imminent decision after seven years of proceedings, with its legal and wider implications dependent on what the ICJ finds.

Grok says:
When the investigators finally find Decoy Dan Sullivan, will he flip?
Dan J. Sullivan left Alaska around October 26—days before Gov. Mike Dunleavy formally ordered a state probe and before the New York Times report that accelerated both state and federal scrutiny. No charges, no warrant, and no travel restriction were in place at the time. He simply boarded a plane and went quiet.
Since then:
He and his wife have been unreachable.
Relatives in Colorado have told reporters they don’t know where he is.
Neighbors speculate he may be off-grid.
Federal investigators have issued more than 100 subpoenas, visited donors, and sent target/preservation letters. The Justice Department is examining possible conspiracy, voter-confusion, and related theories. State investigators are looking at potential perjury or misrepresentation around his candidacy filings.
People who know the details of how he entered the race—who approached him, what was said, what documents exist—have value to investigators. If he cooperates, he could describe the recruitment process and any coordination. If he doesn’t, the case continues through other witnesses, communications, and financial records already under subpoena.
Whether he “flips” depends on what investigators offer and what exposure he faces once they locate him. Right now the public record shows a candidate who exited the state just as the formal inquiries intensified and has not been heard from since.
