NOTE 🙏🙏🙏🙏 I have devoted hours of deep thought, reflection, and unwavering dedication to writing this post. Every word carries the strength of my conviction and the depth of my respect for Bharat.

This message deserves to transcend geographical boundaries, cross continents, and resonate in every corner of the world.
Let its light illuminate minds across nations, so that the world may truly understand the extraordinary strength, resilience, and unshakable foundations of Bharat as a राष्ट्र and the enduring spirit of its democracy.

The world must recognize that Bharat's national foundation is not merely a product of political institutions or constitutional arrangements. It is deeply rooted in an ancient civilizational consciousness, cultural continuity, and an enduring sense of national identity.

Bharat is not merely a nation on the world map; it is a living civilization whose roots run deep through the centuries and whose democratic spirit continues to shape its destiny.

Yesterday, when the Honourable Prime Minister of Bharat respectfully picked up a printed image of the Indian map lying on the ground, he demonstrated an extraordinary expression of reverence, devotion, and unwavering dedication to the motherland.

It was not merely a gesture of respect towards a geographical map. It was a profound manifestation of the civilizational consciousness that defines the very soul of Bharat.
The world, including the three other leaders present on that occasion, may require centuries to fully comprehend the philosophical depth of राष्ट्र, the spiritual significance of भारतमाता, and the extraordinary relationship between the Indian people and their motherland.

Bharat's conception of the motherland represents one of humanity's most profound civilizational and cultural philosophies.

भारतीय civilization did not merely recognize the land as a geographical territory. It elevated the motherland to the sacred status of माता the Mother.
More importantly, this philosophy recognized the dignity, existence, nurturing power, affection, and spiritual supremacy of मातृशक्ति the Divine Feminine in the form of भारतमाता.

The motherland was not conceived merely as soil, mountains, rivers, forests, or territorial boundaries. She was envisioned as a living embodiment of collective consciousness, cultural continuity, spiritual inheritance, and civilizational existence.
The philosophical depth of this conception is extraordinary.

भारतमाता is not merely a national personification. She represents an enduring relationship between the land, its civilization, culturre its people, and the sacred consciousness that binds them together.

BHARAT IS NOT MERELY A POLITICAL STATE
If we examine the political map of the world, we discover that modern states are generally defined by political sovereignty, territorial jurisdiction, constitutional authority, and governmental institutions.

That is why the term State represents a political and legal entity.
But can the existence of Bharat be confined to such a narrow political definition?
Certainly not.

Bharat is a sovereign state in the modern constitutional sense, but its civilizational identity extends far beyond the boundaries of political statehood.

Thats why Framers of constitution had put Ram Darbar  and other its civilizational  and cultural photo  in original constitution. 

Bharat is not merely a State. Bharat is a राष्ट्र.
A political state may emerge, expand, fragment, or disappear.
Governments may rise and fall. Dynasties may flourish and perish. Political boundaries may be redrawn.

But a राष्ट्र, rooted in civilizational consciousness, collective memory, cultural continuity, and spiritual inheritance, cannot be reduced to the lifespan of a political administration.
This distinction is fundamental to understanding Bharat.

From the Mughal period to British colonial rule, successive imperial powers attempted to consolidate their political authority over vast parts of the Indian subcontinent.
Yet political domination never completely extinguished the underlying civilizational identity of Bharat.

The British East India Company's political expansion, the Regulating Act of 1773, the successive administrative reforms, and ultimately the Cabinet Mission of 1946 reflect the long and complex history of colonial attempts to establish and maintain political authority.

Despite extensive colonial control, the British Empire could not permanently suppress India's aspiration for freedom or erase its civilizational consciousness.
Eventually, colonial rule came to an end.

This is why Bharat's existence cannot be traced merely to August 15, 1947.
It does not mark the birth of भारतीय civilization.

Modern India achieved independence in 1947. Bharat's civilizational existence is far older.

BHARAT IS MORE THAN A GEOGRAPHICAL (देश)
In its geographical sense, देश refers to a land, region, or territorial space.

Ancient भारतीय philosophical literature frequently employs the concepts of देश and काल—space and time—to examine the conditions of existence and the relationship between phenomena.

But Bharat cannot be understood merely as a geographical space.
Bharat is not simply a piece of land enclosed within political boundaries.

In the civilizational understanding of राष्ट्र, Bharat represents a profound unity of geography, culture, collective memory, philosophical traditions, spiritual consciousness, and shared historical experience.
It is a civilization that has continuously renewed itself across countless generations.

Bharat is not merely a land inhabited by people; it is a civilizational consciousness sustained by its people.

Within the spiritual vision of सनातन धर्म, Bharat is revered as a sacred land where even the देवता are described as longing to take birth.

Such descriptions express the extraordinary sanctity attributed to this land in the भारतीय spiritual imagination.

From this philosophical perspective, Bharat is not merely a passive geographical entity.
It is understood as a living civilizational consciousness, capable of preserving, regulating, renewing, and transmitting its cultural and spiritual inheritance across generations.

THE PSYCHOLOGY AND PHILOSOPHY OF NATIONAL SYMBOLS

To understand the significance of the Prime Minister's gesture, we must first understand the deeper psychological and philosophical functions of symbols.

Symbols are not merely physical objects or visual representations.
They serve as powerful mediums through which deeply embedded emotions, beliefs, memories, aspirations, and collective identities find expression.

A symbol can awaken feelings residing within both the conscious and subconscious dimensions of the human mind.
It can transform abstract ideals into emotionally meaningful experiences.

It can connect individuals with something far greater than their immediate personal existence.
This is precisely why the National Flag, राष्ट्रगीत, राष्ट्र-गान, and other national symbols possess such extraordinary emotional significance.
For millions of Indians, these symbols are not merely ceremonial representations of a political state.

They embody sacrifice, freedom, civilizational continuity, collective dignity, national unity, and devotion to the motherland.
A national symbol may be physical in its form, but the emotions, ideals, and collective memories associated with it extend far beyond its material existence.

The spiritual philosophy underlying मूर्ति पूजा, or idol worship, also offers an important perspective on the relationship between symbols, human consciousness, devotion, and the experience of the sacred.

I intend to explore this fascinating philosophical and psychological subject in greater detail in a separate article.

WHY THE NATIONAL FLAG OF BHARAT HOLDS SUCH SACRED SIGNIFICANCE
Now, returning to the central issue, let us consider the legal and philosophical treatment of national flags.

In the USA anyone can Burn the National Flag of USA and there would be no punishment. 
She the hollowness concept of there , there is no concept of such sacrosanct entity. 

They will teach us democracy and concept of statecraft etc  ???
Certainly Not at All.
बच्चे हैं वो ,उन्हें सीखना होगा भारत की शरण में आकर. 

Bharat follows a different legal approach.
Under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act   strictly punishable not for national flags but other national symbols.

The distinction is not merely legal. It also invites a deeper discussion about the philosophical relationship between national symbols, collective identity, and freedom of expression.
For countless Indians, the तिरंगा represents far more than the sovereignty of a modern political state.

It represents the honour, dignity, sacrifice, faith, ideals, and aspirations associated with the राष्ट्र.
It carries the emotional inheritance of generations who struggled, suffered, and sacrificed for the freedom of Bharat.
Its significance is inseparable from the reverence that millions of Indians feel.

And that is why the Prime Minister's gesture carried such profound symbolic significance.
THE तिरंगा: THE HONOUR, PRIDE, AND SOUL OF BHARAT
How many patriots, freedom fighters, revolutionaries, and courageous sons and daughters of भारतमाता sacrificed their lives so that the तिरंगा could fly freely over an independent nation?

How many endured imprisonment, torture, persecution, exile, and death while dreaming of a free Bharat?

How many mothers sacrificed their children?

How many families surrendered their happiness?

How many unnamed heroes disappeared into the pages of history after giving everything for the freedom of their motherland?

Their sacrifices are woven into the moral and emotional significance of our National Flag.

The तिरंगा is not merely a combination of three colours. It is a living reminder of the courage of our freedom fighters, the sacrifices of our martyrs, and the unfulfilled aspirations of generations who dreamed of a free and dignified Bharat.
 
Empires may rise and fall.
Political powers may emerge and disappear.
Governments may change, and geographical boundaries may undergo transformation.
But the deeper civilizational consciousness of Bharat continues to connect its people across generations.

According to Maharshi Aurobindo, 
""the spirit of self-sacrifice is not commonly found among all nations or individuals.
This spirit is exceedingly rare and belongs to the highest order of human virtues.

It represents the blossoming of humanity’s moral evolution, marking the transformation from the selfish instincts of animal nature toward the selfless and divine qualities of human existence.

A person who possesses the capacity for self-sacrifice has already transcended the animalistic tendencies within himself.
Such an individual carries within himself the seeds of a future, higher, and more evolved humanity.

A nation that possesses the collective strength and capacity for self-sacrifice in the service of its national ideals has secured the foundations of its future.""

इस तिरंगे की आन, बान और शान के लिए न जाने कितने देशभक्तों, स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों और भारत माता के सपूतों ने अपने प्राणों का बलिदान दे दिया है।
तिरंगा हमारी साँस है। हर भारतीय इसे मुक्त आकाश में लहराता हुआ शान से देखना चाहता है। कोई भी सच्चा भारतीय इसे ज़मीन पर पड़ा हुआ नहीं देखना चाहता, चाहे वह तिरंगा झंडा हो या तिरंगे झंडे का कोई अन्य स्वरूप।

text:
ICYMI O/N - WEDNESDAY, 18 NOVEMBER

NVIDIA:

Nvidia (+3%) boosted its sales forecast for next year and vowed to improve access to critical supplies, while tamping down speculation that Jensen Huang might return. The company added $150 billion to its stock-buyback program and said revenue will grow 75% in the next fiscal year, up from a previous forecast of 70%. (BBG)

Nvidia said it would submit its quarterly 10-Q “in the coming weeks,” rather than alongside the results as usual. (WSJ)

Nvidia’s spending commitments rose to $518bn from $366bn, including $390bn of supply-purchase commitments versus $279bn, mainly for memory. Cloud-service and data-centre leases rose to $102bn from $74bn, including $74bn not yet commenced; planned FY2028 supplier spending is $203bn. (Nvidia, BBG)

CoreWeave jumped more than 9% (NBIS +7%) after hours as Nvidia’s call reassured investors that support for strong existing cloud customers would continue. Asian equities struggled to sustain the initial Nvidia-led bounce. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index was little changed, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.1%. (WSJ, BBG)

Nvidia will scrutinize future financing assistance, Kress said, prioritizing strong customers and projects involving land, power and buildings. Some guarantees would lapse if projects were delayed or failed to obtain financing. (WSJ)

Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones told the earnings call that the board unanimously accepted Jensen Huang’s voluntary resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, directly confirming its previously reported position. Heidrick & Struggles is handling the successor search; executives declined questions on his departure or the investigation. (WSJ, BBG)

Nvidia is still facing a push from some directors to bring Huang back despite the board’s public position, Semafor reports. Arm’s Rene Haas and Marvell’s Matt Murphy have been considered for CEO; Haas has expressed concern about taking the role amid the reinstatement campaign. (Semafor)

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s roughly 3.5% holding gives him a route to nominate two independent directors under proxy-access rules, Reuters reports. Nominees would still need shareholder approval; the right does not automatically give him board seats. (RTRS)

Nvidia sales staff introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice before the 2022 export curbs, then suggested Megaspeed’s overseas chip-rental route after restrictions began, The Information reports. The article distinguishes that then-legal remote access from subsequent alleged physical chip diversion. (The Information)

Nvidia’s former sales chief Jay Puri oversaw business with customers including Alice Huang, The Information reports, and is married to former Supermicro executive Cenly Chen, who managed its Nvidia relationship. Neither has been criminally charged in the cited export-diversion case. (The Information)

US banks asked for extra protection to expand financing for a data center operator that previously sold computing power to Megaspeed International Pte. Citigroup and JPMorgan added new language to financing documents for a potential upsized $6.6 billion loan sought by Bain Capital-owned Bridge Data Centres that makes it the borrower’s responsibility to comply with restrictions on chip access. (BBG)

MACRO:

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an urgent warning Tuesday about a critical vulnerability discovered in Java. The vulnerability is the second flaw discovered in major programming languages in recent weeks with the help of AI tools, and leaves much of the internet exposed to cyberattacks if it isn’t patched immediately. (Politico)

Marco Rubio said there was no indication recent US technology outages were connected or caused by hostile actors, describing separate events with individual explanations. The White House said officials had reviewed the incidents individually; a coordinated cyberattack has not been established. (BBG, WSJ)

NSA closed its campus to most employees Tuesday night as restoration of its classified internal network remained incomplete, reversing an earlier instruction to return normally. NSA said mission-critical capabilities remained operational; sources reported no evidence of a cyberattack. (CNN)

Work on Trump’s proposed US-China investment board has stalled, a person familiar told Bloomberg. Officials have largely treated it as a channel for existing investment complaints rather than facilitating new Chinese projects. (BBG)

Bloomberg’s new analysis identified 137 Chinese transactions scrutinised by CFIUS, finding that grounds for rejection expanded from one category in 2008 to at least eight by 2025, extending well beyond sensitive technology. (BBG)

Trump plans a meeting with Mexico’s Sheinbaum on the sidelines of APEC, a White House official said. The encounter comes amid trade negotiations and US pressure over Chinese goods entering through Mexico. (BBG)

Fidelity International is neutral on Treasury duration, with macro chief Salman Ahmed saying even a 6% US 10-year yield would not make bonds particularly cheap. He cited persistent inflation, rising debt and weaker diversification benefits. (BBG)

Morgan Stanley expects the Fed’s rate midpoint to reach 4.375% by March (50bps of hikes), remain there through 2027 and fall in H1 2028. It forecasts two-year Treasury yields at 4.70% by Q4 2027 (4.80% currently). (WSJ)

Capital Economics expects a sustained AI-equity downturn to slow US growth, curb Fed tightening and lower Treasury yields and the dollar. (WSJ)

Analysts forecast global earnings growth of 16% in 2027, down from 33.5% this year, according to Bloomberg data compiled by the FT. Slower AI investment growth, depreciation and higher financing costs feature in banks’ explanations. (FT)

Barclays forecasts the S&P 500 at 8,700 next year, roughly 9% above its projected end-2026 level. Morgan Stanley forecasts a 15% gain, according to the FT’s roundup of banks’ 2027 outlooks. (FT)

Truist’s Keith Lerner urged underweight investors to consider adding technology exposure after the valuation reset. He argued that much of the downside from leadership, financing and AI-investment concerns was already reflected in prices. (BBG)

HSBC continues to favour dollar strength, citing a resilient US economy, a hawkish Fed and reduced policy uncertainty in its 2027 outlook. (WSJ)

A Texas data-centre investor and developer told the FT that he and others not yet building would stop spending until the incoming government’s rules became clear. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on restricting data centres and cutting subsidies. (FT)

Senate permitting reform negotiators have finalized changes to the energy permitting bill, BAAJA, ahead of the final vote expected this week, adding tribal-review provisions and compensation protections for landowners affected by transmission projects. (Punchbowl’s Mark Siegel, Politico)

Rep-elect Jake Johnson endorsed Jeffries for speaker after receiving assurances of votes to end Trump’s tariffs and the Iran war. (Axios)

Gold fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025, trading down 2%. Silver (-3.5%) also dropped sharply. (BBG)

Japan's exports rose for a 14th successive month in October, government data showed on Wednesday, setting a record monthly value as robust global investment continued to support demand for shipments related to semiconductors. (RTRS)

Japan’s 20-year bond auction drew weaker demand, with bid-to-cover falling to 3.64 from 5.84 and below the 3.92 annual average. The tail widened to 0.29 from 0.07, its widest in a year. (BBG)

BoJ Governor Ueda said the planned food sales-tax cut would probably support growth, but its effect on underlying inflation was highly uncertain. He reiterated the bank’s intention to continue raising rates as economic conditions warrant. (BBG)

A Japanese Finance Ministry panel warned that Takaichi’s economic strategy depends on preserving market confidence, according to a draft obtained by Bloomberg. It urged stronger fiscal discipline and opposed borrowing to finance the defence buildup. (BBG)

Citi’s Osamu Takashima estimates foreign investors’ currency hedging added roughly ¥25tn of yen selling over the year to July 2026. He told the FT that hedging Japan’s AI-linked equity rally could offset forces otherwise supporting the currency. (FT)

The PBOC strengthened its daily yuan fixing to 6.7118 per dollar, its strongest since July 2022, signalling tolerance for gradual appreciation as China hosts APEC. (BBG)

UBS forecasts the yuan reaching 6.25 per dollar by end-2027, matching Nomura at the bullish end of market forecasts. Research chief Eric Lin cited easing outflow pressure and appreciation expectations in a Bloomberg interview. (BBG)

Xi Jinping pledged tariff cuts and welcomed foreign investment in Wednesday’s Apec business address, while warning that unilateralism and protectionism were “rampant”. (FT)

Chinese bank stocks are benefiting from rotation out of AI shares, with BofA describing state-owned lenders as a defensive destination for hedge-fund flows. The CSI 300 Banks Index has gained more than 4% since Nvidia’s scandal emerged. (BBG)

China and South Korea concluded negotiations on upgrading their free-trade agreement and pledged to develop cultural exchanges, Bloomberg reported, citing Xinhua’s account of Xi and Lee’s Wednesday meeting. (BBG)

South Korea’s state-run think tank sharply raised its growth outlook for next year, betting the global artificial intelligence boom will continue to power semiconductor exports and investment to help sustain the economy’s momentum. (BBG)

Australian wage growth accelerated to 3.5% year-on-year, above the expected 3.4%. Quarterly wages rose 1.1%, the fastest increase since late 2023. (BBG)

UK CPI accelerated to 3.6% y/y in October from 3.5%, matching consensus but below the BOE’s 3.7% forecast. Core inflation held at 2.8% and services inflation at 3.7%, with energy costs driving the headline pickup. Sterling fell while traders pared tightening bets, with swaps implying another 90bp by end-2027. (BBG, FT)

The Bank of England said on Wednesday that inflation was expected to rise further by the middle of next year due to cost pressures already in the pipeline, in a statement responding to Wednesday's official consumer prices data. (RTRS)

Morgan Stanley expects two more BoE hikes to 4.50% by February, against almost four priced by markets. (WSJ)

Cornwall Insight forecasts a 26% rise in the UK energy price cap to about £2,166 a year in January, which would be the largest increase since 2022. Ofgem’s decision is due later this month. (BBG)

Goldman forecasts European earnings growth of 7% in 2027 versus 18% this year, largely reflecting a slowdown in energy profits. Morgan Stanley forecasts 7.5% earnings growth and a 15% rise in the Stoxx Europe 600. (FT)

France and other indebted nations must rein in spending or face even higher borrowing costs, and markets could play a key role in disciplining governments, the European Central Bank said, indicating it was in no hurry to intervene in markets. (RTRS)

The European Central Bank said the growing presence of global hedge funds makes European government bonds more vulnerable to an abrupt repricing. (BBG)

Germany’s coalition agreed to cut household electricity tax by about 2 cents per kWh to 0.1 cents during 2027, also extending relief to smaller businesses. Financing for a permanent reduction remains unresolved. (BBG)

Schroders’ global unconstrained fixed-income fund holds no French government bonds, strategist James Bilson told Bloomberg, citing the difficulty of finding a durable political solution to France’s budget problems. (BBG)

Morgan Stanley favours long-duration Bunds and gilts for 2027, targeting year-end ten-year yields of 3.10% (3.36% currently) and 5.00% (5.32% currently), respectively. (WSJ)

Morgan Stanley expects elevated French–German spreads to persist through election uncertainty, forecasting 135bp in Q4 2027 and 115bp in Q4 2028, versus a 149.7bp latest close. (WSJ)

Indian officials are reviewing a possible 50% cut in securities transaction tax on cash equities alongside higher derivatives levies, people familiar said. The proposals remain under consideration ahead of February’s budget. (BBG)

Bank Indonesia unexpectedly raised its policy rate 25bp to 6.00% to support the record-low rupiah and contain inflation risks. Twenty-two of 38 economists in Bloomberg’s survey had expected a hold. (RTRS, BBG)

Bank Indonesia will reduce domestic NDF hedging premiums and introduce cross-currency repo transactions against specified dollar securities, adding incentives and liquidity tools to support rupiah assets. (BBG)

Trump claimed a major new Philippines trade deal, but Philippine officials said no tariff rate or specific commitments had been agreed. Talks will continue on US energy and food supplies. (BBG)

South Africa’s rand weakened past 17 per dollar as annual inflation accelerated at its fastest pace since 2024, a day before policymakers are widely seen leaving interest rates unchanged. (BBG)

The global platinum market will swing back to a deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday. (RTRS)

CRU expects cobalt demand from consumer electronics to fall 24% this year as expensive memory chips depress gadget sales. Its analyst said a demand recovery was unlikely before later next year. (BBG)

IRAN:

Iran’s army claimed it targeted Patriot, drone and missile installations at Kuwait’s Ali Al Salem air base. Kuwait said it countered hostile drones in its first Iranian attack since September, according to Reuters; damage to the claimed targets was not independently confirmed. (RTRS, Kuwait Army)

Bahrain said it intercepted renewed Iranian aerial attacks, the third assault this week on the country hosting the US Fifth Fleet. (RTRS)

Several US soldiers were reportedly injured in a drone attack on Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, according to Iranian state media citing unnamed sources. (IRIB)

US and Iranian forces have exchanged strikes almost daily, with many US operations left unacknowledged by the Pentagon, NBC News reported. (NBC)

Al-Akhbar reported an Iranian two-day peace proposal that would require the US to end hostilities, lift oil sanctions and its naval blockade, and release frozen Iranian assets on day one, before Tehran reopens Hormuz and begins talks on a final agreement, including its nuclear programme, on day two. The proposal condenses Iran’s earlier seven-day plan, with sequencing still the main sticking point: Washington reportedly wants nuclear concessions upfront and to defer some commitments, while Qatari mediation has yet to resolve the impasse. (Al-Akhbar)

Smaller tankers carried more than 2 million barrels a day through Hormuz in October, a wartime high, Vortexa data showed. Their growing role helped overall exports reach 11.4 million barrels a day, the highest since the war began. (BBG)

China's exports of refined oil products in October rose 14.6% year-on-year but fell from September, customs data showed on Wednesday. (RTRS)

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen carried out extensive attacks on the Houthis in the latest flare-up in fighting between the kingdom and the Iran-backed militia. (BBG)

QatarEnergy's efforts to reduce its exposure to future disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could leave it controlling roughly a quarter of global LNG supply within a decade, eclipsing rivals such as Shell, but raising concerns about market concentration and commercial risks. (RTRS)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Putin told business leaders in Shenzhen on Wednesday that sanctions had strengthened Russia while damaging western economies. He advocated a broader Eurasian economic partnership ahead of Thursday’s expected meeting with Trump and Xi. (FT)

EU officials are racing to agree a budget of up to €2tn and as much as €70bn of 2027 Ukraine funding before France’s election, WSJ reports. Le Pen’s lead has heightened fears that a future French veto could disrupt both packages. (WSJ)

Brussels will propose a €45bn Ukraine loan today, comprising €25bn for defence and €20bn for budget support, according to plans seen by the FT. (FT)

Brussels would service new non-EU G7 loans using profits from frozen Russian assets. It will also seek guarantees from six triple-A non-EU countries to raise up to €5bn more for Ukraine. (FT)

Xi met Putin in Shenzhen ahead of the APEC leaders’ meetings. Putin said he expected considerable benefits from the Trump–Xi talks, according to CNN’s account. (Meeting footage, CNN)

A new analysis cited by WSJ finds China’s uranium-enrichment capacity now exceeds civilian requirements. Harvard researcher Hui Zhang believes secretive facilities near Emeishan could support weapons production; Beijing says it maintains only the nuclear capabilities necessary for national security. (WSJ)

Patriot missile production faces a carbonised-rayon bottleneck: sole approved US processor Park Aerospace depends on limited French supply from ArianeGroup, WSJ reports. Park’s CEO expects an extra French line in 2028 and a proposed US factory around 2030; L3Harris is qualifying another source but gave no completion date. (WSJ)

EQUITIES:

Crypto futures tied to Anthropic’s stock market debut have fallen alongside artificial intelligence stocks, but they still imply a blockbuster valuation of about $1.7 trillion, well above the $1.4 trillion the company would be worth at the top of its proposed initial public offering range. (BBG)

Anthropic’s existing backers Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel and Altimeter plan to buy billions of dollars of shares in its IPO, Bloomberg reports. Altimeter is seeking $5bn. (BBG)

SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son said Wednesday that passing on Anthropic because he had already backed OpenAI was a mistake. “I wish I’d invested back then,” he told a Nikkei event in Tokyo. (FT)

OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Sales, combining a dedicated Sales plugin with more than 30 new or expanded partner plugins. Integrations cover CRM, prospecting, meeting notes, proposals and contracts, including Salesforce and HubSpot. (OpenAI)

Meta researcher Jason Wei announced he is leaving Meta’s TBD lab after a year to become Mercor’s chief scientist. (Jason Wei on X)

La Caisse is the leading bidder in advanced talks for a stake in Bain’s Bridge Data Centres, Reuters reported. The sale process targeted a $5bn valuation, but negotiations are non-exclusive and terms remain unsettled. (RTRS)

Tencent Holdings’s aggressive spending on AI has begun to stall profit growth, heightening the pressure on China’s most valuable company to reorganize its business to try and commercialize artificial intelligence. (BBG)

Micronics Japan is considering faster production-capacity expansion to meet Samsung and other chipmakers’ demand, including a new facility by 2030. (Nikkei Asia)

Rakuten Bank plunged 19% to its daily limit after its securities unit warned Tuesday of a possible client-data leak. Up to 11.25 million accounts face exposure of login IDs and client codes, though transaction credentials were not compromised. (BBG)

ASE Technology Holding and SPIL reached a multibillion-dollar Nvidia funding agreement for expanded Taiwan advanced packaging, with additional dedicated capacity expected by mid-2029. New lines span bumping, interposer fabrication, assembly and testing. (Nvidia)

TrendForce forecasts HBM4 prices of $3–5.5 per Gb in 2027, versus more than $2.05 this year, according to ZDNet Korea. (ZDNet Korea)

text:
✝️ PHYSICAL HEALING — TEN LIVES TO LIFT BEFORE GOD
November 18, 2026 | Praying for the Sick, Injured, and Recovering
📖 Psalm 147:3 (WEB)

“He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.”

Behind every diagnosis is a human life that cannot be reduced to a medical chart. Healing concerns more than survival. It concerns restored strength, freedom from suffering, opportunities reclaimed, and the dignity of every person created in God's image.

Today, we bring ten real people before the Lord.

🙏 1. ROBYN COFFIN — BREAST CANCER

Actress Robyn Coffin, known for Chicago Fire, publicly disclosed a breast cancer diagnosis in November 2026. Her medical team was planning surgery and recovery care.

OUR PRAYER:

Heavenly Father, surround Robyn with Your healing presence. Guide her surgeons, protect her through treatment, and restore every affected part of her body. Grant her courage when uncertainty rises, strength when treatment is exhausting, and renewed health in the days ahead. In Jesus' name, Amen.

🙏 2. GRANT KAWAHATSU — RARE BLOOD CANCER

Grant was diagnosed with polycythemia vera after severe breathing difficulties led doctors to discover fluid accumulation and a nearly collapsed lung. Following surgery and immunotherapy, he began preparing for a marathon to support cancer research.

OUR PRAYER:

Lord Jesus, sustain Grant's recovery. Protect his lungs, blood circulation, and remaining strength. Let treatment continue to control his disease. Transform his testimony into encouragement for others facing frightening diagnoses. Amen.

🙏 3. NATALIE LUCIANO — KIDNEY CANCER RECOVERY

A nurse practitioner and retired Army captain, Natalie unexpectedly discovered kidney cancer during an examination for appendicitis. Surgery successfully removed the affected portion of her kidney. She has been reported cancer-free.

OUR PRAYER:

Father, preserve Natalie's health and protect her remaining kidney function. May future examinations remain reassuring. Restore her endurance and bless her desire to help others through her experience. Amen.

🙏 4. JOHNNIE “DJ” JONES — HEART TRANSPLANT

Missouri freshman football player DJ Jones underwent heart transplant surgery in October 2026. His coach reported that the operation went well and that he was recovering.

OUR PRAYER:

Lord, protect DJ's transplanted heart. Guard against rejection, infection, and complications. Give his physicians wisdom in managing medication and rehabilitation. Restore his strength and lead him toward a fulfilling future. Amen.

🙏 5. BOBBY LARISA — RECOVERING AFTER HEART FAILURE

A 38-year-old former firefighter and father of four from Rhode Island, Bobby received a heart transplant after years of worsening cardiac disease. His community rallied around his family during recovery.

OUR PRAYER:

Merciful Father, strengthen Bobby's new heart and his entire body. Protect him throughout rehabilitation. Provide for his family financially and emotionally. May the man who devoted himself to rescuing others experience extraordinary care and restoration. Amen.

🙏 6. ISABELLA “BELLA” BONILLA — CHILDHOOD HEART DISEASE

Eight-year-old Bella spent more than fifteen months hospitalized before receiving a heart transplant in July 2026. She was subsequently able to return home.

OUR PRAYER:

Jesus, hold Bella close to Your heart. Protect her transplant, strengthen her growing body, and bless her with years of health and discovery. Give her family peace and comfort the donor family whose generosity made her surgery possible. Amen.

🙏 7. LILA SHAPIRO — LIFE-THREATENING BLOOD SUGAR DISORDER

Six-year-old Lila lives with glycogen storage disease type 1a. She requires carefully timed cornstarch doses throughout the day and night to prevent dangerous drops in blood sugar. A new gene therapy offers future hope.

OUR PRAYER:

Father, protect Lila's blood sugar and every delicate process sustaining her life. Preserve her through childhood and open the way to safe, effective treatment. Give her parents restful nights and freedom from constant fear. Amen.

🙏 8. MARLEY BERTHOUD — RARE GENETIC DISEASE

Marley, age eleven, lives with Bachmann-Bupp syndrome, a rare genetic disorder. Experimental treatment has helped her develop strength, communication, and movement, inspiring research that may benefit other children.

OUR PRAYER:

Lord, continue Marley's progress. Strengthen her muscles, protect her development, and expand her opportunities to communicate and participate in life. Bless the researchers whose discoveries may bring healing to many families. Amen.

🙏 9. EUGENIA PARIS — SPINAL CORD INJURY

University of Miami student Eugenia sustained a spinal cord injury in a crash that left her unable to walk. She underwent extensive rehabilitation and began preparing to participate in the New York City Marathon.

OUR PRAYER:

Jesus, bring healing to Eugenia's injured spinal cord. Strengthen her body, preserve her health, and increase her independence. Guide rehabilitation specialists and advance medical understanding of nerve repair. May every achievement open another possibility. Amen.

🙏 10. BROCK KELLY — SUDDEN PARALYSIS

Content creator Brock Kelly reportedly experienced paralysis from the waist down following a rare spinal cord injury associated with surfing in November 2026.

OUR PRAYER:

Heavenly Father, protect Brock from further injury and complications. Bring restoration wherever possible to damaged nerves and movement. Surround him with excellent medical care, patient encouragement, and the determination required for rehabilitation. Amen.

🕊️ A CLOSING PRAYER FOR PHYSICAL HEALING

Father of mercy,

We have spoken ten names, and You know countless others.

We pray for cancer patients awaiting results, children struggling to survive, people enduring chronic pain, those undergoing surgery, and families watching over loved ones in intensive care.

Give researchers discoveries, doctors discernment, nurses endurance, and caregivers compassion.

Where restoration is possible, let it flourish. Where suffering continues, provide relief, dignity, courage, and faithful companionship.

Teach us that prayer is not a substitute for loving action. Inspire us to visit, encourage, provide, support medical research, and help carry the practical burdens of those who suffer.

May our prayers become expressions of Your compassion, and may our compassion become evidence of Your love.

In the powerful and merciful name of Jesus Christ,

Amen.

text:
18 NOVEMBER 1916 AFTER 141 DAYS OF FIGHTING, THE BATTLE OF THE SOMME FINALLY CAME TO AN END. One hundred and ten years ago today, Field Marshal Sir Douglas Haig brought the British offensive on the Somme to a close.

The battle had begun on 1st July 1916. That first day remains the bloodiest in British Army history. Approximately 57,000 British casualties were recorded, including more than 19,000 men killed. Many soldiers had been told that the enormous preliminary artillery bombardment would destroy German defences. But when the infantry advanced, numerous German machine-gun positions remained intact. Whole units suffered devastating losses.

Among them were the famous Pals battalions; men who had enlisted together from the same towns, workplaces and communities. For families waiting at home, the consequences were unimaginable. But the Somme did not end after that first terrible day. Fighting continued throughout the summer and autumn. In the heat of July, soldiers advanced across devastated fields. By October and November, heavy rain had turned parts of the battlefield into a landscape of mud, shell holes and shattered trenches.

Men struggled through ground so waterlogged that movement itself could become exhausting and dangerous. On 15th September, during the Battle of Flers-Courcelette, the British introduced tanks into battle for the first time. These extraordinary machines offered a glimpse of future warfare, but the early tanks were mechanically unreliable and available in small numbers. They did not deliver the decisive breakthrough hoped for. When the offensive ended on 18th November, British and French forces had advanced in places by approximately seven miles. The German defensive system had been battered but not decisively broken... And the human cost was staggering.

The National Army Museum records approximately:
• 420,000 British Empire casualties
• 200,000 French casualties
• At least 450,000 German casualties
German casualty estimates vary considerably between historians.
These figures include men killed, wounded and missing; they are not figures for deaths alone. The original Allied objectives had included relieving pressure on the French army at Verdun, wearing down German forces and breaking through enemy defences.
The Somme did contribute to the attrition of German forces and the development of British military tactics.
But whether those gains justified such immense losses remains one of the most difficult and contested questions in First World War history.

For the soldiers who endured it, the Somme was not simply a military operation marked on a map. It was cold, fear, noise, exhaustion and grief. It was friends who never returned. It was letters sent home. It was families receiving telegrams that changed their lives forever. And it was an entire generation confronting the terrible reality of industrialised warfare.

Today, 110 years after the final day of the offensive, we remember the British, Commonwealth, French and German soldiers who died, and the countless lives altered by the battle. Their suffering must never become merely another statistic in a history book.

🕯️ We will remember them.
#LestWeForget #BattleOfTheSomme

Dr Lakhu Luhana Says Army Dominance Has Turned Balochistan into Fascist Colony at BNM Conference

Wednesday, 18 November, 2026 | #BNMConferences , 
#13NovBalochMartyrsDay , #BNMinGermany , #Girarun

https://t.co/xMlj3t3HBj

The chairman of the World Sindhi Congress has told a conference in Germany that the sacrifices of Baloch martyrs have transformed Baloch society and that the current situation in Balochistan amounts to a form of “fascist colonialism”.

Dr Lakhu Luhana, speaking at a Baloch National Movement (BNM) event in Hannover marking Baloch Martyrs’ Day, said the martyrs gave their lives so that their nation could live in freedom, peace and dignity on its own land. He described periods of subjugation as the darkest times in the history of nations, but said the martyrs showed that no people can be kept in chains indefinitely if they refuse to accept them.

He argued that the sacrifices have produced what he called a “magic” in Baloch society: the rise of a middle-class leadership and a significant role for women. He said thousands of women are now active in the struggle for rights and freedom, an internal liberation that would otherwise have taken decades or centuries.

Luhana rejected the description of the situation as mere internal colonialism. He said the phenomenon has changed form over time and that Balochistan is now under what he termed fascist colonialism driven by Punjabi chauvinism and the overwhelming dominance of the army. He claimed that politicians are not elected but employed by the military, that parliament and the judiciary have been hollowed out, and that the ruling elite is morally bankrupt.

He said the state’s economic model rests on the extraction of resources from oppressed nations and on foreign funds obtained by acting as a proxy. With those external sources weakening and Pakistan’s economy under severe strain, he argued, the military’s greed has deepened and it is now seeking to take almost everything that remains — land, minerals and water — from Balochistan and other regions. He cited reports of millions of acres of land being taken and mineral samples being offered for sale abroad.

Luhana linked the increased desperation of the state to a rise in enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, collective punishments and pressure on relatives of activists living abroad. He noted that international attention to human rights has diminished as global powers face their own problems. He also observed that struggles are growing among Baloch, Pashtuns, Sindhis and even in Pakistan-administered Kashmir because people see no other option for survival.

Quoting the late Sindhi leader G.M. Syed, he said consistent, honest work with clear strategy and commitment would eventually cause the system to make mistakes and weaken. He described the Baloch and Sindhi struggles as mutually reinforcing and said the martyrs of one nation are the martyrs of the other. He ended by expressing hope that freedom, dignity and peace would come sooner rather than later through continued commitment and strategy.

text:
A few years ago, a contract running down at Arsenal meant dread. Fans had learned to expect the worst, because the club had lost one key player after another: Robin van Persie to Manchester United, Cesc Fàbregas to Barcelona, Samir Nasri to Manchester City and Ashley Cole to Chelsea and other top players. It became almost a tradition. Bigger offers, more ambitious projects and the promise of major trophies elsewhere kept pulling the best players away, and Arsenal often felt like a stepping stone rather than a destination.

Today the picture is completely different. We no longer even checks when contracts expire. That's not because contracts have stopped mattering, but because the perception of the club has been transformed. Players now want to be at Arsenal, to be part of the project and to compete for trophies, rather than looking for the exit.

The change runs through everything: the mentality, the ambition, the project itself and, most importantly, the respect Arsenal command in world football. The club has gone from watching its best players leave to seeing them excited to commit their futures. This is a remarkable journey, and one that fans don't always appreciate enough. 

Thank you, Mikel Arteta.

text:
Through 13 strategic commodity lines outlined in his book, Organizing Land for National Economic Transformation, Gen. Salim Saleh advances a model that connects agricultural production to factories, manufacturing, employment and export markets, placing organized production at the centre of Uganda's industrialization ambitions.

Uganda's industrialization ambitions face a fundamental challenge: the country cannot build a competitive manufacturing economy if the factories it establishes cannot secure enough locally produced raw materials to operate consistently.

It is a challenge that goes beyond agricultural productivity. It concerns how land is organized, where commodities are produced, how farmers are connected to markets and whether industrial investments are deliberately matched with the productive capacity of surrounding communities.

This is the economic argument advanced by Gen. Salim Saleh, Chief Coordinator of Operation Wealth Creation @OWC_ug, in his book, Organizing Land for National Economic Transformation, co authored with Dr. Pascal Wathum Odoch.

Gen. Saleh identifies 13 strategic commodity lines that Uganda must deliberately organize and develop to establish a dependable agricultural supply base for its industries, expand value addition and increase export earnings.

The commodities are cotton, coffee, maize, rice, cassava, sugarcane, oilseeds, horticultural products, livestock, dairy, fisheries, forestry and tea.

His proposition is that these commodities should not be treated as isolated agricultural activities, but as interconnected economic value chains, with production areas deliberately organized around the industries that depend on their output.

Under this approach, regions with strong potential for particular commodities would be developed into specialied production zones and connected to processing facilities, storage infrastructure, transport networks and markets through organised commodity corridors.

The objective is to establish a direct relationship between what farmers produce and what industries require, ensuring that agricultural output has a clear commercial destination while factories have reliable access to raw materials.

Cotton provides one of the clearest illustrations of the industrial opportunity. Lango, Acholi, Busoga and West Nile as regions with potential for organised cotton production, which could support a much wider textile and garment manufacturing industry.

Rather than exporting cotton as a primary agricultural commodity, the proposed value chain would extend from cultivation and ginning to spinning, fabric production and garment manufacturing.

This would allow Uganda to capture more value at successive stages of production while creating employment for farmers, factory workers, transporters, designers and other participants in the textile industry.

Coffee presents a similar opportunity. Uganda's established production areas in Central, Eastern and Southwestern regions could be more deliberately connected to washing stations, roasting facilities and instant coffee processing plants. 

This would strengthen the country's capacity to supply international markets with processed and branded products, rather than relying predominantly on exports of raw or minimally processed beans.

The same thinking extends to food and industrial crops. Maize, rice and cassava can sustain milling, food manufacturing, starch production and animal feed industries. Sugarcane offers opportunities in sugar processing and the utilization of industrial by products, while oilseeds can supply edible oil refineries and related manufacturing enterprises.

In livestock and dairy, organized production would support abattoirs, meat-processing plants, leather industries and dairy factories. 
 They depend on improved breeding, veterinary services, commercial feed production, collection centres, cold storage and dependable transportation.

Horticulture and fisheries offer further opportunities in fruit and vegetable processing, preservation, packaging and export-oriented production, while forestry and tea can supply industries producing higher value goods from agricultural and natural resources.

What connects all 13 commodity lines is the intention to move Uganda from predominantly selling what it produces towards building industries around what it grows.

The urgency of this proposition is reflected in Uganda's own industrial performance. The Fourth National Development Plan (NDP IV), covering 2025/26 2029/30, reports that the country has established more than 2,263 agro-processing facilities, yet 40 per cent are non functional and more than half operate below capacity.

Tea factories operate below 60 per cent capacity on average, the country's nine largest dairy processors at 57 per cent, coffee processing facilities at approximately 40 per cent, maize mills at 46 per cent and fish processing facilities at below 30 per cent.

The national development plan identifies inadequate supplies and inconsistent quality of raw materials, weak value chain coordination, poor infrastructure, unreliable electricity and limited working capital among the factors contributing to this underperformance.

 It also highlights cases where processing infrastructure was established without sufficient consideration of the quantity and quality of agricultural production available to sustain it.

These figures expose a critical gap in Uganda's industrialization journey. Building processing infrastructure is only one part of the equation,  the production systems, supply networks and commercial arrangements that keep factories running are equally important.

Gen. Saleh's commodity corridor approach seeks to address this gap by making industrial planning inseparable from agricultural production planning. 

Instead of establishing factories and subsequently searching for raw materials, investment decisions would be guided by the productive potential of particular areas, the commodities they can supply and the industries that can sustainably process them.

This would also provide a stronger basis for directing investment towards irrigation, mechanization, electricity, rural roads, storage facilities and agricultural technology in the areas where they can generate the greatest economic returns.

For farmers, the implications are significant. Organized production can help households move away from uncertain markets and fragmented selling arrangements towards more predictable commercial relationships with processors and other buyers. Cooperatives and farmer organisations can strengthen this process by aggregating produce, facilitating access to inputs and machinery, improving bargaining power and connecting producers to financing and larger markets.

The opportunities also extend beyond the farm. As production becomes more organized and processing industries expand, demand grows for transport, warehousing, packaging, equipment maintenance, logistics, financial services and other enterprises that support the agricultural value chain.

 These activities create additional employment and business opportunities, particularly for young people.

The proposed commodity organization model reinforces an important dimension of that mandate: farmers must not only produce more, but produce commercially, at the required quality and scale, with access to reliable buyers and industries capable of adding value to their output.

It also complements the wider national development agenda, including the Parish Development Model and the agro industrialization programme under NDP IV, which emphasise commercial production, value addition, stronger market access and improved coordination across agricultural value chains.

However, achieving this ambition will require deliberate execution. Commodity zones must be supported by credible production data, clear market demand, appropriate infrastructure, financing, research, extension services and strong participation from private investors. 
Farmers must also remain central to the arrangements, benefiting from the markets and economic opportunities created around their production.

Ultimately, Gen. Saleh's proposition challenges Uganda to reconsider how it measures the economic value of its agricultural resources. The question is no longer simply how much land the country has or how much agricultural produce it can grow, but how effectively those resources can be organized to support industries, create employment and generate sustainable wealth.

The next phase of Uganda's industrial transformation will not be determined by factories alone. It will depend on how effectively the country organises its land, mobilises its farmers and connects production to industry. That is the foundation upon which agricultural potential can become industrial capacity and national wealth.

7 Secrets of Amla Navami in Vedic Astrology

1. Worship the Living Vishnu-Lakshmi Tree: On Kartik Shukla Navami, Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi specially reside in the Amla tree. Worshipping it (with water, flowers, roli, akshat, and a ghee lamp) while chanting  Om Namo Narayanaya or Om Hrim Shrim Lakshmiye Namah draws eternal 'Akshaya Punya' (imperishable merit).

2. Eat Sattvic Food Under the Amla Tree: Sitting and eating a pure meal under the tree is considered equal to receiving direct 'prasada' from Vishnu. It cleanses sins, balances the three 'doshas', strengthens 'Prana', and is said to remove planetary afflictions related to health and longevity.

3. Offer Amla to Surya: Amla is deeply linked to the Sun (vitality, soul power, father). Offering Amla pieces in water while chanting 'Om Bhaskaraya Namah' pacifies weak Sun, improves confidence, eyesight, and authority in the chart.

4. Perform Parikrama (Circumambulation) : Walking around the Amla tree 7, 11, 21, or 108 times while remembering Vishnu opens the flow of Dharma and Artha. It is especially powerful for removing obstacles caused by Rahu-Ketu or Pitra Dosha.

5. Give Akshaya Dana: Charity of Amla, food, grains, clothes, or money done on this day never diminishes. It creates lasting Lakshmi Yoga -like results and is believed to erase even heavy karmic debts.

6. Strengthen Shukra & Family Happiness: Offering white flowers, sugar, and rice near the tree while chanting Shukra mantras or praying for marital harmony and children pacifies Venus and brings sweetness in relationships and progeny bliss.

7. Align with the Bright Fortnight Energy: Kartik Shukla Paksha is the waxing phase of growth and light. Navami carries the energy of completion and protection. Actions taken with pure intention on this day (especially under the Amla) multiply in power and stay with you across lifetimes — the true meaning of Akshaya.

These practices work best when done with a clean body, calm mind, and sincere bhavana (feeling).

"I NEED YOUR HELP. MY NAME IS HEYAM. HELP ME TO LIVE

Hello to the free world, I'm Hiyam from Gaza. This is the sixth war I've faced, preceded by five others, and I'm here to raise funds for myself and my family. Please take a moment to read about the tragedy that has befallen me and my family in this ongoing genocide. I feel ashamed that this situation has forced me to ask for help. My mother and father dedicated their lives to ensuring a decent life for us and building a large, beautiful home for us and our grandchildren, after spending forty years working tirelessly and serving the community. My mother, as the principal of a UNRWA school, and my father, as an Arabic teacher, saved up until they built our five-story house, with each apartment measuring 190 square meters on a 500-square-meter plot of land. They felt it was important for their grandchildren to have a large garden so they could play and release their energy under the suffocating siege of the Gaza Strip. Then the war came and destroyed our home. They left us with not a single room to shelter us. The building, with its distinctive color, is no more; it's just a pile of rubble. We are now homeless and scattered, and a few clothes are not enough in this bitter cold. They didn't even let my 70-year-old mother and 79-year-old father spend the rest of their lives in their home, the home they suffered so much for.

We became at the mercy of landlords, living in rented accommodation. We were displaced twelve times, each time by the Jews or by merciless landlords. In both cases, we were forced out. They demanded exorbitant sums, exploiting our need for shelter and the war. We fled our home under heavy fire. I'll never forget the amount of fire that poured through the windows from the intense shelling, nor will I forget the last prayer I did in our house. We left without clothes, food, bedding, medicine, or diapers because of the heavy bombardment. We didn't know where to go. We went to the Red Crescent hospital, but it was overcrowded with displaced people, and we couldn't find a single empty space. After hours of searching, we left, crying in the street, not knowing where to go. We were forced to go to relatives and stayed for a month. Then, friends helped us with just two mattresses and two blankets, which we took and fled to Mawasi al-Qarara on January 1, 2024. The place was frightening; people were afraid to live there, and it was very close to danger. We rented a room without a bathroom for $500. There was no kitchen, no water for drinking or use, and it was bitterly cold. We didn't have warm clothes in such cold weather, and the sea winds were strong. We were returning from the hospital after two days because my sister’s sons were suffering from dehydration and were in bad condition. We were very exhausted, and the children were crying. There was no electricity or light. It was a night like a scene from a miserable horror movie! We lived there for five months despite the cold, and we all suffered from respiratory problems due to the cold that lasted for a year until we recovered. There were days when 14 members of my family slept in a 3x4 meter space because of the storms. Also, gunboats would come and fire shots, and I miraculously survived once, Elhamdullah. On the night of my sister’s son birthday, February 22, 2024, he was sick, and we had prepared ourselves to take him to the doctor when we were surprised by the sudden entry of tanks in a special operation. They surrounded us for eight hours, which was the longest and most miserable night of my life. They killed our neighbors, arrested the men, tortured the women, destroyed the cars, and a tank ran over our beautiful young neighbor, who was completely paralyzed. She remained in a coma for a whole year, living only on machines, and then she died on the same date of the following year. And we miraculously survived.

After 5 months, the owner of the room told us that he wanted to rent it to an international organization. We had to leave because they would pay him a huge amount. Elhamdullah and then my friend, we found an apartment and moved to it. During that period, we suffered from famine, and my sister and I contracted hepatitis A. After we recovered, we became dehydrated due to hunger. We used to roam the streets looking for sanitary pads, milk for my young nephew, and one kilo of flour. We were soaking and kneading the pasta instead of flour. I used to go to sleep crying because of my intense longing for the smell of bread. A loaf of bread was a very distant dream for me during that period.

Two months later, the Jews asked us to evacuate the area. We didn't have a tent or anywhere to go, so we moved to our relatives' tent in Al-Mawasi. It was 3x3 meters, and three families lived inside. We were 11 people in a small space. It was a tragedy; sewage was flowing from the bathroom attached to us below us, and we couldn't sleep at night. After a week, the Jews approached us and ordered us to evacuate the camp, but we made a collective decision not to leave, and we actually stayed. Transportation costs are very high, and at that time we had spent everything we had in the last displacement, and we didn't have anything to make us leave again...

Red bumps are covering our bodies, especially my sister's children, due to the intense heat.

After the Jews withdrew from the area and the area where the apartment is located, we returned to the apartment and stayed for a while. Then the Jews returned after several months and asked us to evacuate the area. At that time I was at the clinic with my sick father and I returned to my place of residence quickly. I told my mother and tried to collect what we could of mattresses and clothes and we moved to Al-Mawasi again.

We stayed in a tent for a while, but my father and mother's health was very bad. My father fell into the sewage pit that followed the bathroom in the tent twice, as my father's eyesight is weak and he cannot see well. My mother needs to have two joints implanted in her knees. She cannot walk in the sand, so she fell and stayed in bed for two months. We were then forced to look for a house in Deir al-Balah, the only city that the Jews left undamaged, and perhaps we would find a place there. We found a room and a bathroom and moved there.

We lived there for two months in appalling conditions. The bathroom was infested with worms. It was a famine, and we didn't have a morsel of bread, a kilo of lentils, or even a kilo of rice. We would buy a kilo of lentils because it was cheaper than a kilo of flour, grind it, knead it, and bake it like bread to stave off our hunger. We paid $500 in rent in cash, and the withdrawal cash commission was 48-50%. I went to doctors constantly, every day, for my father's sake. Hunger had ravaged his body during that time; he couldn't walk, and his blood pressure was so low he could barely see due to malnutrition. I remember one time I went to a clinic and told them my father was sick and asked them to check his blood pressure. They found he was slowly dying, so they gave him an IV drip and a small bag of nutrient solution. My father was starving and tried to feed me some of it because I was hungry like him, but I refused because it wasn't enough for him. I felt so oppressed that they could see my father dying of hunger while they had large quantities of nutrient solution meant for those suffering from famine, yet they still chose to give it to their friends in front of me, who were healthy, let my father go home with nothing to eat. They told me to make him a bowl of lentils, and I told them that we had left him half a bowl of lentils for breakfast that morning before I brought him here. We all went hungry without breakfast, yet they still let us go back without a single small bag of nutritious food ..💔

Also, one of the hardest days of my life was when my sister’s Yahya was martyred, my sister Aziza. He was sitting next to her inside the tent, reminiscing about his beautiful memories. He told his mother that he longed to eat apples and laughed. Then he went outside to sit in front of the tent, and a bullet from a quadcopter entered his neck and killed him. The news was devastating for my grieving sister. We went and took her, her husband, and her children to our place of residence at that time in Deir al-Balah. She was unable to stand because she had cancer and had received a dose of chemotherapy two days prior, and she was not well. We wanted to feed them, but we had no food. We only had half a loaf of bread and half a plate of lentil stew with rice, which we brought and placed in front of them, feeling ashamed of what we offered because they were exhausted from crying so much, and we had nothing to feed them. Everyone got up, hungry...

That night, my sister and I tried to run after the aid trucks to get one kilo of flour to feed them. The situation was very dangerous, everyone was carrying a weapon, thousands of people were scrambling for every one kilo, but we failed and returned empty-handed.

Two months after we arrived, the people from the north moved to the south. There was nowhere to rent, not even a place to pitch a tent. The south was very crowded, and rent prices had skyrocketed. The landlord ordered us to vacate the house in the morning and rented it to displaced people from the north for $1000. That day, we wandered the streets crying, searching for a place to shelter us. We found an abandoned place inhabited by dogs and cats, unfit for human habitation, so we rented it for $600 cash. The cash commission had increased to 50-57%. The place was very bad, and the uneven ground caused my mother and father to fall three times and be hospitalized. We stayed there for two months, and during those two months, the landlords subjected us to insults and abuse. They prevented us from leaving, from receiving guests, and from the children playing. Then they evicted us so they could rent it to displaced people from the north for an even higher price.

We moved into a room and bathroom that we rented for $500. On the first day, after we moved our things, the landlady told us that the rental period was only 3 months. Then we moved to an apartment where we have been for the past 6 months, paying $500 in rent monthly in cash. The second day we moved into the apartment, my uncle passed away, and people came to offer their condolences to my father for his brother. Unfortunately, the landlord asked us to leave, saying that he did not want us to receive guests or even leave. However, we had signed a rental agreement, and for the past 6 months we have been suffering with him. He harasses us and steals from us repeatedly, and we have all become depressed, unfortunately. He asked us to increase the rent, and now that the contract has expired, he told us to vacate the house. We are forced to move, but we do not know where we will go, as I have been looking for a place to rent for a month and a half and have not found anything yet.

Our bodies are disfigured by insects, and there is no cure, or if one were available, it would be very expensive.

Often we are forced to drink unclean water due to the lack of available water.

For me, after nine years of trying to leave Gaza, I was ready to travel on October 15, 2023. I obtained a visa to visit Dubai to look for work, achieve self-sufficiency, and support my family, especially my sister Khadija, a single mother of two with no income due to the scarcity of job opportunities in Gaza. However, war broke out, and I couldn't travel because the Rafah border crossing was closed. Unfortunately, my visa became invalid because the entry date expired on November 17, 2023. Little did I know that the suitcases I had bought to fulfill a dream I had nurtured for so many years would be used to escape death and displacement. Everything I worked for for years was lost in the blink of an eye. I spent all my time in front of my laptop, working as a graphic designer and mobile app developer, and now I am without my laptops, which I lost in the bombing of my house, and without work. I am suffering and feeling psychological pressure about it to the point that I developed alopecia. I have been cut off from programming since the beginning of the war. I dreamed of becoming a successful mobile app developer, but the war took away my dream. I used to lose sleep at night and work for this dream. If I wanted to own a laptop with average specifications to start over, that would mean I need $3000! Despite this, Elhamdullah.

These days I can travel by get obtain the necessary travel clearance that costs $30,000 per person. This means that if I wanted to travel with my parents, my sister and her two children, we would need $180,000 to be able to cross the Egyptian border without any other costs.

I lost my beautiful car, which I loved and owned for eight years. I wasn't thinking of replacing or repairing it because I'm very attached to my things, like they're my little child who grew up with me, but unfortunately...

Now I miss it so much and need it because my parents can't walk long distances and transportation is difficult. It's not just her that I've lost, but all my belongings, and I hope to receive compensation from Allah.

Regarding our physical health: My mother suffers from chronic high blood pressure and gout. She needs replacements her two knee, a slipped disc, cervical spondylosis, and cervical spine deformity, and can only walk with a cane. My father has vision problems due to hunger and the intense grief he experienced after seeing our house bombed. He also has hearing problems, prostatitis, and developed tremors during the war. He also has kidney problems. My sister suffers from rheumatoid arthritis due to stress, and one of her five-year-old children has developed gray hair due to the trauma of the bombing. For me, In addition to alopecia, I suffer from a complete tear in one of my shoulder tendons, and my condition has worsened with carrying water long distances. I need continuous physical therapy. We urgently need monthly medication for both physical and mental health.

As for basic necessities, they are unavailable. Since October 7, 2023, we have been spending our nights in complete darkness. We don't have a battery to light our place at night, as each one costs between $2,000 and $3,000. We all struggle to obtain the basic necessities of life, such as rent, water, diapers, sanitary pads, medicine, milk for my sister's children, flour, tissues, and gas for cooking. Most of the time, we cook with firewood. As for electricity, it has been cut off since the war began. We travel long distances, walking to try to charge our phones, knocking on doors of houses with solar panels to charge them... Sometimes we go without phones for 20 days. We don't know the fate of the rest of my siblings who are suffering from poverty because of the war, or my family and friends, many of whom have died and whom I have lost in this genocide.

Whether it's a donation or simply sharing this campaign with your network, every single one matters. Your support means more to me than words can express, and I am grateful for any help you can offer as I work to rebuild my life.

Salam👋

text:
The beach was quieter than they expected.

A few families were gathered near the water, and several couples walked along the shore. The sun was bright, but the breeze made the weather comfortable.

Dunk removed his sandals and walked towards the water.

Joong followed a little behind.

For a while, neither said anything.

They simply walked.

The waves moved gently against their feet, leaving small trails of foam on the sand.

Dunk stopped and looked towards the horizon.

“It’s pretty.”

“Yeah.”

Joong looked at him instead.

Dunk noticed.

“What?”

“Nothing.”

“Why are you looking at me?”

Joong smiled.

“You’re pretty too.”

Dunk rolled his eyes.

“You’re still like this.”

“Like what?”

“Always saying things.”

Joong laughed.

“Can’t help it.”

Dunk shook his head, but he was smiling.

They continued walking until they found a quiet spot to sit.

Dunk took a bottle of water from his bag and offered it to Joong.

Joong accepted it.

“Thank you.”

They sat side by side, leaving a little space between them.

After a while, Dunk spoke.

“I haven’t been here since we broke up.”

Joong looked towards him.

“Me neither.”

Dunk nodded.

“I thought it might feel strange coming back.”

“Does it?”

“A little.”

Joong lowered his eyes.

“I’m sorry.”

Dunk turned towards him.

“Joong.”

“Sorry. I know.”

Dunk smiled faintly.

“You don’t have to apologise every time we talk about the past.”

Joong chuckled.

“I’m trying.”

“I know.”

Dunk looked back at the sea.

“Actually, I think I wanted to come here because I didn’t want this place to feel sad anymore.”

Joong listened.

“I remember our trip. I remember being happy. I also remember feeling like I wasn’t really there with you sometimes.”

Joong’s chest tightened.

“But I don’t want to keep remembering it that way.”

Dunk turned towards him.

“I want to remember the good parts too.”

Joong nodded.

“You should.”

Dunk smiled.

“We did have a good time, didn’t we?”

“We did.”

Joong paused.

“And I’m sorry I made you feel like those memories belonged to someone else.”

Dunk looked at him for a moment.

Then he nodded.

“Thank you.”

They returned their attention to the sea.

Joong didn’t try to say anything else.

He was beginning to understand that sometimes, the best thing he could offer Dunk was the space to speak without feeling like he needed to comfort him afterwards.

⸻

They had lunch at a small restaurant near the beach.

Dunk ordered seafood fried rice, while Joong chose noodles.

Halfway through the meal, Dunk reached across the table and stole a piece of Joong’s food.

Joong looked at him.

“Excuse me?”

“What?”

“That’s mine.”

“I just wanted to try.”

“You have your own.”

Dunk smiled innocently.

“Yours looks better.”

Joong shook his head.

“Some things never change.”

Dunk laughed.

And for a moment, Joong saw the boy he had fallen in love with.

The one who used to steal food from his plate. The one who would send him ridiculous videos in the middle of the night. The one who laughed with his whole face.

But this time, Joong didn’t mistake that familiarity for permission to return to the way things were.

He simply smiled and pushed his plate slightly closer.

“Here. Take some more.”

Dunk looked at him.

“Really?”

“Yeah.”

“Thank you.”

Joong watched him take another bite.

It was such an ordinary thing.

And he was grateful for it.

⸻

After lunch, they stopped by a small shop selling souvenirs.

Dunk was looking through a display of keychains when Joong noticed a little sunflower charm.

He picked it up.

For a second, he considered buying it.

Then he remembered everything that had happened with the flowers.

He remembered how Dunk had once shown him a bouquet with so much excitement, only to have that excitement quietly diminished by a careless comment.

Joong put the keychain back.

Dunk turned around.

“What were you looking at?”

“Nothing.”

Dunk glanced at the display.

“Sunflower?”

Joong nodded.

“Yeah.”

Dunk picked up the charm himself.

“It’s cute.”

text:
Greg’s office smelled like new carpet and cheap coffee. He’d laid out two documents and a pen, aligned to the edge of the desk.

“I want to be upfront,” he said. “The building’s going to be sold. Doesn’t have to be a bad thing for you.”

“What’s the offer?”

“Fifteen thousand dollars. Moving costs, first and last at a new place, everything. All you do is sign Addendum C and agree to be out by March 2027.”

Fifteen thousand dollars. Security deposit, movers, first and last with two kids—my stomach turned over.

I thought about Mr. Henderson, who thought he’d done something wrong. I thought about the doorframe at home, two sets of pencil marks that would end in a kitchen I wouldn’t live in.

“I’ll think about it,” I said.

I went home and didn’t think about it for one second. I printed page three, circled the heading in red, and knocked on every door that night. I didn’t mention the spreadsheet. I just held up the page and said, “Read this before you sign. Call Indiana Legal Services if you have questions.”

By Sunday, four neighbors had contacted the landlord to dispute their signatures and request that the addendum be withdrawn. Mrs. Davis in 4C brought me a casserole and said, “I almost signed. Thank you for coming by.”

The buyer’s November 30 deadline passed without the required 14 signatures. On December 2, 2026, the deal fell apart.

On December 5, Greg sent a final email with no emoji.

Please disregard Addendum C. Your lease remains in effect as originally signed.

The building sold in January anyway, to a smaller buyer who didn’t care about the paperwork. The new owner’s lawyer called me in February to ask what it would take.

I told him my lease runs through March 2028.

Mr. Henderson moved out last week, to his daughter’s place in Fort Wayne. I helped him carry boxes down. I read every page of his new paperwork out loud before he signed it.

text:
At 18, Chris Webber was the most famous college player in America, and he wasn't allowed to earn a dollar.
A booster later said he gave him $280,000 anyway.
Michigan paid for it. The NCAA got its money back.

Receipts: No. 1 pick in 1993. $178 million in NBA salary. Five All-Star games, Hall of Fame in 2021.
His legal cut of the Fab Five boom: ZERO.

In the video below, the money talk nobody gives you. "A lot of times you'll get cold money. Like, here you go, stack, open up a restaurant." Then: "This is the mistake I ran into."
Then the baggy shorts. Where he grew up, tight clothes meant you were broke. Michigan turned that into a national look.

1993 title game. Down two, 11 seconds left, he calls a timeout Michigan doesn't have. Technical foul. North Carolina wins.
Priciest timeout in college history. The real bill came later.

A Detroit booster named Ed Martin told investigators about the $280,000. Webber denied it to a grand jury, then pleaded guilty in 2003 to criminal contempt.

In 2002 Michigan forfeited more than 100 wins, took down four banners, including both Fab Five Final Fours, and returned $450,000 to the NCAA, the money from two Final Four runs. The school cut ties with him for 10 years.
The players got erased from the record book. The NCAA got its check back.

The NBA paid him the legal way. In 2007 the 76ers bought out his deal, reportedly for around $36 million, and days later he signed with Detroit.
The Timeout Tycoon finally found a loophole: getting paid to leave.

In 2021 he launched a $100 million cannabis fund with a New York asset manager, aimed at minority entrepreneurs.
"I'm just trying to make money and help people," he says.
At 18, that sentence got the banners taken down.

Hypothetical: you're 18, the most famous player in college basketball, and everyone around you is selling your look. A booster offers cash. Take it, or play for free?
