Millworks Technologies H1 FY27 Concall Highlights:

👉H1 FY27 & Future Outlook :
▫️FY27 revenue to cross ₹200 Cr; target not revised
💠Backed by the order book; revenue has crossed ₹50 Cr including October
💠Aim to dispatch ₹30–40 Cr each in November and December; Q4 to be the larger quarter
💠Business is H2-weighted; ~70% of FY26 revenue from operations came in H2
💠Orders worth ~₹30 Cr executed in September were billed in October, so the revenue falls in H2 FY27
💠A large Indian defence order planned for H1 moved to H2 as customer and regulatory approvals took longer; no order has been cancelled
💠Remaining H2 deliveries are mostly export projects, not Indian defence
💠Management denied commentary on an earlier 247cr revenue figure for FY27.

▫️Receivables and the auditor's qualified opinion:
💠Majority (~70%) of the receivables is held up in one Indian defence order for an investee company, delivered in March; electronic warfare parts, around 17 inspections across the country
💠Qualification is due to uncertainty on completion of that defence order, with Army receipts and documents pending, and receivable days beyond 180
💠Auditors visited the facility and saw the inventory; purchase orders and project documents were shared
💠Indian defence cycle is typically 8–12 months; Millworks will not take this much Indian defence exposure again

▫️Margins to improve as deferred revenue is recognised and new capacity is utilised
💠Build-to-spec work earns ~3–5% higher margin than build-to-print

▫️Receivables: majority expected to be received in Q3 FY27, with the large defence-order amount expected in the first or second week of December
💠Management will announce the receipt through the exchange

▫️H1 FY27 financials: revenue from operations ₹17.37 Cr; total income ₹18.11 Cr vs ₹45.77 Cr in H1 FY26
💠Gross margin ~37% vs ~38% in H2 FY26, with higher raw material prices on geopolitical disruption
💠Raw material ₹10.92 Cr; employee cost ₹4.46 Cr; other expenses ₹0.93 Cr
💠EBITDA ₹1.81 Cr (10.00% margin) vs ₹20.65 Cr in H1 FY26
💠Finance cost ₹1.81 Cr; depreciation ₹1.46 Cr; PBT ₹(1.46) Cr
💠Net loss ₹1.83 Cr vs PAT of ₹12.48 Cr in H1 FY26; EPS ₹(1.24) vs ₹10.38
💠Loss is operating leverage: fixed costs ran in full and people were added ahead of new capacity, while revenue moved to October
💠Inventory rose to ₹28.34 Cr from ₹11.47 Cr in March, all in finished goods and WIP waiting to be billed

▫️FY28: targeting 60–70% YoY revenue growth
💠First article samples made this year convert to production orders next year
💠Shift from build-to-print to build-to-spec, with more assemblies and sub-assemblies, for better margins
💠Build-to-spec expected to overtake build-to-print within ~2 years; mix to move towards 50:50 first

▫️Segment order of importance: defence, then rail, then aerospace, then semiconductor machinery parts
💠Aim to take aerospace ahead of rail

▫️Defence strategy: more focus on export defence, which brings advances and clear payment timing
💠Indian defence will not be dropped; the share of Indian defence will be balanced going forward

▫️Tailwinds: indigenisation push and rising global demand for precision components from India

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Order book ₹230 Cr (Nov 2026), 1.55x FY26 revenue
💠Includes a new ₹111 Cr export order from an Israeli defence sector company, the largest single order in company history

▫️₹111 Cr export order:
💠Scope: machined and sheet metal parts, bought-out items, assemblies and sub-assemblies
💠First article samples in 3 months; first development takes 6 months; full execution 12–14 months, i.e. by Q4 FY28

▫️IPO proceeds: ₹160.34 Cr fresh issue
💠Working capital: ₹61.94 Cr used of ₹81.50 Cr, mainly paying suppliers for the large defence programme, supplier advances for H2 materials and inventory build
💠Machinery: ₹28.73 Cr spent of ₹61.03 Cr earmarked
💠₹59.03 Cr held in fixed deposits and bank accounts, to be used as per the offer document

▫️Unit 4 expansion (Nelamangala):
💠27 of 52 new machines installed; installation and commissioning in stages; balance machines arrive in Dec 2026 and Jan 2027
💠Machining capacity to rise 1.75x post expansion, enabling more complex high-precision jobs
💠Anodizing plant operational in Jan 2027, giving end-to-end in-house solutions; Nadcap certification to follow in Jul–Aug 2027
💠All four manufacturing units operational

▫️Semiconductor machinery parts:
💠Working with two large customers, approvals complete; current supplies are small
💠Needs a dedicated clean-room facility, in process; to be ready around Jan–Feb 2027 (Q4 FY27), after which the opportunity will be pursued

▫️Aerospace tier 1 qualification:
💠Currently tier 2, supplying to large aerospace companies via Bangalore and Hyderabad players
💠Process audits by major aerospace companies under way; next audit in Feb 2027, with a large European aerospace company expected to clear and give trial orders
💠French tooling company projects to convert into orders in 2027, a major part of aero tooling assemblies and sub-assemblies

▫️Build-to-spec capability:
💠Metal 3D printing centre of excellence with Markforged (US); prototypes within ~4 weeks of concept design vs more than 3 months earlier
💠Design software and scanning facility added; prototypes billed as part of design; 3–6 months from prototype to production
💠Two Israeli customers and one German customer, on build-to-print for 3–5 years, have moved to build-to-spec

▫️R&D projects:
💠German customer: complete assembly (private label); design done, prototype ready, field trials in ~3 months; the customer bears the entire R&D cost
💠IC engine and jet engine projects: longer cycle, cost borne by the company; revenue impact in ~2 years
💠R&D budget not disclosed

▫️New partnerships and subsidiary:
💠Vidhwan Aeronautics made a subsidiary for aero engine components
💠MoU with TridenTech to co-develop UAV engines

▫️Certifications:
💠AS9100 Rev D for all four factories, valid till May 2027
💠IRIS (rail) certification for one plant targeted May 2027, to open orders in Europe and the US
💠EN welding certification: welders being trained

👉Q&A :

▫️Export receivables and terms:
💠Substantial amounts received in October and first week of November; balance to be closed by first week of December
💠Exports to a specific European country now carry 30% advance with the PO, roughly in line with the raw material share of 40–45% of cost
💠Payment now tied to 30–45 days from invoice date, not delivery; all shipments ex-works
💠Rail customers across ~12 countries, 6–7 years of association, no payment delays and no advances

▫️Investment in Quickpay (defence drone maker):
💠~8% stake taken when it held an order of ~960 loitering munition drones; Millworks supplies components
💠Advances are paid for components that must be bought in Quickpay's own name under its defence licence (GPS and electronics)
💠No further investment decided; will consider support for its Indian Army projects once receivables are cleared

👉 Others :
▫️Balance sheet: net worth ₹232.79 Cr; debt to equity 0.15x; cash higher than debt

▫️FY26: revenue from operations ₹148.77 Cr, EBITDA ₹56.65 Cr (36.93% margin), PAT ₹36.38 Cr
💠Defence 69.43% and railways 23.65% of FY26 revenue; exports 27.47%, to 9 countries

On November 18, 2026, Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a 22-year-old alleged Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander carrying a ₹15 lakh bounty, was killed in an encounter with Indian security forces in Kulgam.

But how did an ordinary carpenter become a wanted militant?

From Carpenter to Terror Suspect

Lateef, a resident of Kulgam, reportedly worked as a carpenter before abandoning his education and joining Lashkar-e-Taiba in November 2025.

According to police accounts, he was influenced by militant Zakir Ahmad Ganai. Investigators also linked him to the Kashmir Revolutionary Army (KRA), described by security agencies as a Lashkar-linked front.

Lashkar-e-Taiba, the Pakistan-based terrorist organisation responsible for the 2008 Mumbai attacks, has long been accused of supporting armed militancy in Kashmir.

A Trail of Blood and Allegations

Lateef was suspected of involvement in several attacks:

- 𝐉𝐮𝐥𝐲 22, 2026: 𝐊𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐟 𝐚 𝐩𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐧 𝐀𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐧𝐚𝐠.
- 𝐉𝐮𝐥𝐲 31, 2026: 𝐊𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐰𝐨 𝐦𝐢𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐊𝐮𝐥𝐠𝐚𝐦.
- 𝐍𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 11, 2026: 𝐀𝐭𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐨𝐧 𝐚 𝐂𝐑𝐏𝐅 𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐣𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐥.

These allegations were reported by investigators but were not established through a completed criminal trial.

His Final Hours

On November 16, his associate Umar Nisar Dar was reportedly killed during an encounter, while Lateef escaped.

Two days later, security forces surrounded Lateef inside a mosque in Kulgam's Jangalpora area.

Police reportedly offered him an opportunity to surrender through a video call. According to officials, he refused and opened fire.

The encounter ended with his death. Authorities said the mosque remained unharmed.

Who Is Glorifying Terrorists in Kashmir?

One of the most troubling aspects of militancy is the propaganda that attempts to portray armed extremists as heroes or martyrs.

Militant sympathisers and extremist propaganda networks have historically used emotional tributes, photographs, slogans, and social media narratives to romanticise violence.

However, there is no independently verified evidence identifying specific Kashmiris or organisations glorifying Lateef following his death. Such accusations should not be directed at the wider Kashmiri population without proof.

The Unanswered Question

India's Home Minister Amit Shah described Lateef as Kashmir's last known active local Lashkar terrorist.

But eliminating one militant does not automatically dismantle the networks that recruit, radicalise, finance, or shelter extremists.

The deeper battle is against the ideology that turns young men into militants and the propaganda that attempts to turn their deaths into symbols of heroism.

Kashmir deserves peace, not another generation sacrificed to terrorism.

text:
One person has been taken into custody in connection with the November 11 arson attack on the Gadsden Islamic Society mosque in Gadsden, Alabama, the FBI's Birmingham Field Office and Gadsden Police announced. Surveillance footage shows a masked individual in gray clothing and a hooded sweatshirt approaching the mosque's entrance and throwing a lit incendiary device that started a fire. Authorities said the arrest followed tips from the public. The suspect's identity and charges have not been released, and police have not said whether they are treating the attack as a hate crime.

The mosque was empty at the time and no one was injured. A rug outside the entrance burned, but the fire was put out before it could spread. Yousef Al Abbasi, a co-founder of the Gadsden Islamic Society, said the imam's wife spotted the flames from across the street and rushed over with her husband and child to put out the fire. The mosque called the attack an assault on Alabama's Muslim community and on everyone's right to religious freedom, and urged state leaders to condemn it.

The FBI had offered a reward of up to $20,000 for information leading to an arrest and conviction, and the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) offered a further $10,000. Gadsden Mayor Craig Ford condemned the attack and thanked investigators. The arson comes amid a rise in attacks on mosques across the US, including a July fire at the Northeast Philadelphia Islamic Center, where the suspect now faces federal civil rights charges.

Today's Corn Belt News

Published: Wednesday, November 18, 2026

Crop Progress Snapshot The 2026 U.S. soybean harvest is functionally complete while late corn combining pushes toward the finish line, according to Monday afternoon's USDA NASS report for the week ending November 15. National corn harvest progress advanced to 88% complete nationwide, trailing 2 percentage points behind last year's 90% pace and 4 points behind the five year average of 92%. 

Top producer Iowa continues to lag historical norms at 84% harvested (11 points behind its five year average), while Ohio reached 80% complete following localized rain delays.

National soybean harvest progress hit 96% complete nationwide, running 3 percentage points ahead of last year and 1 point ahead of the 95% five year average. Minnesota and North Dakota joined southern states at 100% finished, while Ohio reached 97% and Iowa neared full completion. 

Concurrently, winter wheat seeding for the 2027 crop reached 92% complete nationwide, with emergence at 82% and quality ratings jumping 4 points on the week to 53% good to excellent.

Weather and Outlook Warmer weather across much of the central Midwest is creating favorable conditions to wrap up remaining harvest operations and late fall fieldwork. However, forecasters are tracking two approaching storm systems expected to bring scattered showers, locally heavy rain, and early snow across parts of the Northern Plains and Upper Midwest. 

While the incoming moisture will temporarily park combines in northern tiers, it provides welcome late season soil moisture recharge for newly emerged winter wheat stands.

Markets and Prices Grain traders on the Chicago board are balancing final harvest receipts against ongoing export demand and processing margins. December corn futures (/ZC) are trading at 444'0 (444.00 cents per bushel), easing slightly as commercial harvest supplies move toward completion. 

January soybeans (/ZS) sit at 1221'6 (1221.75 cents per bushel for the Jan '27 contract), holding steady amid domestic crush demand and tariff uncertainties. 

Wheat futures show December KC HRW (/KE) at 628'0, Chicago SRW (/ZW) at 587'4, and Minneapolis Spring Wheat (/MWE) at 639'6. Interior basis bids remain closely tied to local elevator storage capacity as bins fill up.

Policy and Farm Bill Update Legislative momentum is building on Capitol Hill as Senate Agriculture Committee leaders renew a push to pass a five year farm bill before year end. Lawmakers are working to reconcile the House passed Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 (H.R. 7567) with the Senate Agriculture Committee's Agricultural Act of 2026 (S. 5526). 

Core negotiations continue to focus on strengthening farm safety nets, modernizing dairy and crop insurance frameworks, and expanding rural energy programs. Meanwhile, major farm groups continue pressing Congress to pair farm bill passage with permanent, year round nationwide E15 sales to bolster domestic grain demand.

Ethanol Outlook The domestic ethanol processing sector maintains robust late autumn output, anchoring interior cash corn basis across the Midwest. According to the latest EIA weekly data, U.S. fuel ethanol production averaged 1.13 million barrels per day, running 5.1% above the same week last year, with Midwest plants producing 1.07 million barrels per day. 

Commercial ethanol inventories tightened slightly to 24.345 million barrels while exports held steady at 140,000 barrels per day. In its November Short Term Energy Outlook, the EIA maintained its full year 2026 and 2027 production forecasts, underscoring consistent baseline grind demand.

Fuel and Fertilizer On farm operating budgets received substantial fuel relief this week as crude and retail diesel prices dropped sharply. According to EIA data updated November 16, the Midwest regional average on highway diesel price fell 23.4 cents to $5.967 per gallon (down from $6.201 the prior week), dropping below the $6.00 mark for the first time since early September. 

On the futures board, January WTI Crude Oil (/CL) has pulled back to $83.89 per barrel while Natural Gas (/NG) trades at $3.267 per MMBtu. 

In feed and retail input markets, soybean oil (/ZL) sits at $61.12/cwt and soybean meal (/ZM) trades at $337.80/ton, while cooler autumn temperatures are encouraging active late fall anhydrous ammonia applications across cleared fields.

Diversification and Resilience Midwest operations are continuing to expand risk mitigation strategies through extended crop rotations, the integration of small grains, and the strategic use of perennials. These practices are being paired with localized bioenergy projects and targeted livestock integration to diversify revenue streams. 

The broader adoption of these systems is designed to improve long term soil health, optimize internal nutrient cycling, and provide financial buffers against intense market volatility and unpredictable weather patterns.

Ag Tech and Innovations The adoption of advanced biological inputs, targeted precision tools, autonomous field robotics, and real time sensor networks continues to accelerate across the Corn Belt. Producers are leveraging integrated data platforms to optimize input efficiency, reduce total fuel consumption, and scale back variable operational expenses. These automated solutions are increasingly viewed as essential tools for maintaining strict environmental compliance and protecting profit margins during challenging production seasons.

Livestock and Feed Cattle markets remain well supported while hog contracts continue to soften ahead of winter. Feeder Cattle (/GF) is trading near 335.500 cents per pound and Live Cattle (/LE) sits near 218.700 cents per pound, whereas Lean Hogs (/HE) eased to 52.975 cents per pound. 

Lower diesel prices and steady feed corn costs offer welcome margin relief for feedlot transport and winter ration budgeting, while pastures settle into seasonal dormancy.

Farmland Sales and Values The 2026 Corn Belt real estate market is displaying noticeable resilience with moderation, marking a clear transition from rapid capital appreciation to a stable, highly selective environment. 

This shift is driven by tight overall inventory, heightened buyer caution amid compressed crop returns, and localized demand focused strictly on premium acreage. While national farm real estate averages hover around $4,350 per acre, prime cropland throughout the Corn Belt routinely commands double that figure, averaging between $8,000 and $9,000+ per acre.

State level metrics highlight a distinct two tiered market where Class A ground holds firm while marginal acres experience minor softening:

Iowa: Overall values remain stable to slightly softer, with high quality tillable ground holding firm despite benchmark surveys noting minor aggregate declines of 1.5%. Public auctions average $11,900 per acre for disclosed sales, though highly productive soils with top CSR2 ratings frequently command premiums between $20,000 and $25,600 per acre in strong counties such as Lyon, Sioux, and Johnson.

Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio: Strong competition for premium tracts persists, pushing exceptional farms to auction results between $14,000 and $22,000+ per acre.

The broader eastern Corn Belt shows signs of stabilization, with lower quality or blemished parcels drawing fewer bidders due to rising input costs and geopolitical uncertainty.

Nebraska: Trends are mixed across the state, balancing localized benchmark gains with an overall statewide average decline of roughly 1% to $3,905 per acre. High quality irrigated tracts in counties like Butler remain highly sought after at $13,000+ per acre, while pasture prices are well supported by strong cattle market fundamentals.

Broader Midwest (MN, MO, SD): Performance remains highly variable. High quality row crop land easily commands auction premiums ranging from $8,000 to $19,000 per acre. 

Meanwhile, recreational parcels and properties near urban development zones exhibit higher price volatility, though a historically low supply of available farms prevents broad downward price pressure.

The combination of limited inventory, steady investor interest, and 1031 tax deferred exchanges keeps the market selective rather than weak. Tight margins and elevated interest rates will likely maintain this steady to soft trend for the remainder of 2026, though well marketed, highly productive tracts will continue to draw active bidding.

Other Notes 

Recent export inspections confirm steady grain shipments to primary international destinations, offering vital demand relief to local terminals. 

Concurrently, regional supply chains are adapting to shifting environmental standards as biofuel advocates push back against restrictive out of state greenhouse gas regulations and RFS exemption requests that impact Midwest ethanol markets.

Futures trading involves significant risk. Information provided is for educational purposes only.

Opportunity Arkansas Announces New Executive Vice President

Conway, AR — Opportunity Arkansas (OA) announced today that J. Robertson has been named the organization’s first-ever Executive Vice President. Robertson, who joined OA in mid-2024, most recently served as OA’s Policy Director and previously as Public Affairs Director.

In this new role, Robertson will oversee Opportunity Arkansas’s operations and work alongside OA’s Founder and CEO Nic Horton to carry out the organization’s long-term vision. He will also lead major initiatives that span the organization while continuing to play a central role in OA’s policy and communications work.

Horton offered the following statement on today’s announcement:

“Since the first day he stepped foot on the job, J. Robertson has exemplified the values that make our organization and our state great: hard work, initiative, care for others, and grit. He’s a creative problem solver, a fierce advocate for the next generation, and an all-star teammate. A recognized leader at the state capitol and within the conservative movement across Arkansas, J. has no doubt made both OA and our state better, and I know he’s just getting started.

This transition couldn’t come at a better time: with socialism on the rise and the Left energized, we’ve got more generational problems to solve and many gains to protect together. OA’s work is as important and as needed as it has ever been.

J. has the full confidence of myself and the rest of our Board of Directors. Let’s get to work!”

Robertson added:

“I’m humbled by the confidence that Nic has placed in me, and I’m honored to be a part of this incredible organization. 

This work is deeply personal to me. My wife and I chose to put down roots and build our family here in Arkansas because we love this state and we believe that Arkansas’s best days are ahead. I want Arkansas to become a real Land of Opportunity—a place where my children will put down roots someday—and we are going to keep fighting every single day to make that a reality. 

Opportunity Arkansas is leading the charge to shape the future of our state for the next generation, and I am honored to help lead this team as we protect the progress we’ve made and keep pushing forward to solve more generational problems.”

The move comes as OA prepares to enter its fifth year as one of the state’s leading conservative organizations.

Since its launch in late 2022, OA has worked alongside state policymakers to deliver 73 policy wins for the people of Arkansas including universal education freedom through the LEARNS Act, $1.5 billion of income tax cuts, the elimination of the state grocery tax, and cash welfare reform.

text:
Podcast Summary | Candace: WORLD IS ENDING?! Nationwide Outages, Mossad In DC & State Blocking Tyler Robinson Evidence Access?

Overview

A rapid succession of system failures—Microsoft, the FAA, Workday payroll, major banks, Apple, and United Airlines—is framed not as routine maintenance but as evidence that critical infrastructure is breaking faster than authorities will admit. The speaker argues that official reassurances follow a predictable script and that institutions have strong incentives to conceal cyberattacks and state involvement. That suspicion extends to Washington: an unscheduled visit by the MSAD director, a CIA meeting with Israel's Mossad chief, and a CNN report that Iran is planning a dirty bomb in DC are read as connected events pointing toward pressure for war. The through-line is a demand for skepticism toward official narratives, paired with a parallel focus on the Tyler Robinson case, where access to bullet fragment evidence becomes a test of whether a fair trial is actually possible.

Key Themes

- A cluster of outages across Microsoft, the FAA, payroll systems, banks, Apple, and United Airlines is treated as a pattern rather than coincidence, eroding confidence in official explanations.
- The speaker argues governments and corporations have strong incentives to deny cyberattacks, so hedging language like "no evidence" or "no indication" should be read as evasion rather than reassurance.
- AI is framed as an offensive accelerant, with reporting on open-source hacking tools and agentic threat activity cited as proof that attack timelines are compressing to machine speed.
- Bill Gates is presented as an example of elite indifference—someone suggesting society may need to "suffer a few of the negatives" of a major cyberattack before responding.
- The Iran war is described as the dominant election issue, with Republican losses framed as a referendum against being dragged into war on Israel's behalf.
- The CNN dirty bomb report is challenged on a "who benefits" basis, with the speaker arguing Iran has little incentive to provoke the US while Israel would gain from US action.
- The Tyler Robinson evidence dispute is framed as a test of judicial fairness, with the speaker arguing the state's effort to block defense observation of FBI testing could destroy potentially exculpatory material.
- The examiner's inconclusive finding—she could not determine whether the bullet matched the rifle—is treated as significant reasonable-doubt material that the defense has a right to protect.

Detailed Summary

The immediate trigger is a run of failures compressed into days, not months. Microsoft and Outlook went down around November 12. An FAA nationwide ground stop followed on a Friday. A Workday payroll and benefits outage hit Target, Walmart, Charles Schwab, and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. A banking outage linked to Chase impacted Wells Fargo and Bank of America the following Monday. Malicious subversion of popular websites stole crypto and targeted iPhone users across 178 organizations, including Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and IKEA. United Airlines then suffered its own widespread system outage.

The speaker notes the weekend had notably few reported outages compared with weekdays, a detail offered to suggest the failures track business activity rather than random chance. The rhetorical frame is simple: one is random, two is coincidence, three is a pattern, and ten means they're lying. Against that, authorities and companies keep offering reassuring explanations after each event, and the pattern itself is presented as the reason those explanations fail. The cumulative effect is described as ongoing stress and eroding public confidence, especially when pay, benefits, and bank access are affected. The speaker cites a statistic that 60 to 70 percent of Americans could not raise $1,000 cash within 48 hours, which makes payroll and banking failures far more than inconvenience.

A specific target is a CNN headline stating that a highly classified US national security communications network went down. The speaker identifies it as NSA Net, cites six sources, and focuses on the wording that there was "no evidence of a cyber attack." That phrasing is treated as evasive rather than exculpatory. The same logic is applied to United Airlines saying there was no indication its outage was cybersecurity-related—no indication does not prove absence. Jay Clayton, the Director of National Intelligence, said the government sees no indication of a coordinated or state-sponsored cyber attack and attributed the outages to institutions patching and upgrading systems, with some handoffs and restarts not going as expected. The speaker disputes that many systems would all patch and fail within the same few business days, and reads hedging phrases like "we don't see evidence" and "fairly confident" as proof of concealment.

The AI dimension is layered on top. A TechCrunch headline is cited reporting that the FBI says an open-source AI hacking tool breached networks in under three hours. A Google headline describing "agentic threat activity crossing a significant threshold" is cited for adversaries using generative AI to compress attack timelines, scale operations, and execute multi-stage intrusions at machine speed. The speaker frames the AI revolution as having created tools now being used offensively, and points to Apple outages affecting iCloud, Apple Pay, the App Store, Apple business services, on-device services, and AppleCare support around 2:30 p.m. Eastern as further evidence of breadth. Smaller items—an International Ice Hockey Federation cyber attack and an Ecuador energy provider in Norway detecting an attack with operations unaffected—round out the picture.

Bill Gates enters as the emblem of elite response. In a November 9 CBS interview, Gates is described as saying a big cyber attack causing problems could make people say the warnings were right, and that society may need to "suffer a few of the negatives" before responding fully. He also acknowledged that hacking retirement accounts could create uncertainty. The speaker interprets this as elite indifference to ordinary people's losses and argues Gates is treated as an unquestionable authority on cyber emergencies and pandemics, with influence granted by wealth and timing rather than merit. Historical deceptions are invoked to justify distrust: the JFK, RFK, MLK, and Malcolm X assassinations, 9/11, and weapons of mass destruction claims tied to Rumsfeld and Cheney-era assurances.

The political thread runs through the Iran war. The speaker says Republicans were "absolutely annihilated" in recent elections, with the war in Iran described as the overriding issue in exit polls. Republicans are said to have lost the House, governorships, and state houses, and Democrats are said to hold 56 Senate seats. JD Vance is said to have suggested the Iran war may not be a good idea. The Mossad director, Roman Gofman, visited Washington for talks with CIA director John Ratcliffe and was expected to travel to Miami to meet envoy Steve Witkoff, according to Axios. Axios also reported that Netanyahu is pressing Trump to resume the war against Iran. The speaker connects the timing of the outages to this unscheduled visit and to political fallout over the war, suggesting Israel, wanting the US to fight Iran, might retaliate by making life difficult for American officials—leaking information, threatening officials, or staging incidents blamed on Iran.

That sets up the dirty bomb claim. CNN reported that US intel indicates Iran is developing plans to potentially detonate a dirty bomb in Washington DC targeting senior Trump administration officials, citing seven US officials and noting debate over how mature the planning is and that it is not an indicator of imminent attack. The speaker applies a "who benefits" test: Iran has little incentive to provoke the US, while Israel would benefit from US action against Iran. The report is framed as likely a lie, possibly sourced from Israel to provoke a response, and CNN and intelligence officials are accused of repeatedly pushing false stories, with the "Iran two weeks away from a nuclear weapon" claim cited as the recurring example.

The Tyler Robinson case occupies the back half. Evidence includes at least a bullet jacket fragment and four lead bullet fragments, with preliminary hearing testimony suggesting possibly seven fragments total and three unaccounted for. The defense requested a pause on FBI testing over concerns the fragments could be damaged or destroyed, and sought only to observe the additional examination rather than stop testing outright. The state filed a motion in response, saying testing could damage or destroy the fragile material through peeling back the jacket with pliers or making etchings.

The state's affidavit invokes FBI laboratory policy barring defense personnel and experts from observing lab activities, citing security, classification, and case sensitivity. The FBI Quality Assurance Manual section 1.8G restricts lab access to FBI personnel, allowing authorized non-FBI personnel only when escorted, and prohibits access for the purpose of viewing lab activities. The manual references ISO 7025 and ANAB accreditation requirement AR3125, and the speaker examines the underlying standards directly. ISO section 6.3.4 requires measures to control facilities, including access, contamination prevention, and separation of incompatible activities—satisfied, the speaker says, by the QA manual. ISO section 7.7.1.7 requires labs to cooperate with customers and representatives, including reasonable access to relevant areas to witness customer-specific activities, which the speaker says permits the defense request. ANAB 6.3.4.1 requires a procedure addressing security and access, including access by visitors, which the speaker says also allows visitor access. The conclusion is that the FBI could grant a specific exception or dial back its policy and remain in compliance without losing certification, and the policy cited is a manual revision dated 15 days before the filing.

The examiner's history is framed as a credibility problem. Her prior report concluded she could not determine whether the bullet was fired from the particular rifle, described as significant reasonable-doubt material, and the current status of the bullet comparison is indeterminate absent further testing. In a prior certification test she said she could not tell whether it was a match while the correct answer was "not a match," mirroring her inconclusive conclusion here. The speaker argues destruction of the bullet would favor the prosecution, not the defense, because it could remove potentially exculpatory evidence if the true result would have been "not a match"—directly disputing the state's claim that loss of the bullet would only favor the defense. A judge will hold a hearing on the evidence dispute in mid-January, described as the first real test of the judge and the defense team, since the preliminary hearing was treated as a foregone conclusion.

The stated standard throughout is a fair trial, not a preferred verdict—a process everyone can trust regardless of outcome. Delay is framed as normal, with the case timeline compared to another case that took about four years to return to court, and expected trial timing discussed as June 2029. The speaker also advances a theory that Robinson "was not supposed to live" and that his survival "screwed up a lot of things for a lot of people," and argues technology should be evaluated for potential harmful uses before deployment, especially if misuse could cause catastrophic harm. Attacks on infrastructure, the speaker says, never benefit ordinary people. Closing remarks touch on a CIA headquarters electrical fire in Langley, Virginia, and a call to marginalize opponents of the show's line, before a scheduling note: back tomorrow and Thursday, off Friday through Sunday, then Monday and Tuesday next week, with Wednesday through Friday of Thanksgiving week off.

text:
Podcast Summary | This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von: #696 - Katt Williams

Overview
Katt Williams presents his memoir Nine Lives, No Wives, and 69 Concubines as the story of someone who did not have life figured out and was helped by God, and he says he could not write it until it had a great ending. The throughline is skepticism aimed at consistency: raised by devout Jehovah's Witnesses, he did not object to religion itself but to being taught things he did not believe and to living a double life, and he pressed questions about camels, the ark, and Jonah that he felt were treated as off-limits. Books and the library became his escape and his model of empowerment, a bicycle became freedom and practical mobility, and at 14 he made what he calls a dismissal or self eviction rather than a runaway exit. He ties his later choices to that foundation: door-to-door sales, an abrupt pivot to comedy, an unconventional approach to relationships, and a settled belief that his life has been guided and will be reviewed.

Key Themes
- Skepticism was driven by wanting claimed truth to match verifiable details, not by a rejection of religion itself, and the cost was feeling that honest questions were unwelcome.
- The library functioned as empowerment: entering a subject knowing nothing and leaving with answers became a repeatable method for confronting the world.
- Leaving home at 14 was framed as an organized choice announced at the dinner table, not an escape, and he says he acted because he feared the situation could break him.
- Emotional deprivation at home was measured against television families, and he says he only understood the distance from his parents more fully after leaving.
- Door-to-door work taught transferable persuasion: tailored pitches, belief in the product, and the conclusion that rejection is about being an uninvited stranger rather than about religion.
- Hardship in Coconut Grove produced a lasting rule against drugs, formed by hearing addicted adults describe how one decision ruined otherwise good lives.
- The carnival revealed how rigged games and prize economics work, and the lesson he drew was that he would never be broke in America.
- His path into pimping came through a door-to-door encounter and was presented to him as a management and security role, and the pivot from that life to comedy was abrupt.
- He frames his life as a story being written and later reviewed, with help arriving at each juncture, and he says faith guided his exit from bad paths.

Detailed Summary
The memoir is titled Nine Lives, No Wives, and 69 Concubines. He frames it as needing a great ending before it could be written, and as the story of someone who did not have life figured out and was helped by God. The book shows God appearing at every juncture, with help arriving whenever he needed it, and he credits that as evidence his success is not solely his own doing. He says he wanted to leave his story open-ended because he believes a larger story is being written.

His upbringing was devout Jehovah's Witness. He appreciated some teachings, including explanations of the pagan origins of holidays, but questioned others. His objection was not to religion itself but to being taught things he did not believe, and he did not want to live a double life. He describes not wanting to be told scripture was the word of God with no imperfections and then finding mistakes.

His skepticism centered on consistency between claimed truth and verifiable detail. He cites camels not being domesticated until long after the Abraham story, the scale of animals on Noah's ark at roughly 22,000, and whether a person could live inside a whale. He says he wanted truth and answers and felt some questions were treated as off-limits or sacrilegious. He distinguishes Jesus from Christianity, saying Christianity came after Jesus, and he wanted to know what religion Jesus followed.

The library was his escape. He describes the empowerment of entering knowing nothing about a subject and leaving with answers, pulling five or six books on one subject and spending all day before leaving the books on the table. A librarian remembered him for making librarians' work difficult.

A bicycle represented freedom and practical mobility, and he prioritized speed and efficiency over danger. He rode through ditches and mounds at a 40-acre seminary property years before BMX existed, used paper maps, and took highways as the fastest route.

He describes becoming comfortable riding a motorcycle on the interstate, saying the first ride is the toughest. He was motivated by cutting an hour-and-20-minute trip to 45 minutes so he could get back to religious activities. He says he did not care about the dangerous part, only the time saved.

He had to return from rides to put on a suit and participate in religious activities, including going door to door as a Jehovah's Witness, which he frames as an obligation to ensure everyone has at least heard about God rather than a requirement to convert or recruit anyone. He describes knocking on roughly 900 doors with about nine people happy to see them.

He later sold books and magazines and all-purpose cleaner door to door, and says it was easier to push products because he believed in each one. Magazine pitches were tailored by asking what people enjoyed, then offering titles like Sports Illustrated, Field & Stream, and Car and Driver. Cleaner was an easy sale by finding something filthy at the door and cleaning a visible circle. He worked with door-to-door Italian food salesman Donnie Ferrari for almost 30 days, and Donnie got into a physical beef with a Kirby or Electrolux vacuum salesman. He concludes that door-to-door rejection seems tied to being an uninvited stranger rather than to religion.

He says he did not run away from home but made an organized choice, telling his parents at the dinner table the night before. He framed leaving as asking how he would handle the situation if he was a man. He says he knew his parents did not like him even though they fulfilled parental duties of food, care, and education, and that he only understood this more after leaving. His relationship with his mother was emotionally distant, and he says he could not feel her and did not realize the effect until later.

He left at 14, describing it not as running away but as a dismissal or self eviction. He packed all his clothes into one suitcase and found there was still room, realizing he did not really have anything. He took his Rottweiler puppy and had roughly $1,200 saved from shoveling snow and cutting grass. At a truck stop he looked at license plates to pick a warm destination, avoiding snow, then told a truck driver a fabricated story about being separated from his family and offered money for a ride. He rode in the back of the 18-wheeler with the puppy, and the driver, who had dropped off tomatoes, was returning empty. He ended up in Miami in 98-degree heat with winter clothes from Ohio, near a warehouse district.

He frames his childhood as emotionally deprived and says he learned about parental affection from television, citing The Waltons and Little House on the Prairie, and sitcoms that made him wonder whether mothers are supposed to kiss their children. His mother could be affectionate mainly when he was physically sick. He reflects that he was sheltered and naive and expected life to work out like stories in books. He describes thinking of his life as a story, consciously treating hard moments as good chapters and as main character energy. He says his stated reason for leaving was that he feared the situation could break him and he did not want his story to show he knew what was happening and stayed anyway. He says Jesus had left at the same time, and he viewed Jesus as a brother who left and was perfect, which served as a map for leaving.

Living homeless in Coconut Grove around 1984 to 1985, he encountered about 50 or 60 drug addicts, most with stories of being doctors, lawyers, or family people whose lives were ruined by a substance. Hearing only negative, life-ruining stories as a kid made him determined never to try drugs, and nobody described any fun or parties. People around him were hardcore users of substances including heroin, opioids, and PCP, and he says he never saw a happy crackhead and viewed crack as too powerful after witnessing what it made people do. He also recounts resisting eating from the trash; a stranger walked up and gave him $100, which he had never received before, and he says he stopped asking God for money after that, reasoning God has plenty. He says he sold the puppy to a family who wanted to give it a good home, reasoning it would be better off than in a homeless encampment.

The carnival fascinated him as a world of misfits that came and left. Learning the games were rigged made it more exciting rather than less, with owners breaking down how each trick worked and confirming that whenever something seemed too good to be true, it was. The basketball rim is the wrong size and not round, so the ball must go dead center. Stuffed animals have no value outside the carnival but carry great status as prizes. Seeing the economics of an $1,800 truckload of stuffed animals generating about $380,000 convinced him he would never be broke in America.

His parents' marriage appeared perfect, with 50 to 60 years together and no arguments or separations he witnessed, which shaped his assumption that you find one woman and marry her. He grew up not knowing divorce existed until much later and delayed marriage fearing he would pick wrong before becoming successful. He rejects the framing that he fears commitment, saying he wanted what biblical figures had in many wives and concubines, that he has been a husband to a few, that he loves people for life, and that he would marry tomorrow if he met the right person. He approaches multiple relationships with upfront honesty, telling women early that someone else loves him dearly and he cannot imagine removing that person. He says a long marriage may have made him expect a perfection that is probably not out there, and a tension exists between wanting commitment and wanting to leave the option for the story to continue.

He had no direct exposure to pimping before encountering it through door-to-door sales. He knocked on a door where several prostitutes lived, and their pimp had just been killed on the corner in front of them. They explained the job as management and security, with him there for looks, keeping bad guys away, and ensuring business runs fluidly, which he found appealing. He says he stayed long enough for the women to get back on their feet and be successful again. He describes the exploitation system as broken, noting that the more broken a woman was, the better she tended to operate, due to callousness and disconnect, and that the women would do something else if they felt they were worth it. He says he learned a great deal from the women about what they disliked in men and still applies those lessons.

The pivot into comedy was abrupt. He won a standup contest that led to touring with comedians within days, moving from pimping on Friday to professional comedian on tour by Sunday. He says he initially was not trying to make an impact; he concluded he just had to be funny enough, tracked comedians' 15-minute sets, counted laughs, and set out to exceed those numbers. He took comedy seriously as an alternative to selling drugs, asking God for something he could do instead.

He describes learning grooming and hygiene habits from women's expectations, framing cleanliness as a social and relational practice. He mentions reading books that discussed the lifestyle before ever seeing it but could not imagine beating a woman and keeping her around. He describes going to strip clubs after becoming successful and telling dancers they were too good for this place, paying for dances but telling them to relax.

Discernment is described as pattern recognition across history and current events plus a willingness to seek answers without caring what the answer is. He says he became suspicious as a child about standard explanations of Egypt and the pyramids, doubting that copper tools could explain what he saw. A claim is made that about 34% of female murder victims are killed by an intimate partner, attributed to the Bureau of Justice Statistics.

He frames his life as guided by faith, repeatedly asking God for a way out of bad paths and believing he was consistently answered. He describes praying specifically to the one true God in each difficult situation because he had no friends or family to turn to. He studied what he believes was an Asian religion and Egyptian writings, both describing a life review after death, and he believes life is a story being written that will be reviewed or graded after death, citing recurring themes in religious writings he studied.

He says having children taught him about love and that helping ensure others' childhoods were better could help repair his own upbringing. He did not always plan to have children but is grateful for having been responsible for many and for what it taught him. He is now a grandfather and reflects that his grandfathers were the greatest possible men while regretting how little life they had left when he knew them. He describes wanting to be a young, successful grandfather able to actively engage with grandchildren, unlike the older grandfathers he knew.

Proceeds from Cat Williams and Nutcrackers go to autism charities at three locations nationwide, with the organizations selected from all over the country, and the faster the items are purchased the sooner they will stop selling them. He says he is not out of the water still regarding marriage. He narrates the audiobook of Nine Lives, No Wives, and 69 Concubines, and more examples of divine intervention appear later in the book.

I think "RB" is the right call, but not because you're short. This week is a bye problem: Bijan and Stevenson are both off. Once they're back, you have Bijan, Gordon, Stevenson and C-Rod. What you're missing is a reliable RB2 next to Bijan. That's worth upgrading, but you don't need to overpay to do it.

**Your current RB2 options aren't bad.** Gordon has been firmly in control of the backfield in Miami. He just had a 24-touch game, and the Fantasy Footballers expect him to remain in a high-volume role in a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills. The catch is that he depends on touchdowns. C-Rod is stuck in a three-way split in Jacksonville. Stevenson has been flex-level. Put together, that's a decent group, but nobody you'd lock in for a playoff week.

**Use Pitts as your trade chip.** Carrying two starting TEs is your one real surplus. Hockenson is questionable, but Kevin O'Connell said the Vikings expect Hockenson (wrist/chest) to make progress ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers. If he plays this week, Pitts becomes expendable. Packaging Pitts with C-Rod for a lead back is the cleanest move. Find a team that's weak at TE and has an extra starting RB, and that deal is easy to sell.

**Don't sell your WRs.** Your receivers are already thin with Nacua out, since both will be out for the next month, at least. Moving Olave or St. Brown for an RB just moves the hole to WR. Nacua coming back for the playoffs is your WR upgrade, so hold him.

text:
Actually, the US government subsidizes the US car manufacturing industry as well.
Through the Department of Energy's Advanced Technology Vehicles Manufacturing (ATVM) Loan Program, the federal government provides billions in direct, low-interest loans to automakers and parts suppliers to build or retool U.S. factories.
Under the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), Washington introduced substantial supply-chain subsidies.
The Department of Energy's Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains has distributed billions in direct grants to help legacy auto plants retool for hybrid and electric vehicles.
States and localities pledged over $13.8 billion for EV and battery factories alone.
States like Georgia, Michigan, Tennessee, Kansas, and North Carolina routinely offer multi-billion-dollar packages that include free land, state-funded road and utility upgrades, property tax abatements, and payroll tax rebates.
I would imagine that most countries around the world have subsidized selected industries at one time or another.
As far as profit motive, there are a number of private companies like BYD that operate on standard commercial profit models and whose shares are publicly traded. And there are a number like Dongfeng that are owned by central or municipal governments and operate under other motivations like job creation etc.

text:
"Nobody knew this, but the Yankees tried to hire me to play one more year in 1961. Shortly after my last game, my agent Fred Corcoran got a call from Dan Topping, the Yankee owner, and they met at the Savoy Plaza in New York.
According to my agent Fred, Mr. Topping said:
"Would Williams play one year with the Yankees, strictly pinch-hit for us for what he's making now -- $125,000?"
"I'm sure if I had wanted him to, Mr. Yawkey would have worked it out.
But I wasn't interested in playing for the Yankees.
What did New York have to offer?
A lot of bad air and traffic jams.
I told Fred to forget it, not to promote anything.
I wasn't interested.
I was never going to hit another ball in a big league park."
Ted Williams, who would of been MLB's first Designated Hitter!
The 1960 Yankees were loaded with lefty outfielders, thanks to Roger Maris who won the MVP with a 160 OPS+, the switch-hitting Mickey Mantle with 40 homers, 162 OPS+, and Yogi Berra, who at 35 was still a solid hitter with a 118 OPS+.
A month later, Ted Williams turned down several television jobs and unsuccessfully tried to purchase, "The L.L. Bean Company", and mostly enjoyed a life of hunting and fishing.

WWE Unreal Season 3 Is Coming: Cast, Release Date, Episodes, and What to Know

Go behind the scenes as John Cena says goodbye.

By Christopher Hudspeth

June 23, 2026

WWE Unreal is making its return with a fresh batch of behind-the-scenes action in Season 3.

After taking fans deeper than ever inside World Wrestling Entertainment’s creative process, the hit docuseries will once again pull back the curtain on some of the biggest moments, boldest decisions, and unforgettable storytelling with some of the WWE’s greatest legends who’ve shaped the industry and new stars who are emerging as prominent parts of the future.

What will be shown in WWE Unreal Season 3?

In WWE Unreal Season 3, John Cena says goodbye, a fan favorite returns, and the next generation of Superstars rise to the occasion.

The series takes viewers inside the writers room as injuries, last-minute pivots, and career-defining decisions reshape WWE’s biggest season yet heading into WrestleMania 42.

Who will be featured in WWE Unreal Season 3?

The cast of WWE Superstars featured in WWE Unreal Season 3 includes John Cena, Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, AJ Lee, Trick Williams, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer, Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Chelsea Green, Matt Cardona, Seth Rollins, and Becky Lynch.

When does WWE Unreal Season 3 come out?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will be released on July 21.

How many episodes are in WWE Unreal Season 3?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will have five 50-minute episodes.

Netflix News

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

Bridgerton Season 4 — The Regency-era drama returns later in the month (Part 1 premiering around Jan 29), with plenty of masquerade glamour and romance — the premiere events are already making waves!

Other notables include:

Kidnapped: Elizabeth Smart (true-crime docuseries)

New seasons of hits like Unlocked: A Jail Experiment, Love Is Blind: Germany, and WWE Unreal

Stand-up specials and reality shows keeping the variety flowing.

Plus, don't miss the Stranger Things 5 making-of documentary One Last Adventure, which premiered earlier this month for fans wanting a deep dive into the finale. Netflix is clearly doubling down on big stars, book adaptations, and high-energy originals to keep viewers hooked in 2026. (Grok)

Netflix: News

Netflix is a global streaming service providing a vast library of films, TV shows, documentaries, and mobile games. As of 2026, it has approximately 325 million paid members across more than 190 countries.

Pricing & Plans: Subscription plans typically range from $7.99 to $24.99 per month.

Content Offerings: Includes "Netflix Originals" (like Stranger Things and Squid Game), licensed content, and a growing selection of live programming and video podcasts.

Device Compatibility: Streamable on smart TVs, game consoles, smartphones, tablets, and via https://t.co/YlumK0CxOt.

Features: Supports offline downloads, personalized recommendations, and a dedicated "Netflix Kids" experience with parental controls.

Recent 2026 Developments

Warner Bros. Merger News: As of January 21, 2026, Netflix has moved toward an all-cash $27.75-per-share offer to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, aiming to outbid Paramount.

Market Reaction: Despite a Q4 earnings beat, Netflix shares saw a 7% decline in some markets (e.g., Frankfurt) on January 21, 2026, due to investor concerns regarding the financial weight of the Warner Bros. acquisition.

New Initiatives: The company is expanding into vertical video features for mobile and has recently launched video podcasts.

Live Events: Upcoming live events include the world-record climber Alex Honnold's "Skyscraper Live" ascent of Taipei 101 on January 23, 2026.

(In Case You Missed It)

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Seasons & Episodes

The series has released two seasons as of January 2026:

Season 1: Premiered July 29, 2025. It chronicled the lead-up to the debut of WWE Raw on Netflix and WrestleMania 41. Notable segments included a look at John Cena's high-profile storyline turns and the return of Charlotte Flair.

Season 2: Released January 20, 2026. This five-episode season focuses on the "Road to SummerSlam 2025" and features superstars like Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Rhea Ripley, and Cody Rhodes.

It delves into real-life drama such as R-Truth's contract negotiations and Naomi's previous walkout from the company.

Season 3: Confirmed to be in development, expected to focus on John Cena's retirement tour.

Key Personalities Featured

Executives: Paul "Triple H" Levesque (Narrator), Peyton Manning (Executive Producer).

Superstars: John Cena, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Rhea Ripley, Becky Lynch, Seth Rollins, and Bianca Belair.

Merchandise

Related promotional items and apparel are available, including:

Action Figures: Mattel has released sets like the "Hall of Champions" 4-pack featuring legendary superstars seen in the series.

text:
HOMAN v. BRANDY BARREL PUB GRILL INC (2020)Appeals Court of Massachusetts.
Patricia HOMAN v. BRANDY BARREL PUB & GRILL, INC., & others.1

19-P-1355
Decided: August 11, 2020
By the Court (Singh, Wendlandt & McDonough,2 JJ.3

"Plaintiffs often rely on direct evidence of drunken behavior such as loud or boisterous conduct to meet their burden. See, e.g., Cimino, 385 Mass. at 325 (testimony that patron became “loud, and vulgar,” and “obnoxious”); Gottlin v. Graves, 40 Mass. App. Ct. 155, 158 (1996) (testimony that patron appeared drunk and that his “whole manner changes when he drinks”); Hopping v. Whirlaway, Inc., 37 Mass. App. Ct. 121, 123 (1994) (testimony that patron “look[ed] like he had a few” and “seemed to ‘be feeling pretty good’ ”). The plaintiff here has no such evidence. Indeed, witnesses who were at the bar on the evening of the plaintiff's accident testified that she showed no signs of intoxication at any time before she fell. To survive summary judgment, the plaintiff thus needed to come forward with sufficient circumstantial evidence to allow a jury to infer that she must have displayed signs of intoxication prior to being served her last drink. See Douillard, 433 Mass. at 165.

Here, the only evidence that the plaintiff has to support an inference that she was visibly intoxicated at the time of last service is expert testimony opining that, in order to have had the BAC she did when admitted to MGH, she must have been served the equivalent of ten shots of vodka."

" The direct evidence was that the plaintiff did not appear visibly intoxicated. Moreover, the plaintiff failed to supply any additional circumstantial evidence of visible intoxication. The plaintiff did not, for example, have her expert calculate what her BAC would have been at the time she was served her last drink. Instead, he only calculated the plaintiff's BAC at the time of the accident -- some thirty minutes and two and one-half units of alcohol consumption later. The plaintiff also did not testify regarding the number of drinks required before she became intoxicated or obtain testimony from friends or acquaintances who had seen her intoxicated and could describe her appearance and behavior when intoxicated. Compare Douillard, 433 Mass. at 164-168 (reversing summary judgment in favor of defendant bar and finding triable issue as to visible intoxication based upon evidence that bar patron had elevated BAC after his arrest, testimony that patron usually became drunk after seven drinks, testimony describing how patron behaved when drunk, and expert testimony calculating what patron's BAC would have been at time of last service). In short, while the plaintiff has offered evidence that would allow a jury to infer that she appeared visibly intoxicated after she fell, her evidence does not support an inference that she appeared visibly intoxicated at the time she was served her last drink. The plaintiff therefore does not have evidence sufficient to demonstrate that the defendant was negligent, much less willful, wanton, or reckless. The Superior Court judge properly granted summary judgment."

Accordingly, we conclude that a jury could not find that the defendant engaged in willful, wanton, or reckless conduct based upon the record in this case
